 Example: Tranquility ("Spells cost [one] more to play during battle") makes a spell token cost [1].
304.11c A spell token is never in a hand. An effect that counts the cards in a hand does not count spell tokens. See rules 402, 304.10.
 Example: Dreadspawn Horror does not count spell tokens as cards in hand.
304.11d A spell token that has been cast is still a token while it is on the stack. See rule 406.
 Example: Download can take a Fireball that has already been cast and is on the stack.
304.11e A token has a mana cost, which is often 0. Effects that change the cost of playing spells apply when a spell token is cast. See rules 111, 702.
 Example: Tranquility makes a spell token cost [1] in battle.
304.11f Many tokens have an X value, set by the effect that created them: "Create a Crystal 3" creates a Crystal whose X is 3. A token's X is its size, not a cost. See rule 107.
304.11g A spell token with Burst is cast together with every other spell token of the same name that its controller has in that region. They are still separate spells. See rules 803, 702.
title: CR 304.11–304.11g

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 304. Tokens
(continues 304.11: A spell token is a spell that is in play. Its controller may cast it from play; casting it works the same way as casting a spell from the hand.)
304.11h A spell token is not a unit and has no stats. An ability that refers to a unit token does not apply to a spell token. See rule 300.5b.
 Example: The World Shepherd watches for unit tokens being created; a spell token being created does not trigger it.
title: CR 304.11h

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 304. Tokens
304.12 A spell token cannot move to another region on its own. Its controller may bring it into the enemy region with an attack, but only together with at least one attacking unit, and the move cannot be undone. See rule 604.
 Example: A Fireball rides into the enemy region with an attacking The Foretold and stays there after the Foretold dies; with no attacking unit it stays home.
title: CR 304.12

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 304. Tokens
(continues 304.12: A spell token cannot move to another region on its own. Its controller may bring it into the enemy region with an attack, but only together with at least one attacking unit, and the move cannot be undone.)
304.12a A counterattack may bring spell tokens the same way: spell tokens that stand in the region the counterattacking units leave from may go with them. See rule 610.
title: CR 304.12a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 304. Tokens
(continues 304.12: A spell token cannot move to another region on its own. Its controller may bring it into the enemy region with an attack, but only together with at least one attacking unit, and the move cannot be undone.)
304.12b A spell token created in an enemy region during combat can be cast there at once. See rule 304.11a.
 Example: A Fireball created for the attacker in the enemy region during combat is castable there at once.
title: CR 304.12b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 304. Tokens
304.13 During regroup, every spell token still in play is erased, including unused spell tokens in their controller's own region. See rules 506, 304.9a.
 Example: With Harbinger of Immolation in play, its controller's spell tokens stay through regroup.
title: CR 304.13

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 304. Tokens
304.14 When an effect refers to each unique token (Automaton of Abundance), two tokens are the same unique token only if they have the same name, the same X and the same stats set by the effect that created them. A token created with no stats set has its own printed stats.
 Example: With Automaton of Abundance in play, Manufacture creates a Robot 3, a Robot 2 and a Robot 1: three unique tokens, so one extra of each is made.
 Example: Three Robot 2s are one unique token.
 Example: A 3/3 and a 5/5 unit token made together are two unique tokens, so Automaton of Abundance makes a 3/3 and a 5/5 more.
 Example: A unit token created with no stats set and one created as a 1/1 are one unique token.
304.14a An additional copy of a token (Automaton of Abundance) is created with what the effect that created the original gave it: its name, its X, and any stats that effect set ("a 3/3", "an X/X").
 Example: With Automaton of Abundance in play, creating a 3/3 unit makes two 3/3s.
 Example: With Automaton of Abundance in play, Spawntender ("Create an 8/8 unit.") makes two 8/8s.
title: CR 304.14–304.14a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 304. Tokens
304.15 Creating a token is not playing it. A unit token that an effect created was not played. See rules 701, 304.11b.
 Example: Manufacture creates Robot tokens. That is not playing them, so Bloomcaster and Stalwart Sentinel do not trigger.
title: CR 304.15

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 305. Modifications
305.1 A modification (mod) is a card that is applied to another card instead of being played. A modified card is treated as a single card with all of the text its mods add, except that a spell or a spell token that is modified gains only the mod's attributes (721). The two kinds of modification are augment and graft. See rules 720, 721, 722, 723, 724.
 Example: Curio Drifter augmented onto a Good Whale is not played and gives the Whale Evasive; Biotoxicity is grafted; a Fireball augmented with Bloomcaster does not create 1/1s.
title: CR 305.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 305. Modifications
305.2 Applying a mod is not playing a card, so an ability that triggers on playing a unit or a spell does not trigger on it. See rules 701, 720.
 Example: A Virus applied from hand during battle is not a card being played, so Void Mandible ("When a nontoken card is played during battle…") does not trigger.
title: CR 305.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 305. Modifications
305.3 Modifying is done during the deployment phase. A Virus can also be applied from the hand during battle. See rules 507, 723.
title: CR 305.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 305. Modifications
305.4 A card's augment and graft text works when the card is played normally, not only when it is applied as a mod. See rules 721, 722.
title: CR 305.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 305. Modifications
305.5 A spell or spell unit with a graft symbol resolves normally when it is played, and can later be applied as a graft from the bin. See rule 722.
 Example: Spawntender, a spell unit with a graft icon, resolves normally when played: it creates its 8/8 and its own body spawns.
 Example: A dead Leaping Lillik in the bin can be applied as a graft.
title: CR 305.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 3. Card Types › 305. Modifications
305.6 During deployment, a spell token in play may be augmented, with any augment and not only a Virus. During a battle, a Virus may also be applied to a spell token in play in the battle's region, either player's (723.2). The spell token gains only the mod's attributes, not its text. See rule 721.
 Example: A Fireball augmented with a mod granting {Powerful} deals double damage when cast.
 Example: Carapace Devourer, an augment that is not a Virus, may augment a spell token during deployment.
 Example: In battle a player applies Chitin Shredder, a Virus, to a Fireball token standing in play. The Fireball gains Powerful and deals double damage when it is cast.
title: CR 305.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 400. General
400.1 The zones of the game are the deck, the hand, the cache, play, the bin, the stack, the erased pile, the recycle pile and the pack. See rules 401, 402, 403, 404, 405, 406, 407, 408, 409.
title: CR 400.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 400. General
400.2 Play and the stack are the active zones. The hand, the deck, the bin, the cache and the erased pile are inactive zones. See rules 404, 406, 803.
 Example: A printed Unstable card is erased leaving play or the stack, and only binned leaving the hand, the deck or the cache.
400.2a Whether a zone is active matters to {Unstable}: an {Unstable} card is erased in place of entering a bin only when it leaves an active zone. A card leaving an inactive zone for a bin is binned normally, {Unstable} or not. See rules 405, 803.
 Example: Aberrant Statweaver (printed {Unstable}) discarded from a hand goes to the bin and stays there: the hand is inactive.
 Example: The same card negated off the stack is erased: the stack is active.
title: CR 400.2–400.2a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 400. General
400.3 Each player has their own hand, cache, bin and erased pile. See rules 402, 403, 405, 407.
title: CR 400.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 400. General
400.4 A card that leaves play for a bin, a hand, a cache or an erased pile goes to that zone of the player who controlled it when it left play, not to its owner's. See rules 102, 711.
 Example: A unit stolen with a control-changing effect is recalled. It goes to the hand of the player who stole it.
 Example: A stolen unit dies. It goes to its controller's bin, and its controller trashes it.
 Example: A stolen unit is erased from play. It and its mods go to the erased pile of the player who stole it.
400.4a A card's owner never changes. Changing zones, changing controller and being put into play out of another player's zone all leave the card owned by the same player.
 Example: Wake the Dead puts a unit from the opponent's bin into play under the caster's control; the opponent still owns it.
 Example: A stolen unit that is recalled is still owned by the player it was stolen from.
title: CR 400.4–400.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 400. General
(continues 400.4: A card that leaves play for a bin, a hand, a cache or an erased pile goes to that zone of the player who controlled it when it left play, not to its owner's.)
400.4b If the effect that moves a card names where it goes, the card goes there instead.
 Example: Pull Under: "Delete target unit. If you do, put it and all of its mods into your bin." The deleted unit and its mods go to the bin of Pull Under's caster, whoever controlled the unit.
title: CR 400.4b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 400. General
(continues 400.4: A card that leaves play for a bin, a hand, a cache or an erased pile goes to that zone of the player who controlled it when it left play, not to its owner's.)
400.4c In constructed, a card's owner is the player who brought it to the game. See rule 901.
title: CR 400.4c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 400. General
400.5 An ability that works while its card is in a bin or a cache ("if I am in your bin") works only while the card is in that zone. It never works while the card is in play. See rule 706.
 Example: Cinder Scuttler ("When you deal combat damage to an opponent, if I am in your bin, recall me.") dies in the same combat damage sub-step in which another attacker hits the opponent. It was not in the bin when the damage was dealt, so it is not recalled.
400.5a Copies of one card in the same bin or cache share one such ability: it triggers once for that zone, not once per copy.
 Example: Two Cinder Scuttlers in a bin: one combat hit on the opponent recalls one of them, not both.
title: CR 400.5–400.5a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 400. General
(continues 400.5: An ability that works while its card is in a bin or a cache ("if I am in your bin") works only while the card is in that zone. It never works while the card is in play.)
400.5b "Your bin" in such an ability means the bin the card is in: the player whose bin it is controls the ability, whoever once played the card.
 Example: Rotling ("When I leave your bin, … You may pay [1] to draw a card") leaves the opponent's bin. The opponent, whose bin it left, is the one offered the draw.
title: CR 400.5b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 401. Deck
401.1 The deck is the face-down pile that cards are drawn from and that packs are dealt from. See rule 503.
title: CR 401.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 401. Deck
401.2 The cards in the deck are hidden: no player may look at them or at their order. A card put on the bottom of the deck is not revealed unless the effect says so. See rule 408.
title: CR 401.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 401. Deck
401.3 In live draft, all players draw from one shared deck. See rule 902.
401.3a In constructed, there is no shared deck: each player has their own deck. See rule 901.
title: CR 401.3–401.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 401. Deck
(continues 401.3: In live draft, all players draw from one shared deck.)
401.3b "The deck" in card text means the deck of the effect's controller: the shared deck in live draft, that player's own deck in constructed.
 Example: In constructed a Glimpse 1 reveals the top of the deck of the effect controller, not of the opponent.
title: CR 401.3b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 401. Deck
401.4 A player who must draw from an empty deck when the recycle pile is also empty draws as many cards as there are, and has then run out of cards (104.5). See rules 408, 104.
 Example: With deck and recycle pile both empty, a draw of two draws nothing, and the game ends (104.5).
title: CR 401.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 402. Hand
402.1 Each player has a hand. Drawn cards go to the hand, and cards in the hand are played from there. See rules 503, 702.
title: CR 402.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 402. Hand
402.2 A hand is hidden from the other players.
402.2a An effect that lets a player "look at" a hand shows it to that player only. An effect that makes a player "reveal" their hand shows it to every player.
 Example: Thought Extraction aimed at its caster's own hand shows that hand to nobody else.
title: CR 402.2–402.2a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 402. Hand
402.3 A spell token is never in a hand. An effect that counts or refers to the cards in a hand does not count a spell token. See rule 304.
 Example: Dreadspawn Horror does not count spell tokens as cards in hand.
 Example: Astral Tidewraith's damage, equal to the number of cards in each player's hand, does not count spell tokens either.
title: CR 402.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 402. Hand
402.4 A card enters a hand whenever an effect puts it there: a draw, a recall, or a move out of a bin, the stack, a cache or another hand. Several cards that enter one hand in a single move enter it together, as one event ("one or more cards enter a hand"). See rule 706.
 Example: Collect Remains puts a card from a bin into its caster's hand during battle; Rider of the Tides sees a card enter a hand, though it was neither drawn nor recalled.
 Example: Two cards that move from a bin to a hand in one move enter it together: an ability watching for cards entering a hand triggers once, not twice.
title: CR 402.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 402. Hand
402.5 Discarding a card moves it from its hand to the bin. Discarding is not playing the card: nothing goes on the stack. See rules 405, 701, 801.
title: CR 402.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 402. Hand
402.6 Card text that restricts playing a card "from your hand" restricts only the hand. The card may still be played from any other zone an effect allows.
 Example: Calming Force ("I can't be played from your hand.") cannot be cast from the hand, but a copy in the cache under a live permission can be played.
title: CR 402.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
403.1 The cache is a zone of its own, beside the hand, the bin and the deck. Effects put cards into it ("cache"), out of the hand, the bin, the deck or play. See rules 801, 803.
title: CR 403.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
403.2 The cache is public. Every player can see every cached card, and any prophecy attached to it.
title: CR 403.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
403.3 Being in the cache does not by itself let a player do anything with a card.
403.3a A cached card can be used only while a permission on it is live: a prophecy on it that has been fulfilled, or a glimpse that cached it this turn. See rules 801, 803.
title: CR 403.3–403.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
(continues 403.3: Being in the cache does not by itself let a player do anything with a card.)
403.3b While a permission is live, the cached card can be used in every way the same card could be used from the hand: in every play mode, in every window, and as a mod.
 Example: A glimpsed Virus in the cache is augmented onto an enemy unit during battle.
title: CR 403.3b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
(continues 403.3: Being in the cache does not by itself let a player do anything with a card.)
403.3c A card used under a fulfilled prophecy costs nothing and ignores affinity. A card used under a glimpse costs its mana but ignores affinity. This holds for every way of using it, mods included.
403.3d A cached card keeps its printed timing. A permission says that the card may be used, not when.
title: CR 403.3c–403.3d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
403.4 The cache is not the hand. A cached card cannot be discarded, and card text that names the hand does not reach the cache. See rule 402.6.
title: CR 403.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
403.5 When a glimpse permission ends, the card stays in the cache, with no permission.
title: CR 403.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
403.6 A cached card can be targeted. A player's cache can be targeted only by an effect that resolves in a region where that player is present. See rules 110, 601.
 Example: In deployment, Prismatic Observer can recall only a card from its own player's cache.
 Example: In battle, with both players present, it can reach the opponent's cache.
title: CR 403.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
403.7 When a unit in play is cached, only the card goes to the cache. Its mods go to the bin. See rules 410, 720.
title: CR 403.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 403. Cache
403.8 A card in the cache under a live glimpse permission may be prophesied where it stands. It does not move and is not cached a second time, and the glimpse permission is used up. See rule 803.
title: CR 403.8

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 404. Play
404.1 Play is the zone of the units, resources and tokens on the table. A unit stays in play until something removes it. See rules 601, 602.
404.1a A token is created directly into play, in the region where it was created. See rule 304.
 Example: Galactic Germination cast by the attacker creates its unit tokens straight into play in the battle region.
404.1b A spell unit enters play as it resolves, in place of going to the bin. See rule 303.
 Example: Jelly resolves into play as a unit and does not go to the bin.
title: CR 404.1–404.1b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 405. Bin
405.1 The bin is a player's discard pile. See rule 400.3.
title: CR 405.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 405. Bin
405.2 A card goes to the bin when: a unit dies or is deleted; a unit is sacrificed; a spell resolves; a card is discarded; or a card that was being played is negated or fails to resolve, unless a rule sends it elsewhere. See rules 704, 801.
405.2a A spell unit that is prevented from resolving (for example because its targets became invalid) does not spawn. It goes to the bin.
 Example: A negated Jelly, a spell unit played through Hooba-Pon, does not enter play.
405.2b An ambushing unit whose ambush fails to resolve goes to the bin. See rule 803.
title: CR 405.2–405.2b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 405. Bin
405.3 A unit that dies goes to the bin of the player who controlled it when it died, unless the effect that kills it names another bin or the unit is {Unstable} (see rule 405.5). If it is a card, the player whose bin it enters trashes it; a token is never trashed. See rules 400.4, 801, 405.5, 405.4.
 Example: Pull Under deletes an enemy unit and puts it into its caster's bin; the caster trashes it.
 Example: A token that Pull Under deletes enters the caster's bin but is not trashed.
title: CR 405.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 405. Bin
405.4 A card that enters a bin from any zone except the stack is trashed. A card that comes from the stack is not, and a token is never trashed. A nontoken mod erased together with its {Unstable} host is not trashed either. See 801. See rule 801.
405.4a A spell played for free while another effect resolves (for example by Tides of the Cosmos) and then put into the bin counts as coming from the stack, so it is not trashed.
 Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays an ordinary spell for free; it goes to the bin and is not trashed.
title: CR 405.4–405.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 405. Bin
405.5 An {Unstable} card that would enter a bin from an active zone is erased instead: it ends on the erased pile, not in the bin. One that dies in play is still trashed (rule 801.2h). See 803. See rules 803, 713, 400.2a.
 Example: A unit carrying a mod is {Unstable}. When it dies, it ends on the erased pile and is not left in the bin.
title: CR 405.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 405. Bin
405.6 A card in a bin is identified only by its name and by which copy of that name it is. An effect that has named one copy keeps naming that copy as other copies of its name leave the bin (405.6b).
 Example: Two copies of a card are in a bin and a spell targets the second. The first copy is taken in response: the target is still the card the spell aimed at, now the only copy.
405.6a "Another" said by a card in a bin excludes that one copy, not every card with its name. See rule 110.
 Example: Blightwalker is trashed while another Blightwalker is already in the bin; the older copy is "another" and can be chosen.
405.6b An effect that refers back to a card that just entered a bin ("that card", "it") means that copy. If that copy has left the bin, the effect finds nothing. It never takes a different copy of the same name. A card a spell or ability targets in a bin is held the same way: the target stays on the copy it named while other copies of that name leave, and if that copy itself leaves before the effect resolves, the target is gone.
 Example: An {Unstable} unit dies and is erased instead of staying in the bin. Biomass Devourer's "erase it" then finds nothing, and does not erase an older copy of the same card already in that bin.
 Example: Two copies of a card are in a bin. A spell targets the second, and the second is taken in response. The spell finds nothing; it does not take the first copy instead.
 Example: A spell targets the first of two copies, and the first is taken in response. The spell does not slide onto the second copy.
title: CR 405.6–405.6b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 405. Bin
405.7 A card leaves a bin whenever an effect takes it out, for any reason: recalled, played, cached, erased, recycled, prophesied, or applied as a mod. A "when I leave your bin" ability triggers on every such departure.
 Example: Writhing Host leaves the bin when it is erased to pay for a haste play.
title: CR 405.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 405. Bin
405.8 An augment or graft may be applied from the bin as well as from the hand, during deployment, if its cost is paid and its affinity met. See rules 720, 721, 722.
405.8a A {Virus} card in a bin can be applied only as an ordinary mod during deployment. It cannot be used as a mod during battle. See rule 723.
 Example: Bumblecrab, a {Virus}, sits in a player's bin. In deployment it can augment out of the bin; in battle it is offered only from the hand.
title: CR 405.8–405.8a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 405. Bin
405.9 A card can be played from a bin only when an effect or the card's own text allows it. The card keeps its printed timing unless the permission says it may be played "now". See rule 702.
 Example: Abyssal Evocation lets its caster play spells from the bin in this battle; only {Battle} spells there can be played.
405.9a A card played from a bin is {Unstable} only if the permission says so. A card played from a bin under its own text does not become {Unstable}. See rule 803.
 Example: A spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation gains {Unstable}, so it is erased rather than going back to the bin.
title: CR 405.9–405.9a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 406. The Stack
406.1 The stack is the zone where cards being played, and abilities, wait to resolve. The last thing put on the stack resolves first. See 703. See rules 703, 704.
title: CR 406.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 406. The Stack
406.2 A spell unit on the stack is not yet in play. It enters play only when it resolves. See rule 303.
 Example: Mycelial Mentor, played with Bloomcaster out, is still on the stack while Bloomcaster's 1/1 is made, so the Mentor never sees the 1/1.
title: CR 406.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 406. The Stack
406.3 A spell token that has been cast is on the stack, and is still a token there. See rule 304.
 Example: Download can take a Fireball token already cast and on the stack.
title: CR 406.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 406. The Stack
406.4 When a card on the stack resolves, is negated or fails to resolve, it goes to the bin unless it enters play or something sends it elsewhere: an {Unstable} card is erased (see rule 405.5), a card whose own text erases it goes to the erased pile (see rule 406.4a), and a recall puts it into a hand. A card that goes to the bin this way is not trashed, because it comes from the stack. See rules 704, 405.4, 405.5, 406.4a.
 Example: A non-{Unstable} virus negated off the stack goes to the bin.
406.4a A spell whose text says "Erase me" goes to the erased pile when it resolves, instead of the bin. See rule 407.
 Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays Suspend for free; Suspend goes to the erased pile, never the bin.
title: CR 406.4–406.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 406. The Stack
(continues 406.4: When a card on the stack resolves, is negated or fails to resolve, it goes to the bin unless it enters play or something sends it elsewhere: an {Unstable} card is erased (see rule 405.5), a card whose own text erases it…)
406.4b A self-erasing spell that is negated or fails to resolve goes to the bin. Its "Erase me" never happened.
title: CR 406.4b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 407. Erased Pile
407.1 Erasing a card takes it out of the game. An erased card goes to the erased pile. See rule 801.
 Example: Celestial Purge takes a unit out of the game onto the erased pile: no bin and no death.
title: CR 407.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 407. Erased Pile
(continues 407.1: Erasing a card takes it out of the game. An erased card goes to the erased pile.)
407.1a The erased pile is public.
407.1b Nothing takes a card back out of the erased pile.
407.1c Erasing is not dying and not trashing: an erased card never enters a bin. See rule 410.2.
 Example: A unit erased by Banishment does not die and is not trashed.
title: CR 407.1a–407.1c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 407. Erased Pile
407.2 A card that an effect erases goes to the erased pile, including a mod erased off a host that stays in play (for example to pay a cost). See rule 720.
407.2a A mod taken off its host and put into play as a card of its own (Reclaim the Fallen) does not leave the game and does not go to the erased pile.
 Example: A Pile of Runes is augmented onto a unit. Reclaim the Fallen targets that unit: A Pile of Runes comes off it and stands in play as a unit of its own. It never goes to the erased pile.
title: CR 407.2–407.2a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 407. Erased Pile
407.3 A token is never recorded on the erased pile, because a token is not a card and the erased pile is a list of cards. This holds for unit tokens and spell tokens alike: a token that ceases to exist after entering a bin, a hand or a cache, and a token erased from play or from the stack, are not recorded. See rule 410.5.
 Example: A unit token sent to the cache ceases to exist there and is not recorded on the erased pile.
 Example: A token unit carrying a real mod is erased from play. The mod is recorded on the erased pile; the token is not.
 Example: A spell token recalled off the stack is not recorded on the erased pile.
 Example: A token that dies enters the bin, is not trashed, and then ceases to exist, without being recorded.
407.3a A token mod is never recorded on the erased pile either, however its host leaves play, and also when it is erased off a host that stays in play (rule 720.9a).
 Example: A unit carrying a token mod leaves play in each of the three ways. The token mod is announced as erased each time, and never recorded on the erased pile.
 Example: A token mod reaches neither the erased pile nor a bin, on all three routes.
 Example: A Wraith token mod erased together with its host reaches neither the erased pile nor a bin.
title: CR 407.3–407.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 407. Erased Pile
407.4 A transformed card is recorded on the erased pile as its front face. See rule 410.3.
 Example: A transformed Scholar of the Void erased by Banishment is recorded as Scholar of the Void.
title: CR 407.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 408. Recycling
408.1 To recycle a card is to put it on the bottom of the deck. A recycled card has not left the game. See rule 801.
 Example: A card recycled for a resource is drawn again once the rest of the deck is gone, so it never left the game.
title: CR 408.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 408. Recycling
408.2 A deck has a mark where it originally ended. The recycle pile lies under the deck, past the mark, and is still part of the deck. A card put on the bottom of the deck goes past the mark, into the recycle pile, not onto the bottom of the cards still to be drawn.
408.2a Every card put on the bottom of the deck goes past the mark, whatever put it there: recycling for a resource, the constructed put-back, the cards a glimpse did not cache, and recycled packs alike. Likewise, anything that uses the deck can reach the mark: drawing, milling, caching or revealing the top cards, a glimpse, and dealing a pack alike.
408.2b When anything that uses the deck needs a card past the mark, whatever the reason, the recycle pile is shuffled and put above the mark, under the cards still left in the deck; the mark goes back to the very bottom, with an empty recycle pile behind it. Taking the last card above the mark does not by itself reshuffle the pile: it is shuffled only when a card past the mark is needed. An effect that reveals more cards than are above the mark reshuffles when it reaches the mark and keeps revealing until it has its full number. See rule 401.4.
408.2c Every player can see how many cards are in the recycle pile. No player may look at them.
408.2d The order in which cards were recycled does not matter to the game.
408.2e Each deck has its own recycle pile. In live draft, all players share one pile; in constructed, each player has their own. See rule 401.3.
title: CR 408.2–408.2e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 408. Recycling
408.3 A card recycled out of a hand is not revealed unless the effect says so.
 Example: Bripp recycles a card from a hand without naming it to the table.
title: CR 408.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 408. Recycling
408.4 During the resource step, a player may recycle a card from their hand to create a resource. See 502. See rules 502, 106.
title: CR 408.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 409. The Pack
409.1 In live draft, each player has a pack: a face-down pile of 10 cards dealt from the deck at the start of the game, which that player drafts from. See rules 503, 902.
409.1a Constructed has no packs. See rule 901.
title: CR 409.1–409.1a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 409. The Pack
409.2 A pack may be looked at and used only during the draft step, and no player may look at another player's pack.
title: CR 409.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 409. The Pack
409.3 In the draft step, a player combines the non-token, non-resource cards in their hand with their pack, keeps any of them, and passes the pack on with exactly 10 cards in it. See 503. See rule 503.
title: CR 409.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 409. The Pack
409.4 After each cycle of N+1 turns, where N is the number of players, every pack is recycled and each player is dealt a new pack of 10 cards.
409.4a In team draft, packs are never refreshed. See rule 904.
title: CR 409.4–409.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 409. The Pack
409.5 When a player is eliminated, their pack is recycled. See rule 104.
title: CR 409.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
410.1 A card that leaves play and comes back is a new object. It does not remember its earlier time in play.
 Example: Engorged Caudex is recalled and played again; its once-per-turn grafted draw works again the same turn.
410.1a An effect aimed at a card that has since changed zones does not affect it. An effect aimed at a card that is still in the same zone affects it only if the card is still a legal target for the slot it was chosen for; otherwise that target is lost as well. If every target is lost, the effect fails to resolve. See rules 704, 110.
 Example: An opponent's Luminous Arc is aimed at one of your units; you answer with Organic Exchange on two of your own units. They are still in play, so the Luminous Arc still resolves.
 Example: An opponent ambushes with Orblish Horroth to recall target ally; you take control of that unit in response. It is no longer their ally, so nothing is recalled.
 Example: Minor Kraken's target grows past 5 defense before it resolves, and is not recalled.
410.1b Moving a mod from one unit to another is not a zone change: the mod never leaves play, and nothing despawns. See rule 720.
 Example: Reconfigure moves Bubb and its Growing Plague onto a Robot; Growing Plague's "when I despawn" does not trigger.
title: CR 410.1–410.1b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
410.2 A unit despawns whenever it leaves play, by any route: dying, being recalled, being cached, being exchanged or being erased. A "when I despawn" ability triggers whichever way the unit leaves. See rule 706.
 Example: A Pile of Runes ("[Augment] When I despawn, create a Crystal X") is augmented onto Rune Channeler. Rune Channeler is recalled to its owner's hand: that despawn ability triggers, and a Crystal is created.
 Example: Demon of the Depths ("Whenever one of your units despawns…") triggers when one of your units is erased.
410.2a A unit exchanged out of play (Hooba-Mon, Necromorph) despawns and goes to the bin, where it is trashed, but it does not die.
 Example: Necromorph's exchange triggers no death ability, but the unit despawns and is trashed.
title: CR 410.2–410.2a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
410.3 A transformed card exists as its front face in every zone except play. It turns back over as it leaves play, before anything sees it leave.
 Example: A transformed Scholar of the Void that dies goes to the bin as Scholar of the Void.
 Example: It can then be returned from the bin as a Scholar.
title: CR 410.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
(continues 410.3: A transformed card exists as its front face in every zone except play. It turns back over as it leaves play, before anything sees it leave.)
410.3a A unit that is copying another card (Borrower of Forms) leaves play as itself. If it dies it goes to the bin as Borrower of Forms; if it is recalled it goes to the hand as Borrower of Forms. See rule 710.
 Example: A Borrower that became something else still goes to the bin as Borrower of Forms.
 Example: Recalled, it goes back to the hand as Borrower of Forms.
title: CR 410.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
410.4 When a modded unit is recalled or cached, its mods go to the bin and the unit goes on alone. A token mod ceases to exist instead (see rule 410.4c). See rules 720, 403.7, 410.4d, 410.4c.
title: CR 410.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
(continues 410.4: When a modded unit is recalled or cached, its mods go to the bin and the unit goes on alone. A token mod ceases to exist instead (see rule 410.4c).)
410.4a A mod that goes to a bin when its host leaves play goes to the bin of the host's controller. See rule 400.4.
 Example: A virus on an opponent's unit goes to that opponent's bin when the unit leaves play.
title: CR 410.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
(continues 410.4: When a modded unit is recalled or cached, its mods go to the bin and the unit goes on alone. A token mod ceases to exist instead (see rule 410.4c).)
410.4b A modded card is {Unstable}. When it dies or is erased, it and all of its mods are erased. See rules 803, 405.5.
title: CR 410.4b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
(continues 410.4: When a modded unit is recalled or cached, its mods go to the bin and the unit goes on alone. A token mod ceases to exist instead (see rule 410.4c).)
410.4c A token mod has no card of its own. It never enters a bin; when its host leaves play it ceases to exist.
title: CR 410.4c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
(continues 410.4: When a modded unit is recalled or cached, its mods go to the bin and the unit goes on alone. A token mod ceases to exist instead (see rule 410.4c).)
410.4d An exchange is not a death. But a modded unit is {Unstable}, so when it is exchanged out of play, it and all of its mods are erased, just as they would be if it died. See rules 410.4b, 405.5, 801.
 Example: Hooba-Mon exchanges itself while it carries a mod; it is erased, not left in a bin.
 Example: An unmodded Hooba-Mon exchanged the same way stays in the bin.
title: CR 410.4d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
410.5 A token that leaves play goes to the zone it was sent to (a hand, a bin, a cache) and really is there. It ceases to exist there the next time state-based actions are checked, which is before anything it caused to trigger can resolve. See rules 304, 713, 400.2.
410.5a A unit token that dies enters the bin and is then erased. It is not trashed. See rule 801.
410.5b A recalled token, unit or spell, enters its controller's hand and is then erased. It counts as a card entering a hand for anything that is watching. See rule 402.4.
 Example: A Fireball token recalled off the stack enters its controller's hand, Rider of the Tides sees it, and it is erased.
 Example: Recalling a unit token triggers Rider of the Tides too.
410.5c A token put into a cache enters the cache and is then erased.
410.5d Any spell tokens still in play are erased during regroup. See rule 506.
title: CR 410.5–410.5d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
410.6 A card is played from the zone it came out of, even when another effect plays it as it resolves. A card played from the cache, a bin or the deck is not played from the hand. See rules 701, 702.
 Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays cards off the top of the deck; Proph and Stalwart Sentinel ("from anywhere other than your hand") both see it.
title: CR 410.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
(continues 410.6: A card is played from the zone it came out of, even when another effect plays it as it resolves. A card played from the cache, a bin or the deck is not played from the hand.)
410.6a A spell token is cast from where it stands in play, so it is played from somewhere other than the hand. See rule 304.
 Example: Casting a Fireball token triggers Stalwart Sentinel.
title: CR 410.6a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
(continues 410.6: A card is played from the zone it came out of, even when another effect plays it as it resolves. A card played from the cache, a bin or the deck is not played from the hand.)
410.6b A token created by an effect was not played and came from no zone.
 Example: A token created by an effect was not played, so neither Proph nor Stalwart Sentinel triggers.
title: CR 410.6b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 4. Zones › 410. Zone Changes
410.7 When a unit leaves play for a bin, it dies (or, if it was exchanged out of play, despawns) before anything is trashed. The unit and its mods leave play; then its death or despawn happens, and the abilities that trigger on it trigger; only then is any card trashed (see rule 801.2).
 Example: A unit with no mods dies and goes to its controller's bin. Its death comes first, then it is trashed.
 Example: Hooba-Mon exchanges itself for a unit card in its controller's bin. It despawns, and only then is it trashed. It does not die.
title: CR 410.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 500. General
500.1 A turn has four phases, in this order: the planning phase, the battle phase, the regroup phase and the deployment phase. See rules 501, 505, 506, 507.
title: CR 500.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 500. General
500.2 Turns are global: all players share the same phases and sync up at the end of each step. In a 1v1 or team game, the printed rules take some steps in initiative order: the initiative player, or team, acts first, and the non-initiative player waits to see what they did before acting (see rule 501.4 and rule 507.3). See rule 100.
title: CR 500.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 500. General
(continues 500.2: Turns are global: all players share the same phases and sync up at the end of each step. In a 1v1 or team game, the printed rules take some steps in initiative order: the initiative player, or team, acts first, and the…)
500.2a This client makes the turn fully global. In the resource step, the haste step and deployment, both players act at the same time, and neither sees what the other does until both are done (see rule D1.4). This is a digital convention: a paper game cannot hide one player's actions while the other acts.
title: CR 500.2a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 500. General
500.3 In each turn one player has the initiative. In a 1v1 game the initiative player (IT) acts first and the non-initiative player (NIT) acts after them. See rules 103, 508, 904.
500.3a The initiative is not a token. The Initiative token of the physical game only marks which player has it. See rule 304.
title: CR 500.3–500.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 500. General
500.4 The battle phase is the only phase of the turn in which players can interact, because it is the only time a player can enter another player's region. Outside it, every player is alone in their own region: in deployment a player can do what they like to their own units, but no opponent is there to interact with (see rule 601.4b). See rules 501.3, 505, 703.
title: CR 500.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 500. General
500.5 When the deployment phase and its end-of-turn step are over, the turn is over. The initiative and any packs pass to the next player clockwise (see 508), and the next turn begins with its planning phase. See rules 507, 508.
 Example: After turn 1 ends, turn 2 opens with each player drawing 2 and the draft step open again.
title: CR 500.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 501. Planning Phase
501.1 The planning phase is the first phase of the turn. In it, players prepare for the turn ahead by curating their hands and preparing their resources.
title: CR 501.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 501. Planning Phase
501.2 The planning phase has five steps, taken in this order.
501.2a Refresh: each player's expended resources refresh. See rule 106.
 Example: A resource expended to pay debt in one turn is open again for mana in the next.
501.2b The draw step: see 503. See rule 503.
501.2c The draft step: see 503. In constructed, this step is a draw of 2 and a recycle of 2. See rule 503.
 Example: Turn 2 of constructed: the hand gains 4 (2 for the draw step, 2 for the draft step), then 2 cards are recycled, a net gain of 2.
501.2d The resource step: see 502. See rule 502.
501.2e The haste step: see 504. See rule 504.
title: CR 501.2–501.2e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 501. Planning Phase
501.3 There is no player interaction in the planning phase. No player receives priority in it, and nothing a player does in it can be responded to. See rules 504.3, 703.
title: CR 501.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 501. Planning Phase
501.4 In a 1v1 game, the refresh, the draw step and the draft step happen for both players simultaneously. The resource step and the haste step are taken first by the initiative player and then by the non-initiative player. See rules 500.3, 502, 504, D1.5.
501.4a A step of the planning phase ends for all players together. No player begins the resource step until every player has finished the draft step. See rules 503.2, D1.6.
title: CR 501.4–501.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 502. Resource Step
502.1 The resource step is the step of the planning phase in which players create and activate resources. See rule 106.
title: CR 502.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 502. Resource Step
502.2 In the resource step, a player may take these actions. See rule 106.
502.2a Create a resource by recycling a card from their hand. The resource enters play dormant. There is no limit to how many resources a player may create. See rules 106, 408.
 Example: Recycling a hand card for a fire resource puts a dormant fire resource into play and the card into the recycle pile.
502.2b Activate dormant resources by turning them face up, up to two activations per turn. See rule 106.
502.2c Exchange an active Prismite for a resource of any element, or for a Shard (106.8d). A dormant Prismite cannot be exchanged. See rule 106.
 Example: Two starting Prismites are activated, then one is exchanged for a fire resource, which keeps its active state.
title: CR 502.2–502.2c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 502. Resource Step
502.3 The resource step ends when every player has created and activated all the resources they want. See rule 504.
 Example: One player declaring done leaves the other free to keep activating; the haste step opens only when both are done.
title: CR 502.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 502. Resource Step
502.4 At the end of their resource step, a player with debt pays 1 mana for each debt, and each mana paid removes one debt. The payment is automatic: it is not a choice and needs no action. See rule 112.
 Example: A player with 5 open fire and 3 debt ends the resource step with 0 debt and 2 open mana.
502.4a Paying debt is the last thing in the resource step. After it the player can activate no more resources this turn, and the mana spent on debt is not available to play cards this turn. See rule 112.
 Example: With 3 open mana and 2 debt, the player is left 1 mana: no resource action is offered and a [3] unit cannot be played in deployment.
title: CR 502.4–502.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 503. Draw and Draft Step
503.1 In the draw step, each player draws 2 cards. See rules 401, 402.
 Example: On turn 2 of a live draft each player's 6-card hand becomes 8.
503.1a In a live draft, no player draws in the draw step of the first turn: each player's first draw was dealt with their opening hand (see 103). See rule 103.
503.1b Players draw in clockwise order, starting with the initiative player. See rule 500.3.
 Example: In a live draft the initiative player takes the top 2 cards of the shared deck at the start of the turn, and the other player the next 2.
title: CR 503.1–503.1b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 503. Draw and Draft Step
503.2 In the draft step of a live draft, each player combines the cards in their hand with the cards in their pack, then chooses which cards of the combined pile to keep in hand. The rest go back into the pack. See rules 409, 902.
 Example: A player keeps three pack cards and puts three hand cards into the pack; the hand keeps its size.
503.2a A player must leave exactly 10 cards in the pack, so they end the draft step with as many cards in hand as they began it with. See rule 409.
503.2b Within that limit the choice is free: a player may keep their whole hand and take nothing, exchange their whole hand for pack cards, or anything in between.
 Example: A player who keeps their hand exactly passes the pack exactly as dealt.
503.2c When a player has finished drafting, they pass their pack clockwise to the next player. The draft step is complete once every player has passed their pack. See rules 409, 501.4.
503.2d An effect may make a player skip their draft step.
 Example: With Worldbender in play in a live draft, its controller is never offered the pack and ends the step with 3 more cards: the 2 drawn in the draw step and Worldbender's 1.
title: CR 503.2–503.2d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 503. Draw and Draft Step
503.3 After every cycle of N+1 turns, where N is the number of players, every pack is recycled and each player is dealt a new pack of 10 cards. In 1v1 this happens after the third turn, right before the fourth draft. See rules 408, 409.
503.3a So each player drafts a second time from the pack they were first dealt before the packs are refreshed.
 Example: In 1v1, the pack a player is dealt on turn 1 comes back to them on turn 3 with what they left in it.
title: CR 503.3–503.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 503. Draw and Draft Step
503.4 In constructed there are no packs. In the draft step each player draws 2 more cards from their own deck and then recycles 2 cards from their hand. Since this comes straight after the draw step, the two are taken together: draw 4, then recycle 2. See rules 408, 901.
 Example: Worldbender skips the constructed draft step: its controller draws only the draw step's 2 plus Worldbender's 1, recycles nothing, and loses 3 life.
503.4a The player chooses which 2 cards of their hand to recycle. Until they have, they can take no other planning action. See rule 408.
503.4b The draw of 4 and the recycle of 2 happen on the first turn of a constructed game too. See rules 103, 901.
title: CR 503.4–503.4b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 503. Draw and Draft Step
503.5 Drawing and drafting are actions like any other: a unit that a change in hand size leaves with 0 defense, or with damage equal to its defense, dies as soon as the action is over, except as the constructed sub-rule below says (see 713). See rule 713.
 Example: A Dreadspawn Horror (-1/-1 for each card in hand) taken to 0 defense by the turn's draw dies at once, before any other action is taken.
503.5a In the draft step the combined pile of hand and pack is never a hand: only the cards a player keeps count toward their hand size.
 Example: A Dreadspawn Horror whose controller holds 1 card, draws 2 and keeps 3 through the draft ends the step a 4/2 and lives.
503.5b In constructed, the draw of 4 and the recycle of 2 count as one step. A player's units are not checked for death until that player has recycled their 2 cards, so they are judged on the hand that remains. See rules 713, 901.
 Example: With 1 card in hand, a Dreadspawn Horror goes through draw 4 and put back 2 and ends a 4/2.
 Example: With 3 cards in hand it nets to 5 and dies once its controller has put 2 back.
title: CR 503.5–503.5b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 504. Haste Step
504.1 The haste step is the last step of the planning phase. It comes after the resource step. See rule 501.2.
title: CR 504.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 504. Haste Step
504.2 In the haste step, players may play only haste cards. See rules 207, 803.
 Example: Molten Upheaval, a haste card, is refused in the resource step and accepted in the haste step.
504.2a A card with battle timing cannot be played in the haste step, even when an effect gives it haste or lets it be played as if it had haste. This holds for units and spell units alike. See rule 207.
 Example: Under Dispatch Courier, a battle unit in hand is still not playable in the haste step.
title: CR 504.2–504.2a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 504. Haste Step
504.3 A card played in the haste step resolves immediately. It does not use the stack, no player receives priority, and no player can respond to it. See rules 501.3, 703.
 Example: Tidal Menace played in the haste step is in play at once as a 7/2.
title: CR 504.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 504. Haste Step
504.4 The haste step ends when every player has played all the haste cards they want to play, which may be none. See rule 505.
title: CR 504.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 504. Haste Step
504.5 The haste step happens every turn, whether or not any player has anything they could play in it.
 Example: On turn 1, with only two dormant Prismites each, the step still opens for both players.
504.5a No player is treated as finished with the haste step because they have nothing to play. Each player finishes the step themselves, and a player may stay in it holding nothing they could play.
title: CR 504.5–504.5a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 504. Haste Step
504.6 The end of the haste step is an event. An ability that triggers "at the end of [Haste]" triggers then, before the battle phase begins, including in a turn in which nobody played anything in the step. See rule 706.
 Example: Keeper of Tithes creates an X/X for its controller's expended resources as the step closes.
504.6a An instruction a card carries out "during [Haste]" happens in the haste step. This client asks for it as the step ends.
 Example: Prediction Prophet asks its controller for a number at the end of the haste step, and creates a 5/5 at the start of deployment if it matched.
title: CR 504.6–504.6a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 504. Haste Step
504.7 An effect may let a player play, in the haste step, a card that lacks haste, "as if it had [Haste]". The grant changes only when the card may be played. See rules 504.2, 803.
 Example: Dispatch Courier lets its controller play a deploy unit in the haste step.
 Example: Writhing Host in its owner's bin lets them play a deploy unit in the haste step, erasing the Host as the additional cost.
504.7a A grant that says "Each turn" allows one such play per turn for each card that grants it: two Dispatch Couriers allow two plays.
 Example: One Courier grants one play: a second unit in the same haste step is refused.
title: CR 504.7–504.7a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 504. Haste Step
504.8 Mods are applied in deployment, not in the haste step, even when the mod card has haste. The exceptions are a card that allows mods in the haste step (the sub-rule below) and a Virus applied in battle (see 723). See rules 507, 720, 723.
504.8a A card that says so can allow mods in the haste step: Slurpr lets its controller apply other mods, augments and grafts alike, during [Haste] as if it were deployment. See rule 720.
title: CR 504.8–504.8a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 504. Haste Step
504.9 A card whose prophecy condition ends in [Haste] may be prophesied in the haste step as well as in deployment. Any other prophecy may be prophesied only in deployment. See rule 803.
 Example: Divine Intervention's prophecy ("Your life is 5 or less [Haste]") may be prophesied in the haste step.
504.9a The [Haste] marker does not move a fulfilled prophecy's release: the card is played from the cache only at its printed timing. See rule 803.
title: CR 504.9–504.9a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 505. Battle Phase
505.1 The battle phase is the only interactive phase of the game. In it players manage their units across the regions: they attack into other regions or keep units back to defend. See rules 601, 604.
 Example: Player A attacks with a Good Whale: the Whale moves into Player B's region, and Player A enters that region too.
505.1a A player can interact with opponents and their units only during the battle phase. See rules 507, 601.
 Example: In deployment, an effect that targets a cached card can reach only its controller's own cache; once an attack brings both players into a region in battle, it can reach the opponent's cache too.
505.1b An effect that applies "during battle" applies only in the battle phase. It does not apply in the haste step or in deployment. See rules 504, 507.
 Example: Crevice Lurker makes abilities cost [one] more "during battle". Outside battle the same activation costs its printed [1].
 Example: Counter Thief takes counters placed "during battle"; outside battle it does nothing.
title: CR 505.1–505.1b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 505. Battle Phase
505.2 Battle is made of four steps: the attack step, the block step, the combat step and the after-combat step. They take place separately inside each region. See rules 604, 606, 608, 609.
505.2a In a region that is not attacked, the combat step and the after-combat step are skipped. See rule 609.
 Example: When both players decline to attack, neither round has a combat step, and the battle phase ends with no priority window at all.
title: CR 505.2–505.2a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 505. Battle Phase
(continues 505.2: Battle is made of four steps: the attack step, the block step, the combat step and the after-combat step. They take place separately inside each region.)
505.2b An attack step in which no attack is declared opens no priority window. If both battle rounds are declined, the battle phase has no priority window at all. See rules 506, 605.
 Example: The initiative player declines to attack, then the non-initiative player declines too: the game goes to regroup without either player getting priority, so a Fireball token held for the battle is erased unused.
title: CR 505.2b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 505. Battle Phase
505.3 In 1v1 and team games the battle phase has two battle rounds. In round 1 the initiative team attacks into the non-initiative team's regions. In round 2 the non-initiative team's counterattackers attack into the initiative team's regions. See rules 500, 610.
 Example: The initiative player attacks in round 1; the units the non-initiative player sent at blocks attack in round 2.
505.3a Round 1 runs in this order: (1) the initiative team declares its attacks, sending units into non-initiative regions; (2) a priority window; (3) the non-initiative team declares its blocking formations and may at the same time send units out to counterattack; (4) a priority window; (5) the combat step, in which all units in formation deal combat damage at the same time; (6) the after-combat step, the last priority window in that region. See rules 604, 605, 606, 607, 608, 609, 610.
 Example: The initiative player attacks with a 2/2 Curio Drifter; the non-initiative player blocks nothing and sends a Rune Channeler to counterattack. The unblocked Drifter deals 2, and after the after-combat window round 2 begins.
505.3b Units sent out to counterattack leave the region at once, and are treated as if they do not exist until round 1 is finished. See rule 610.
 Example: A Rune Channeler sent to counterattack is absent for the rest of round 1, and arrives in the initiative player's region for round 2.
505.3c Round 2 runs in this order: (1) the non-initiative team puts its counterattacking units into formation; (2) a priority window; (3) the initiative team declares its blocking formation; (4) a priority window; (5) the combat step; (6) the after-combat step, the last priority window in that region before regroup. See rule 610.
 Example: The counterattacking Rune Channeler arrives in the initiative player's region, attacks, is not blocked and deals 4; after the after-combat window the game goes through regroup to deployment.
505.3d Each team gets only one chance to attack in a battle phase. There is no counterattack in round 2. See rule 610.
 Example: The non-initiative player sent a Rune Channeler at blocks and attacks with it in round 2; the initiative player may block it but cannot send a unit of their own out, and the battle phase ends after round 2.
title: CR 505.3–505.3d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 505. Battle Phase
(continues 505.3: In 1v1 and team games the battle phase has two battle rounds. In round 1 the initiative team attacks into the non-initiative team's regions. In round 2 the non-initiative team's counterattackers attack into the…)
505.3e The non-initiative team may declare attacks in round 2 even if the initiative team declared none in round 1. It may then attack with any of its units, because it never had a block step in which to send counterattackers. See rule 610.
 Example: The initiative player could attack and declines; the non-initiative player then attacks in round 2 with a unit that was never sent.
 Example: Only the non-initiative player has a unit; the initiative player declares no attack, and in round 2 that unit attacks from home.
505.3f If round 1 had a battle, only the units sent out at the block step can attack in round 2. If none were sent, there is no round 2. This holds when an effect ends the battle during round 1 (Temporal Rift): ended before blocks, no unit was sent and there is no round 2; ended after blocks, the units already sent attack in round 2. See rule 610.
 Example: The initiative player attacks, the non-initiative player blocks and sends nobody: the battle phase ends after round 1, and the unit that stayed home is untouched.
 Example: A Good Whale that stayed home while a Rune Channeler was sent out cannot be declared as a round-2 attacker.
 Example: The initiative player attacks and the non-initiative player casts Temporal Rift in the attack window: the battle phase ends with no round 2, though the non-initiative player has a unit at home.
 Example: The non-initiative player sends Rune Channeler at the block step, then casts Temporal Rift: round 1 ends before combat damage, and in round 2 the Rune Channeler attacks.
title: CR 505.3e–505.3f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 505. Battle Phase
505.4 Battle is resolved one region at a time. Once players begin interacting in a region, every step of battle is completed in that region before those players can interact anywhere else. See rule 601.
 Example: In 1v1, every step of round 1 finishes in the non-initiative player's region before round 2 starts in the initiative player's region.
505.4a The regions resolve in clockwise order, starting with the region to the left of the initiative player, so the initiative player's region resolves last. See rule 904.
 Example: In a four-player game the region to the initiative player's left resolves first and the initiative player's own region last.
 Example: In 1v1, round 1 is fought in the non-initiative home region and the initiative home region comes last, in round 2.
505.4b In 1v1, round 1 is fought in the non-initiative player's region, and round 2, if there is one, in the initiative player's region. See rules 601, 610.
505.4c While a region's battle is being resolved, units in any other region, including units that stayed home and counterattackers that were sent away, are treated as if they do not exist. See rules 601, 610.
 Example: Player A attacks with a Rune Channeler and leaves a Good Whale at home. Player B casts Luminous Arc: it can target the attacking Channeler, but not the Whale that stayed home.
title: CR 505.4–505.4c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 505. Battle Phase
505.5 In free-for-all games there are no battle rounds: all players declare their attacks at the same time, using intent cards. See rules 903, 905.
title: CR 505.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 505. Battle Phase
505.6 Anything counted "in this battle" is counted separately for each region, and the count starts again at the start of each battle phase. Things that happen outside the battle phase are not counted. See rule 601.
 Example: During a battle a player discards a card, then their attacking unit dies in combat: two cards have been trashed in this battle. At the next battle phase the count starts again from zero.
505.6a The life a player has lost in a battle is the total of every loss in that battle. Life gained in the battle does not reduce it. See rule 112.
 Example: A player loses 10, gains 8, then loses 3: they have lost 13 life in this battle, and Soul Siphon makes a 13/13.
title: CR 505.6–505.6a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 506. Regroup Phase
506.1 Regroup is a global step that takes place once battle has ended in every region. It resets the game between battles. See rule 505.
506.1a No player gets priority or takes any game action during regroup.
 Example: When the last player passes in the after-combat window, the game goes through regroup and straight into deployment; no one is given priority in between.
506.1b Regroup comes before the deployment phase, not at the end of the turn. So a spell token made, or a temporary change applied, during deployment lasts until the regroup after the next battle. See rule 507.
 Example: Overbloom played in deployment gives +7/+7 "until regroup"; the bonus lasts through the next battle and is gone after its regroup.
title: CR 506.1–506.1b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 506. Regroup Phase
506.2 Regroup does these things, in this order: (1) all players and units return to their own regions; (2) all damage on units is removed; (3) all temporary stat changes are removed; (4) all units leave formation. All spell tokens are also erased. See rule 602.
 Example: After a battle the attacker is back home, both players are back in their own regions, its marked damage and its -2/-2 are gone, there is no formation, and the spell token is erased.
506.2a Each unit that is not in its controller's home region returns there. This includes a unit that was created in another region. See rules 601, 108.
 Example: Life Plant's 1/1s, created in the enemy region during an attack, walk home at regroup.
 Example: The attacker and the counterattacker are both back in their home regions after regroup.
506.2b Each player who entered another region during battle stops being present there, and is present only in their own region again. See rule 601.
506.2c All damage on units is removed. See rule 112.
 Example: A Good Whale carrying 1 marked damage has none after regroup.
506.2d All temporary stat changes are removed. An effect that lasts "until regroup" ends here. See rule 709.
 Example: Overbloom's +7/+7 "until regroup" is gone after the next regroup.
 Example: Jelly's -2/-2 on an attacker is gone after regroup.
506.2e All units leave formation. See rule 602.
506.2f All spell tokens in play are erased, including unused spell tokens in a player's own region. See rules 304, 407.
506.2g A card can keep spell tokens through regroup. While Harbinger of Immolation's [Augment] text applies, its controller's spell tokens are not erased; they keep their X, and they still lose their temporary changes. Other players' spell tokens are still erased. See rules 721, 101.
 Example: With Harbinger of Immolation in play as a unit, your spell tokens stay through regroup.
 Example: With Harbinger of Immolation in play, your Fireball 7 token survives regroup still a Fireball 7, but any temporary changes on it are gone.
506.2h A spell token erased at regroup takes its mods with it. See rules 720, 304.
 Example: A Fireball token augmented during deployment and not cast is erased at regroup, and its augment is erased with it.
title: CR 506.2–506.2h

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 506. Regroup Phase
506.3 Unit tokens are not erased at regroup. They stay in play like other units. See rule 304.
 Example: The 1/1 unit tokens Life Plant made in the enemy region are still in play after regroup, back in their home region.
title: CR 506.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 507. Deployment Phase
507.1 The deployment phase is the last phase of each turn. In it players build up their forces for the next battle by playing cards, activating abilities, and modifying cards with graft and augment. See rule 720.
 Example: In deployment a player plays Ignis Sprite (its spawn trigger makes a Fireball) and then Flame Juggle.
507.1a Any card can be played during deployment except a battle card, which can be played only in the battle phase. See rules 207, 803.
 Example: In deployment a player plays Flame Juggle and gets a Fireball token. Fireball is a battle card, so the token cannot be cast until the battle phase.
507.1b During deployment each player is alone in their own region. A player cannot interact with other players or their units, and treats every other player as if they did not exist. See rules 601, 505.
 Example: Beyond's rot replacement says "target unit", and in deployment only its controller's own units are offered.
507.1c An effect in deployment that refers to opponents finds none. "Each opponent loses 1 life" does not affect any other player. See rule 601.
 Example: Thoughtripper trashed outside battle makes no opponent discard, because no opponent is present.
title: CR 507.1–507.1c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 507. Deployment Phase
507.2 Modifications are applied during deployment. A mod may be applied from the hand or the bin, and a glimpsed mod also from the cache. See rules 720, 403.
507.2a Grafting is done during deployment, whatever the card's speed, even for a card with Haste, and never in battle. A graft can be applied in the haste step only where an effect lets mods be applied then as if it were deployment, such as Slurpr's. See rules 722, 504.
 Example: With a Slurpr in its controller's region, a graft lands during the haste step.
507.2b During deployment a player may augment a spell token they have in play. Only the augment's attributes pass to the token. See rules 721, 304.
 Example: A Fireball 3 token augmented in deployment with Chitin Shredder gains {Powerful}, and when cast in battle it deals 6.
title: CR 507.2–507.2b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 507. Deployment Phase
507.3 In 1v1 and team games the printed rules have the initiative team deploy first. Its players deploy in any order they wish, and then the non-initiative team does the same. See rules 500, 904, D1.5.
 Example: In a 2v2 game both initiative players finish deploying before either non-initiative player begins.
title: CR 507.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 507. Deployment Phase
(continues 507.3: In 1v1 and team games the printed rules have the initiative team deploy first. Its players deploy in any order they wish, and then the non-initiative team does the same.)
507.3a In this client both players deploy at the same time. Neither sees what the other does in deployment until both are done, and either may finish first. See rule D6.
 Example: The non-initiative player is offered plays at once, and can finish deploying while the initiative player is still acting.
 Example: During deployment Player A plays Ignis Sprite; nothing of it appears in Player B's game log while deployment is under way.
title: CR 507.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 507. Deployment Phase
507.4 The deployment phase begins in this order: (1) each player is dealt damage equal to their rot, in initiative order; (2) then abilities that trigger "at the start of deployment" trigger. See rule 112.
 Example: A player controls Beyond, Codex Incarnate and has 2 rot. At the start of deployment the rot comes first: Beyond asks them to pick a unit (they pick their Good Whale), and only after that do 'at the start of deployment' abilities trigger.
507.4a All abilities that trigger at the start of deployment are put on the stack before any of them resolves. See rules 703, 706.
title: CR 507.4–507.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 507. Deployment Phase
507.5 Deployment uses the stack. Each player's plays, activated abilities, spell tokens and triggered abilities in deployment go on that player's own deployment stack, and that stack resolves without anyone acting: no player holds priority in deployment (rule 703.7). See rule 703.
 Example: In deployment, a player cannot ask to keep priority: the ask is refused.
title: CR 507.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 507. Deployment Phase
(continues 507.5: Deployment uses the stack. Each player's plays, activated abilities, spell tokens and triggered abilities in deployment go on that player's own deployment stack, and that stack resolves without anyone acting: no player…)
507.5a A decision one player must answer during deployment does not make the other player wait: the other player may keep playing, and their own deployment stack keeps resolving. See rule D6.
 Example: Player B is answering a choice; meanwhile Player A plays a card in deployment and it resolves.
 Example: Player B has three Wraiths, and their start-of-deployment triggers are asking B to choose. Meanwhile Player A can still act, and can even finish deploying; B's triggers then resolve normally.
title: CR 507.5a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 508. Passing the Initiative
508.1 The end of turn is a special step after deployment finishes. In it, abilities that trigger "at the end of turn" resolve. See rule 706.
 Example: Harbinger of Immolation creates a Fireball X at the end of turn.
508.1a No player can play cards during the end-of-turn step, either after the end-of-turn triggers or in response to them.
 Example: While a General Smof end-of-turn trigger is asking its question, neither player is offered a card, spell token, ability, graft or augment, and an Ignis Sprite play is refused.
title: CR 508.1–508.1a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 508. Passing the Initiative
508.2 After deployment and the end of turn, the turn is over. The next turn begins with the planning phase. See rule 501.
 Example: Once both players are done deploying and the end-of-turn trigger is answered, the turn number goes up by one and the phase is planning.
title: CR 508.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 508. Passing the Initiative
508.3 When the turn is over, the initiative token is passed to the next player clockwise. In 1v1 and team games this means the initiative alternates between the teams every turn. See rules 500, 904.
 Example: The player without the initiative this turn has it once the turn ends, declares the first attack of the next battle, and the turn after that it passes back.
508.3a Draft packs are passed in the draft step: each player passes their pack clockwise to the next player when they finish drafting, and the draft step is complete once all players have passed their pack. The end-of-turn passing of "any draft packs" with the initiative names this same pass; a pack is not passed a second time when the turn ends. See rules 503, 902.
 Example: After both players finish drafting, each holds the pack the other drafted from.
 [Verification of 508.3a was only partial.]
title: CR 508.3–508.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 5. Turn Structure › 508. Passing the Initiative
508.4 The initiative token is not a token. An effect that refers to tokens never affects it. See rule 304.
 Example: Download says "Gain control of target token"; it cannot be used to take the initiative token.
title: CR 508.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 6. Regions, Formations and Battle › 600. General
600.1 Units are the basis of combat. They attack opponents, enter other players' regions and defend against units that enter their own. Combat takes place inside regions (rule 601), with the units that take part arranged in formations (rule 602) made up of columns (rule 603). See rules 601, 602, 603.
 Example: Two units attack into the opponent's region. The defender blocks one of them; the other is unblocked and deals its damage to the defending player.
title: CR 600.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 6. Regions, Formations and Battle › 601. Regions
601.1 All gameplay takes place inside regions. There is one region for each player, and each player starts in their own region.
601.1a Each region is isolated from every other region. Nothing in one region interacts with anything in another region, and each region treats the players and cards in other regions as if they don't exist. See rule 601.8.
 Example: Towering Colossus prints “Enemies gain +2/+2.” An enemy unit standing in a different region from the Colossus does not get the bonus.
601.1b Every effect is specific to the region it takes place in, and never affects anything in another region. Read every card as if it said “in this region”: “Delete target unit” means “Delete target unit in this region”, and “Each player sacrifices two units” means “Each player in this region sacrifices two units in this region”.
 Example: Ghord's controller sacrifices a unit, and each opponent sacrifices a nontoken unit. Only the opponent's units in Ghord's region can be sacrificed this way.
601.1c “All” means all in this region. An effect that affects or counts “all” of something affects or counts only the ones in its own region.
 Example: Cosmic Reversal recalls all other spell units. A spell unit that its opponent left at home, outside the battle region, is not recalled.
601.1d A static ability sees and affects only things in its own region. A triggered ability triggers only on events in its own region: a spell played in one region does not trigger an ability of a unit in another region.
 Example: Flourishing Flora watches for another ally spawning. An ally that spawns in a different region does not trigger it.
