705.6 Some actions are not activated abilities, and rules and effects that apply to activating abilities do not apply to them: applying a mod (an augment or a graft), playing a card as an Ambush, casting a spell token, using a resource, and taking an option a card offers as a spell is played (rule 109.6). See rules 109.6, 701.2, 111.10f.
 Example: during battle Crevice Lurker taxes activated abilities, but applying an augment costs nothing extra.
title: CR 705.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.1 A triggered ability is an ability that happens when something else takes place. "When" and "Whenever" mark a triggered ability. A triggered ability can also happen at a stated time, such as "After combat" or "At the end of turn". See rule 109.3.
 Example: Embermaw Fledgling's "after combat" ability creates an X/X unit after combat.
title: CR 706.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.2 A triggered ability triggers at the moment its event happens, and whether it triggers is decided then (rule 109.3a). It is put on the stack afterwards, at one of the times this section gives, and its targets are chosen and its costs paid only as it is put on the stack. See rules 109.3a, 111.8.
 Example: a "whenever I am dealt damage" ability triggers inside the combat damage step, but is put on the stack, and has its target chosen, after the step.
 Example: the {Alluring} trigger chooses its target as it goes on the stack, and can then be negated.
title: CR 706.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.3 Triggered abilities that have triggered are put on the stack at the times below, depending on when they triggered.
 Example: Eminence of the Barrens damaged by a spell in battle has its trigger on the stack as soon as the spell has resolved, while Lithoghul damaged in combat triggers inside the damage step and is put on the stack only in the after combat step.
706.3a During battle, outside the combat damage step: as soon as the action or resolution that made them trigger is complete, on top of anything already on the stack. Players then receive priority and may respond to them. See rule 703.
 Example: Eminence of the Barrens dealt damage by a spell in battle puts its trigger on the stack, and the opponent may respond to it.
title: CR 706.3–706.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
(continues 706.3: Triggered abilities that have triggered are put on the stack at the times below, depending on when they triggered.)
706.3b During the combat damage step: they wait. They are put on the stack in the after combat step, or at a window between damage sub-steps, as rules 608.9b and 608.9c describe. See rules 608.9b, 608.9c.
 Example: a "when I die" ability of a unit killed by combat damage waits with the others and goes on the stack after combat.
title: CR 706.3b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
(continues 706.3: Triggered abilities that have triggered are put on the stack at the times below, depending on when they triggered.)
706.3c During deployment: on the deployment stack of the player who controls them (rule 703.7). All the abilities that trigger at the same moment are put on that stack before any of them resolves. See rule 703.7.
title: CR 706.3c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
(continues 706.3: Triggered abilities that have triggered are put on the stack at the times below, depending on when they triggered.)
706.3d In the end-of-turn step: they resolve as special actions. No player can play cards in response to them (rule 508.1a). See rule 508.1a.
 Example: while an end-of-turn trigger is asking its controller a question, neither player may play a card.
title: CR 706.3d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.4 An ability that triggers on a card being played, or on something being targeted, is put on the stack above the effect that made it trigger, so it resolves first. It still resolves if that effect is negated afterwards.
 Example: Mycelial Mentor is played while Bloomcaster is in play. Bloomcaster's 1/1 is created before the Mentor arrives, so the Mentor does not see that token being created.
 Example: a spell unit that is negated after Bloomcaster triggered still leaves Bloomcaster's 1/1 behind.
title: CR 706.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.5 Triggered abilities that are put on the stack at the same time are put there in the order of rule 703.4: each player orders their own, the initiative player puts all of theirs on first, and the non-initiative player's resolve first. A player may order their own abilities in any way, whatever made each of them trigger. See rule 703.4.
 Example: a player with a "when I die" ability triggered by combat damage and an "after combat" ability orders the two in one choice.
title: CR 706.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.6 A triggered ability triggers once each time its event happens. If one action makes the event happen several times, the ability triggers that many times. See rule 109.3d.
 Example: an enemy spell that targets two allies triggers Earnest Defender twice, and two 1/1s are created.
706.6a Several cards that enter a hand together in one move are one event. An ability that triggers when a card, or one or more cards, enters a hand triggers once for that move.
 Example: Rider of the Tides is attacking. Its controller plays Tilling the Graves, returning Curio Drifter and Bumblecrab from the bin to hand in one move. That is one entry into the hand, so the Rider triggers once and gets +2/+2, not +4/+4.
title: CR 706.6–706.6a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
(continues 706.6: A triggered ability triggers once each time its event happens. If one action makes the event happen several times, the ability triggers that many times.)
706.6b Each mod that Reconfigure moves onto a new host is applied to that host separately. An ability that triggers whenever a mod is applied triggers once for each of them. See rule 721.
 Example: Reconfiguring a unit carrying three mods onto Perpetual Construct triggers it three times.
title: CR 706.6b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.7 A triggered ability triggers only on events in the region its card is in. An event in another region does not trigger it, even when the event involves its controller. See rule 601.
 Example: Refuse Reclaimer does not grow when a unit dies in a region it is not in.
706.7a An "after combat" ability triggers only in a region where a battle took place. See rule 609.
 Example: A unit with an "after combat" ability in a region where no battle happened does not trigger.
 Example: a unit with an "after combat" ability that stands in the battle region but in no formation still triggers.
title: CR 706.7–706.7a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.8 An ability of a unit that triggers on its own death ("When I die") triggers when the unit dies, although the unit has then left play. The ability is put on the stack in the region where the unit died. See rule 714.
 Example: A "when I die" ability of a unit that died in the battle region can target things in the battle region, not in its controller's home region.
706.8a An ability that triggers when its unit despawns ("When I despawn"), including one a mod gives its host, triggers whichever way the unit leaves play: when it dies, when it is recalled, and when it is cached.
 Example: a host carrying Growing Plague that is recalled to its hand triggers Growing Plague's despawn ability.
 Example: the same host cached triggers it too.
title: CR 706.8–706.8a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
(continues 706.8: An ability of a unit that triggers on its own death ("When I die") triggers when the unit dies, although the unit has then left play. The ability is put on the stack in the region where the unit died.)
706.8b Moving a unit and its mods onto another unit (Reconfigure) is not a despawn: the unit does not change zones, so its "When I despawn" abilities do not trigger. See rule 721.
 Example: Bubb wearing Growing Plague is Reconfigured onto a Robot; Growing Plague does not trigger.
title: CR 706.8b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
(continues 706.8: An ability of a unit that triggers on its own death ("When I die") triggers when the unit dies, although the unit has then left play. The ability is put on the stack in the region where the unit died.)
706.8c Units that die together hear each other. A unit destroyed in the same batch of deaths as other units still triggers on their deaths, and on their cards being trashed, as it would have had it survived. See rule 713.
 Example: Muck Rummager killed by combat damage alongside two allies still draws for its controller trashing those allies.
title: CR 706.8c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.9 An ability that triggers when a spell is played targeting something reads the targets the spell declared as it was played. A target changed onto that thing later does not make the ability trigger, and a target changed away from it later does not undo the trigger. See rule 109.3a.
 Example: a spell played at another unit and then retargeted onto Earthbound Replicator makes no copy.
 Example: a spell played at Earthbound Replicator and then retargeted away still makes its copy.
title: CR 706.9

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.10 An "If you do" clause in a triggered ability is part of that ability, not a separate triggered ability. It resolves as part of the ability, and it is not put on the stack or taxed separately.
 Example: Eminence of the Barrens attacks under an enemy Crevice Lurker and is damaged by a spell. Its controller is asked the Crevice Lurker tax once for the trigger, and the [one] to fight is asked while that same trigger resolves, and is never taxed itself: each trigger costs 2 in all, the tax plus the fight.
title: CR 706.10

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.11 {Alluring} and {Resonant} work as triggered abilities of the unit or source that has them. What they do is put on the stack, so it can be responded to and negated, and an effect that taxes triggered abilities applies to it. See rules 802, 111.10f.
 Example: Crevice Lurker taxes the {Alluring} trigger, and declining the tax stops the lure.
 Example: Containment Protocol negates an {Alluring} trigger waiting on the stack.
 Example: a {Resonant} source's extra damage waits on the stack after combat as that source's ability, and can be negated.
title: CR 706.11

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.12 Some triggered abilities choose a unit without targeting it, such as a Wraith's start-of-deployment ability choosing "an ally". The unit is chosen as the ability begins to resolve, from the units in play then. Several such abilities resolve one at a time, each choosing among the units still in play, so a unit an earlier one destroyed is not offered to a later one. One that finds no unit to choose fizzles. See rule 704.5c.
 Example: three Wraith abilities and one 1/1 ally: only the first is offered the 1/1 and kills it; the other two put their counters on Wraiths still in play, and nothing fizzles.
 Example: all three Wraith abilities are on the stack before the first one asks for its ally, and each asks only after the one before it has fully resolved.
 Example: a Wraith with no other ally is its own only ally. Its ability chooses it without asking and it shrinks to 2/2; nothing fizzles.
 Example: a 1/1 carrying two Wraith augments: the first ability kills it, and the second finds no ally in play and fizzles.
706.12a Choosing a unit this way is not targeting it. It does not trigger "when I become targeted" abilities, and it cannot be redirected.
 Example: a Wraith ability choosing Mohruung does not give its controller a Crystal.
title: CR 706.12–706.12a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 706. Triggered Abilities
706.13 An ability that triggers on a card being played, and then acts on what was played ("negate that effect"), acts on the item that play put on the stack. Another item with the same name and the same controller is not it, whether it is older or newer. A copy of the played spell is not it either, because a copy is not played (see rule 701.5). See rule 701.5.
 Example: Two Burgeons by the same player are on the stack, and only the second one's play makes Void Mandible trigger. The Mandible negates the second Burgeon, not the first.
 Example: A copy of Burgeon sits below a newly played Burgeon. Void Mandible negates the played Burgeon and leaves the copy alone.
 Example: Origon negates the spell whose play made it trigger, even with an identical spell above it on the stack.
 Example: Void Mandible negates a unit Wake the Dead plays by its stack item, not a same-named bystander.
title: CR 706.13

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.1 A static ability states a change that its card continuously makes to the game for as long as the card is in play. See rule 109.4.
 Example: Prickly Protector's "+1/+1 for each other ally" is counted again whenever its stats are read.
title: CR 707.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.2 A static ability does not use the stack. It cannot be responded to or negated, and an effect that changes what abilities cost to activate or trigger does not apply to it.
 Example: Crevice Lurker does not tax Tranquility's "spells cost [one] more"; Tranquility still adds exactly one.
 Example: Aetherflux Golem's "I gain +2/+2" never goes on the stack, so Containment Protocol cannot negate it.
title: CR 707.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.3 Only triggered abilities and activated abilities put anything on the stack. A triggered ability says "When" or "Whenever" or names a time such as "After combat"; {Alluring} and {Resonant} also work as triggered abilities; an activated ability is written with a colon. A sentence that states a standing fact ("I gain +2/+2", "Spells cost [one] more to play during battle") is a static ability, and a sentence that says "instead", "as" or "if" and names no target is a replacement effect. Neither goes on the stack, except that a replacement whose substitute names a target puts that substitute on the stack. See rules 708.1, 109.5a, 706.1, 706.11, 705.1, 708.2a.
title: CR 707.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.4 A static ability applies continuously to everything it describes, including units that enter play after it began to apply. When its source leaves play, the change ends. See rule 709.
 Example: a unit that enters play while Transmogrifant is in play has no attributes, and gets them back when Transmogrifant leaves.
707.4a A unit that enters play while a static ability applies to it enters with the change already made. An ability that triggers on the unit entering play sees the unit as changed.
 Example: under Sandstone Defender a 1/1 enters as a 1/3, so Nectar Ridge Oracle ("an ally spawns with greater defense than power") draws.
 Example: under Infernal Wispweaver a 0/1 Wisp enters as a 2/2, so Nectar Ridge Oracle does not draw.
 Example: Animated Spark's +X/+0 applies to a unit that spawns mid-battle from the moment it spawns.
title: CR 707.4–707.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
(continues 707.4: A static ability applies continuously to everything it describes, including units that enter play after it began to apply. When its source leaves play, the change ends.)
707.4b A static ability that changes stats ("I gain +2/+2") puts no counters on the unit. Effects that count, move, double or remove counters do not see the change, and it ends as soon as its source stops applying it.
title: CR 707.4b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.5 A card's statement that it enters play with counters ("I spawn with two +1/+1 counters") is not a triggered ability. The unit enters play already holding those counters; nothing goes on the stack, and an ability that triggers on the unit entering play sees it with them.
 Example: Aethercap Siphoner (printed 4/4, "I spawn with three -1/-1 counters on me") is seen as a 1/1 by an ability that triggers when it spawns.
 Example: neither Powerforge Synergist's nor Aethercap Siphoner's counters can be responded to.
title: CR 707.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
(continues 707.5: A card's statement that it enters play with counters ("I spawn with two +1/+1 counters") is not a triggered ability. The unit enters play already holding those counters; nothing goes on the stack, and an ability that…)
707.5a The player who spawns the unit puts those counters on it, so everything that applies when counters are put on a unit applies to them: a replacement effect that changes how many are put, a replacement effect that puts them on another unit instead, and an ability that triggers when counters are put on a unit. A unit whose counters are put on another unit instead enters without them. See rules 708.4, 713.2.
 Example: under an allied Flux Resonator a Robot 2 enters as a 3/3.
 Example: Aethercap Siphoner's own -1/-1 counters count as its controller putting counters on an ally, so Scrapyard Custodian draws.
 Example: Aethercap Siphoner spawned during a battle triggers Pestilent Mycelion ("whenever one or more -1/-1 counters are put on a unit").
 Example: During battle, a Robot 2 created where a Counter Thief is enters with no counters: the two counters are placed on the Counter Thief instead, and the Robot, a 0/0, dies.
title: CR 707.5a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.6 A static ability applies only in the region its source is in. See rule 601.
 Example: Rotspore Herald ("Everything is {deadly}") in its home region does not make a spell resolving in the battle region deadly.
title: CR 707.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.7 A static ability applies to everything its text names, with no limit its text does not state. "Everything" means every unit, spell and spell token in its region, on both sides.
 Example: with Rotspore Herald in the region, a spell that deals 1 damage destroys a 7/5.
 Example: a Fireball 1 spell token in Rotspore Herald's region is {Deadly} too.
707.7a A static ability that names "spells" applies to spell tokens too, because spell tokens are spells. See rule 108.2.
 Example: Emberflame Enlightener says "Your units and spells gain {Powerful}". Its controller's Fireball token is a spell, so it has {Powerful} too.
title: CR 707.7–707.7a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.8 A static ability that applies to effects with a number of targets ("spell effects with a single target") counts the targets the effect declared as it was played, including targets that have since become illegal.
 Example: Twin Flame played at two units is not "a single target" for Envoy of Lightning, even after one of them is removed.
title: CR 707.8

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.9 A static ability or replacement effect that a mod gives its host works from the host. "I" and "me" mean the host, "you" and "your" mean the host's controller, and it applies in the host's region. See rule 720.
 Example: Transmogrifant as a mod gives "your other units +2/+2" from its host.
 Example: Crevice Lurker as a mod taxes abilities in its host's region.
title: CR 707.9

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 707. Static Abilities
707.10 A permission a card grants ("You may play one unit with no abilities from your bin each deployment") is a standing fact, not an ability that goes on the stack. Using it cannot be responded to, and an effect that negates activated or triggered abilities cannot stop it.
 Example: The Bonesculptor's permission is used by playing the unit from the bin like any card. Nothing of the permission's own goes on the stack, so there is no ability for Containment Protocol to negate.
 Example: Each Bonesculptor allows one such play each deployment.
 Example: Gridxlan's "If your hand is empty, you may play one unit from your bin during deployment" is a permission too: with its controller's hand empty, it offers any unit in the bin as a play.
title: CR 707.10

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.1 A replacement effect is an ability that changes an event as it happens, written "If … instead". It replaces the event, rather than triggering in response to it. See rule 109.5.
 Example: Flux Resonator ("if one or more counters would be put on a unit by an allied source, put that many counters plus one instead") makes a counter put on an ally one more.
title: CR 708.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.2 A replacement effect does not use the stack. It cannot be responded to, and an effect that negates triggered and activated effects (Containment Protocol) cannot stop it or undo what it did.
 Example: Containment Protocol on the stack cannot negate Nullbringer's life-gain replacement.
 Example: Conduit of Pain's extra damage never reaches the stack, so nothing can negate it.
title: CR 708.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
(continues 708.2: A replacement effect does not use the stack. It cannot be responded to, and an effect that negates triggered and activated effects (Containment Protocol) cannot stop it or undo what it did.)
708.2a A replacement effect whose substitute names a target is the one exception (rule 109.5a): the event is replaced at once, and the substitute goes on the stack as a triggered ability. If the substitute later has no legal target or fizzles, the replaced event still does not happen. See rule 109.5a.
 Example: Beyond, Codex Incarnate replaces its controller's rot damage with -1/-1 counters on a target unit; the damage never lands, whatever becomes of the counters.
title: CR 708.2a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.3 The event a replacement effect replaces does not happen, and the substitute happens instead. Abilities that trigger on the replaced event do not trigger. When the substitute is still damage (damage dealt "as" rot), the damage was still dealt (rule 112.12). See rule 112.12.
 Example: under Nullbringer a player who would gain life loses that much instead; nothing that triggers on gaining life triggers.
 Example: a Robot that Cosmic Conspirator replaces with a Fireball is never created, so nothing that triggers on a unit spawning triggers for it.
 Example: with Blightsea Polyp in play, Zephyrzoa's column still deals combat damage to the opponent, although the opponent gains rot instead of losing life.
title: CR 708.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.4 A replacement effect applies to an event only once. What it produces is not replaced again by the same effect, unless a new event occurs. See rules 608.8c, 708.4a.
 Example: 10 {Piercing} combat damage redirected into a 2/4 Oorblak: 4 destroy it, and the other 6 reach the player; the same Oorblak does not take them again.
 Example: two Nullbringers turn one life gain into one loss, not into a gain again.
708.4a If two or more replacement effects could apply to one event, they apply one at a time. Each applies at most once, to the event as the earlier ones left it, and only if that event still matches its own text; one that has applied does not apply again, so nothing loops. The player the event affects (the player who would be dealt the damage, the player whose rot it is, or the controller of the unit the counters would be put on) chooses the order in which they apply, except where rule 608.8c fixes it. When only one such effect applies, nothing is asked.
 Example: two Oorblaks and combat damage that would be dealt to their controller: the first to apply takes all of it, and the other takes 0, because the damage is no longer being dealt to that player.
 Example: the player who would be dealt the damage chooses which of two Oorblaks applies first, and that one takes it.
 Example: two Counter Thieves: the counters the first redirects onto itself are still being placed on a unit, so the second, which has not applied, takes them; they end on the second to apply.
 Example: the controller of the unit the counters were meant for chooses the order of two Counter Thieves; choosing the second to apply last puts the counters on it.
 Example: two Counter Thieves do not pass the same counters back and forth: each applies once.
 Example: two Automatons of Abundance turn one created token into three: 1, then 2, then 3.
 Example: two Skittering Blights: the player whose rot it is chooses which one takes it as counters; the other has nothing left to replace.
title: CR 708.4–708.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.5 Replacement effects that only change an amount ("that many plus one instead") all apply: each applies once, and their changes add up. A modifier does not apply to its own change, but two copies of the same card are two modifiers and both apply.
 Example: two Conduits of Pain make 1 damage from an allied source into 3.
 Example: two allied Flux Resonators make a Robot X spawn with X plus 2 counters.
title: CR 708.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.6 Effects that double an amount ("Double all life gain and life loss") multiply together. With n of them applying to the same amount, it is multiplied by 2 to the power n.
 Example: three Arbiters of Vitality multiply a life loss by 8.
708.6a When modifiers that add to an amount and an effect that doubles it apply to the same amount, the additions are made first and the result is doubled. See rule 112.9.
 Example: a {Powerful} Bellowing Boulder with Conduit of Pain deals (1+1)x2 = 4 damage to each unit.
 Example: Conduit of Pain and Arbiter of Vitality: the 1 is added before the life loss is doubled.
708.6b A multiplied life loss is lost all at once, as one loss of the whole amount, and only then does the game check whether the player has lost. See rule 104.
 Example: Arbiter of Vitality doubles a lethal loss before the game checks whether the player has lost.
title: CR 708.6–708.6b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.7 When a replacement that changes the number of counters and a replacement that redirects them both apply to the same placement, the number is changed first, and the redirect then moves the whole changed number.
 Example: a Counter Thief beside a Flux Resonator steals the extra counter too.
title: CR 708.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.8 A replacement effect applies only to what its own text names. One that applies when counters "would be put on" a unit does not apply when counters are removed.
 Example: Proliferating Slime does not change how many counters Burn the Blight removes.
708.8a Counters of either sign are counters. A replacement effect that adds to counters being put on a unit adds -1/-1 counters to -1/-1 counters, as it adds +1/+1 counters to +1/+1 counters.
 Example: Flux Resonator makes two -1/-1 counters its controller puts on a unit into three.
title: CR 708.8–708.8a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
(continues 708.8: A replacement effect applies only to what its own text names. One that applies when counters "would be put on" a unit does not apply when counters are removed.)
708.8b Whether counters are put "by an allied source", or put by "you", depends on whose effect put them, not on whose unit they land on. Counters that a redirect moves are still put by the player whose effect put them.
 Example: counters an opponent's effect puts on your unit do not get your Flux Resonator's extra counter.
 Example: counters your effect puts on an enemy unit do.
708.8c Moving counters from one unit onto another removes them from the first and puts them on the second. Only the second half puts counters on a unit, so a replacement effect that applies when counters would be put on a unit changes how many arrive, not how many leave. See rule 708.8b.
 Example: Your Flux Resonator is in play and you cast Scrap For Parts ("Move all counters from target unit onto another target unit"), moving an enemy unit's two +1/+1 counters onto your unit: the enemy unit is left with none, and your unit gets three.
title: CR 708.8b–708.8c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.9 All the tokens one resolution of one effect creates are created together. A replacement effect that acts on "each unique token you created" sees all of them at once, and a token is unique by its name, its X and the stats the effect that created it set, together.
 Example: Automaton of Abundance with Manufacture (a Robot 3, a Robot 2 and a Robot 1) creates three extra Robots.
 Example: three identical Robot 2s created together are one unique token and yield one extra.
 Example: a 3/3 and a 5/5 unit token created together are two unique tokens and yield two extras.
title: CR 708.9

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.10 When an effect says a player's life total can't change, a gain or loss of life for that player does not happen at all, and no replacement effect applies to it.
 Example: with the life total locked by Suspend, Nullbringer has no gain of life to turn into a loss.
title: CR 708.10

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
708.11 A prevention effect ("if damage would be dealt …, prevent it") is not a replacement effect. Prevented damage is not dealt at all (rule 112.11), while damage a replacement effect changes is still dealt (rule 112.12). See rules 112.11, 112.12.
 Example: a unit shielded by Phytochemical Protection and hit by a {Poisonous} unit takes no -1/-1 counters and does not trigger on being dealt damage.
708.11a A prevention effect on a unit prevents all the damage dealt to it, including any beyond what would destroy it.
 Example: a lone shielded blocker is assigned the whole of a column's damage, and all of it is prevented.
title: CR 708.11–708.11a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects
(continues 708.11: A prevention effect ("if damage would be dealt …, prevent it") is not a replacement effect. Prevented damage is not dealt at all (rule 112.11), while damage a replacement effect changes is still dealt (rule 112.12).)
708.11b Prevention applies to the damage as it would be dealt, after the recipient's own doubling ({Vulnerable}). It does not change how damage is assigned or how much is lethal (rule 608.6g). See rule 608.6g.
 Example: a shield changes what is dealt to a unit, never how much of a {Piercing} hit goes past it.
title: CR 708.11b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
709.1 A continuous effect changes the game for a period of time rather than once. It comes either from a static ability, and lasts as long as that ability is in play, only in its region; or from an effect that says how long it lasts, such as "until regroup". See rules 206.6, 113, 707.
 Example: Sudden Bloom gives your units in its region +1/+1 until regroup, and the bonus is gone after regroup.
title: CR 709.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
709.2 A continuous effect applies to a unit that enters play while the effect applies, from the moment it enters. The unit enters play already changed, so an ability that looks at the unit as it enters sees the changed unit. See rule 707.
 Example: under Sandstone Defender ("Your other units gain +0/+2") a 1/1 enters as a 1/3, so Nectar Ridge Oracle ("When another ally with greater defense than power spawns, draw a card") draws.
 Example: under Infernal Wispweaver a 0/1 Wisp enters as a 2/2, so Nectar Ridge Oracle does not draw.
title: CR 709.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
709.3 When the source of a static ability leaves play, its continuous effect ends at once. The units it was changing are again what they would be without it, and they get back any attributes and abilities it had removed. See rule 712.
 Example: a unit that entered play under Transmogrifant has no attributes; when Transmogrifant leaves play it has them again.
 Example: when Infernal Wispweaver leaves play, Wisps sacrifice themselves after combat again.
title: CR 709.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
709.4 A unit's stats are worked out layer by layer, in the order of rule 206.4. Every effect in one layer applies before any effect in the next layer, whatever order the effects began in. Within one layer, effects apply in timestamp order (rule 113). See rules 206.4, 113.1.
 Example: An effect that makes a unit base 4/4 applies over Apex Prime's copy effect whether the copy began before it or after it, because base stats are a later layer than the copy.
title: CR 709.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
(continues 709.4: A unit's stats are worked out layer by layer, in the order of rule 206.4. Every effect in one layer applies before any effect in the next layer, whatever order the effects began in. Within one layer, effects apply in…)
709.4a Before those layers, a copy effect decides which card the unit's printed stats come from. A unit that is a copy of a card has that card's printed stats as its layer 1, and every later layer applies to them (rule 710). See rule 710.
 Example: a Unit Token that becomes a copy of Good Whale and is Unaware reads as a 7/5, Good Whale's printed stats.
title: CR 709.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
(continues 709.4: A unit's stats are worked out layer by layer, in the order of rule 206.4. Every effect in one layer applies before any effect in the next layer, whatever order the effects began in. Within one layer, effects apply in…)
709.4b In layer 4, Tough applies first, doubling the unit's defense, and Balanced after it, making the unit's power and defense equal to the greater of the two. The order holds whatever gave the unit each attribute (printed on it, an augment, an effect or its column) and whichever it gained first. So Tough augmented onto a Balanced unit, Tough given to a Balanced unit by an effect, and a Tough unit attacking with a Balanced unit behind it are all doubled, then balanced. See rule 802.
 Example: Child of Aether (2/0, printed Balanced) augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough) is doubled first (still 2/0), then balanced: a 2/2.
 Example: The same Child of Aether given Tough by an effect is also doubled first (still 2/0), then balanced: a 2/2.
title: CR 709.4b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
(continues 709.4: A unit's stats are worked out layer by layer, in the order of rule 206.4. Every effect in one layer applies before any effect in the next layer, whatever order the effects began in. Within one layer, effects apply in…)
709.4c An attribute is either present or not. A unit that has the same attribute from several sources has it once, and it applies once.
 Example: two Reality Benders on one unit make it Inverted once; they do not cancel out.
title: CR 709.4c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
(continues 709.4: A unit's stats are worked out layer by layer, in the order of rule 206.4. Every effect in one layer applies before any effect in the next layer, whatever order the effects began in. Within one layer, effects apply in…)
709.4d Inverted (layer 5) applies after all of layer 4, whatever order the unit gained its attributes in. A unit that is Tough and Inverted has the same stats whichever of the two it gained first. See rule 802.
 Example: a 1/4 that is Tough and Inverted is a 1/0, in either grant order.
title: CR 709.4d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
709.5 A unit's stats are worked out all at once. A unit whose stats would reach 0 defense partway through the calculation does not die for that; only the final result counts (rule 713). See rule 713.
 Example: a 1/1 with a -1/-1 counter that is Inverted is a 2/2, never a dead 0/0 on the way.
title: CR 709.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
709.6 An effect that exchanges the base stats of two units (Body Swap) gives each unit the other's base stats as they are when it resolves. It is a base rewrite of its own, later than any base rewrite already applying, so it wins over one. See rules 206.5, 113.4.
 Example: your 1/1 and an enemy Wisp that Aberrant Statweaver makes base 3/3 are exchanged: your unit becomes base 3/3 and the Wisp base 1/1, until regroup.
title: CR 709.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
709.7 An effect that doubles a unit's power or defense until regroup gives the unit a temporary stat change (layer 3) of the size that makes the final stat, after every layer, twice what it was. Because the change is in layer 3, it is still there if an attribute in a later layer stops applying.
 Example: a 1/10 Tough unit (a 1/5, doubled) doubled by Burgeon gets +0/+5 and is a 1/20. If it then loses Tough to Monke, it is a 1/10.
title: CR 709.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps
709.8 Where an effect that switches a unit's power and defense until regroup (Invasive Reassignment) applies in the stat layers is an open ruling. The engine applies it as a temporary stat change worked out from the unit's stats when it resolves, so a stat change that comes afterwards applies on top and is not switched.
 Example: An 8/3 unit switched by Invasive Reassignment is a 3/8; if it then gets +2/+0 it is a 5/8, not switched again.
title: CR 709.8

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
710.1 A unit that becomes a copy of a card takes that card's name, printed stats, attributes and text in place of its own. The physical card does not change: in every zone other than play it is still its own card (rule 410.3a). See rules 201.5, 410.3a.
 Example: a Borrower of Forms that copies a unit takes its name, its attributes and its text.
 Example: a unit that is a copy dies and its own card goes to the bin, not the copied card.
710.1a While a unit is a copy, its mana cost and its card type are those of the card it copies. A Borrower of Forms that copied a Robot costs 0, and while it copies a unit it is not a spell unit. See rules 202.7, 303.11a.
 Example: a Borrower of Forms that copied a Robot costs 0, so Lumengrove Lurker can recall it.
 Example: while it copies a unit, Cosmic Reversal's "and spell units" does not recall it.
title: CR 710.1–710.1a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
(continues 710.1: A unit that becomes a copy of a card takes that card's name, printed stats, attributes and text in place of its own. The physical card does not change: in every zone other than play it is still its own card (rule…)
710.1b Counters and marked damage belong to the unit, not to the card it copies. A unit keeps them when it becomes a copy, and keeps them when the copy ends.
 Example: a 1/1 that becomes a 7/5 until regroup and takes two -1/-1 counters dies when the copy ends at regroup.
title: CR 710.1b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
710.2 A unit that becomes an "exact copy" (Borrower of Forms) also takes the stat changes and the counters of the unit it copies, and its card text including the text of its mods. Its layer-1 stats are the copied unit's base stats.
 Example: Borrower of Forms erases its target and takes its stats and counters.
710.2a A copy of a modded unit has what the mods say, but no mod is copied. The copy is not modded, so it is not Unstable. Its copied grafts run as part of its graft cause, and each copied augment gives it that augment's [Augment] box. See rules 722, 721, 803.
 Example: a Borrower of Forms that copied a unit carrying a Powerful virus is Powerful, and is not modded or Unstable.
 Example: A Borrower of Forms that copied a Bellowing Boulder with Flame Juggle grafted has the Boulder's whole trigger, Flame Juggle's grafted part included.
710.2b More grafts may be added to a copy of a grafted unit, but they go underneath the copied grafts. See rule 722.
 Example: A graft added to a Borrower of Forms that copied a grafted unit resolves below the copied grafts.
title: CR 710.2–710.2b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
(continues 710.2: A unit that becomes an "exact copy" (Borrower of Forms) also takes the stat changes and the counters of the unit it copies, and its card text including the text of its mods. Its layer-1 stats are the copied unit's base…)
710.2c When a copy of a modded unit leaves play, only its own card goes anywhere. Nothing is binned or erased for the mods it copied, because it has none. A mod later put on the copy is a real mod, and makes it Unstable as usual. See rules 410.3a, 410.4b.
 Example: a Borrower of Forms that copied a unit with a virus dies, and only Borrower of Forms goes to the bin.
710.2d A [once] ability from a copied augment can be used once per turn on the copy, exactly as if a real mod of that card were on it. A copy of a unit with two augments of the same card has two such uses, one for each. See rule 109.9.
 Example: a Borrower of Forms that copied a Graxxlid-augmented unit can use Graxxlid's ability once per turn.
 Example: A copy of a unit wearing two Debt Blep augments offers two activations, and spending one leaves the other.
 Example: A copy of a unit wearing two Jollyglop augments triggers twice when it is dealt damage.
title: CR 710.2c–710.2d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
710.3 If a unit becomes a copy more than once, the latest copy applies. It does not have two faces.
 Example: an Apex Prime copy made when attacking and another made when blocking leave the unit one copy, the later one.
title: CR 710.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
710.4 A copy of a unit that is itself a copy copies what that unit currently is, not the card printed on it.
 Example: a copy of a Borrower of Forms that copied a virused unit carries the copied virus's text too.
title: CR 710.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
710.5 An effect that creates a copy of its own source ("create a copy of me") creates a token copy of what the source currently is. The token has none of the source's counters and none of its mods. When a unit has the ability through another unit (Ancient One, rule 710.7), "me" is the unit that has it, so the copy is of that unit (rule 710.7a). See rules 304.4a, 714.
 Example: Hooba-God, killed under its own attack trigger, still creates a copy of what it was.
 Example: Three Echoes of Despair beside an Ancient One, after a battle in which a player lost life: three Ancient Ones are created.
 Example: An Ancient One borrowing Echo of Despair, Hooba-God or Swarmling copies itself, not the unit it borrowed from.
title: CR 710.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
710.6 A copy that lasts until regroup (Apex Prime) ends at regroup. The unit is its own card again, still with its counters, and it dies if its own stats cannot survive them. See rules 506.2d, 713.
title: CR 710.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
710.7 An ability that gives a unit "all abilities" of other units (Ancient One) gives it everything in those units' text boxes, including the text their mods give them and the abilities effects have given them, but not their attributes, their name or their stats. The unit has the text only while the other units qualify, and loses it the moment they stop; as it leaves play, whether it dies or is recalled, cached, exchanged or erased, it still has the text of the units it was adjacent to, so their "when I die" and "when I despawn" abilities trigger for it, even when such a unit dies in the same batch as it. It gets nothing from a unit that has lost its abilities, and none of a unit's text that works only while that card is in another zone (such as its bin). Two Ancient Ones adjacent to each other each have the abilities of every unit adjacent to either of them. Each unit it has the text from gives it a use of its own: next to two units with the same [once] ability, it may use that ability twice.
 Example: Ancient One has an adjacent ally's static ability, and loses it when the column breaks.
 Example: an adjacent ally's attributes are not given to Ancient One.
 Example: Ancient One keeps its own name and stats.
 Example: Ancient One between two Jollyglops makes a 1/1 for each of them when it is dealt damage.
 Example: Ancient One between two Debt Bleps has two activations.
 Example: Two adjacent Ancient Ones both have the abilities of a unit adjacent to either of them.
 Example: An Ancient One dying with Reforge the Dead's grant on it and on its two neighbours makes three Robots.
 Example: An adjacent ally that has lost its abilities lends Ancient One nothing.
 Example: Ancient One does not have the bin text of a neighbour in play.
 Example: A dying Ancient One has the "when I die" text of the allies it stood beside.
 Example: A recalled Ancient One has the "when I despawn" text of the ally it stood beside.
 Example: An Ancient One that dies in one batch with both of its neighbours has both of their "when I die" abilities.
 Example: Beside a unit wearing Infernal Wispweaver as a mod, Ancient One has only the Wispweaver's [Augment] text, not the text of its body.
title: CR 710.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
(continues 710.7: An ability that gives a unit "all abilities" of other units (Ancient One) gives it everything in those units' text boxes, including the text their mods give them and the abilities effects have given them, but not their…)
710.7a In text a unit gets this way, "I" and "me" mean the unit that has the text, not the unit it came from.
 Example: next to Gatekeeper of Souls ("I must be targeted if able"), it is the Ancient One that must be targeted.
 Example: Three Echoes of Despair beside an Ancient One: its three borrowed "create a copy of me" abilities create three Ancient Ones.
title: CR 710.7a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
710.8 A copy of a spell is put on the stack above the spell it copies, so it resolves first. It is an effect on the stack like any other: players may respond to it, and it can be targeted and negated. See rules 108.4, 703, 704.2d.
 Example: Earthbound Replicator's copy goes on the stack above the original, so it resolves first.
 Example: the copy can be chosen as a "target effect" and negated by Dematerialize.
710.8a A copy of a spell keeps what the original declared when it was cast: its X, its mode and its targets. Additional costs the original paid are not paid again. The copy is given new targets only if the card that makes it says so. See rule 107.6.
 Example: Maelstrom Charger's copy of Volatile Toxicity uses the original's sacrifice, which is not paid again.
 Example: A copy of Fight keeps both targets the original declared.
title: CR 710.8–710.8a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
(continues 710.8: A copy of a spell is put on the stack above the spell it copies, so it resolves first. It is an effect on the stack like any other: players may respond to it, and it can be targeted and negated.)
710.8b A copy of a spell targets what it targets: an ability that triggers when something becomes a target sees the copy's targets, although the copy was not played. See rule 108.4.
 Example: an enemy plays Burgeon on an attacker beside Earnest Defender and copies it with Maelstrom Charger, keeping the targets. Earnest Defender triggers twice, once for the spell and once for its copy.
710.8c A copy of a spell has no card. An instruction on it to erase itself erases nothing, and however many copies resolve, only the original card goes to a bin. See rule 704.2d.
 Example: a resolved copy of Suspend puts nothing in a bin and its "Erase me." erases nothing; the original Suspend is erased once.
710.8d A copy of a spell carries the {Modular} mods the original was cast with, so their [Augment] attributes apply to the copy too. See rule 724.
 Example: Spellbind cast with Primordial Coalescence as a Modular mod and copied with Maelstrom Charger: the copy on the stack carries the same mods as the original.
title: CR 710.8b–710.8d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 710. Copies and Faces
710.9 A card that transforms in play is the same unit with its other face up: its name, stats and text are those of the face that is up. It keeps that face while it stays in play, and turns back over as it leaves play (rule 410.3). See rules 108.3, 410.3.
 Example: Scholar of the Void transforms into Beyond, Codex Incarnate and is still the same unit.
title: CR 710.9

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 711. Control Change
711.1 When a player gains control of a unit, the unit changes sides: it becomes that player's unit, an ally of that player's units and an enemy of its former controller's. Its owner does not change. See rules 102.4, 102.5, 102.7b.
 Example: A stolen unit is recalled: it goes to the hand of the player who controls it.
 Example: Its owner is unchanged.
title: CR 711.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 711. Control Change
711.2 A unit's mods change controller with it. The unit's new controller controls the mods and their text, so text a mod gives the unit refers to the new controller. See rules 102.6a, 720.
 Example: Mindspore Fiend gives away a modded blocker, and its mods go with it.
title: CR 711.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 711. Control Change
711.3 A unit whose controller changes leaves its formation. If this happens during a battle, the unit stays in the battle out of formation for the rest of that battle: it attacks for nobody and blocks for nobody. It joins its new controller's side at regroup. See rules 602, 506.2a.
 Example: a Robot token stolen by Download mid-battle is out of the formation for the rest of the battle.
 Example: the stolen Robot joins its new controller's side at regroup.
711.3a If a unit that was blocking changes controller, the attacking column it blocked stays blocked. See rules 606, 607.
title: CR 711.3–711.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 711. Control Change
711.4 A unit given to a player who is not present in the region where it stands (for example, during deployment) goes at once to that player's home region, with its mods. During a battle both players are present in the battle region, so the unit stays there. See rules 101.6, 506.2b.
 Example: Mindspore Fiend gives away a modded blocker after combat, and it stays in the battle region.
title: CR 711.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 711. Control Change
711.5 An effect that exchanges control of two units and swaps their positions (Organic Exchange) leaves both units in formation: each takes the other's place, which is on its new controller's side.
 Example: Organic Exchange swaps control, and the attack slot passes to the exchanged unit.
title: CR 711.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 711. Control Change
711.6 An effect that would give control of a unit to the player who already controls it, or of a unit that has gone, changes nothing. An "If you do" that depends on the handover does not happen (rule 101.5a). See rule 101.5a.
 Example: Amphivore carries the grafts Flame Juggle and Ralph, and its trigger runs them three times. The first time, Ralph gives Amphivore to the opponent and creates three 1/1s. The second and third times the opponent already controls it, so nothing changes hands and no more 1/1s are made; Flame Juggle still runs all three times.
title: CR 711.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 711. Control Change
711.7 A unit that leaves play goes to the zones of the player who controls it, not of its owner, unless the effect names another player's zone (rule 405.3). See rules 405.3, 410.4a.
 Example: a stolen unit recalled goes to the thief's hand.
title: CR 711.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 711. Control Change
711.8 A mod is controlled by the controller of the unit it is on. When a mod is moved onto another unit (Rotbeast, Reconfigure), its controller becomes that unit's controller. See rules 720, 410.1b.
 Example: an augment Rotbeast moves onto an enemy takes its Unstable and its static ability with it.
title: CR 711.8

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
712.1 Some effects make a unit lose all its attributes, all its abilities, or both ("loses all attributes and abilities"). While the unit has lost them, they do not apply. See rule 113.3.
 Example: Monke makes other units lose all attributes and abilities during battle.
712.1a Losing all abilities takes everything the unit's text does by itself: its triggered abilities, its activated abilities (which cannot be activated), its static abilities and cost changes, and its replacement effects, whether printed on it, given by its mods or granted to it. A unit that loses its abilities stops applying its static abilities at once, whether a one-time effect (Suppression Field) or a continuous one (Transmogrifant, Monke) took them; two continuous strips that each fall under the other are rule 712.5. See rule 712.5.
 Example: a copy silenced by Suppression Field stops applying the static it copied.
 Example: With Transmogrifant and Sandstone Defender in play, Sandstone Defender has lost its abilities, so a 1/1 token gets only Transmogrifant's +2/+2 and is a 3/3.
title: CR 712.1–712.1a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
(continues 712.1: Some effects make a unit lose all its attributes, all its abilities, or both ("loses all attributes and abilities"). While the unit has lost them, they do not apply.)
712.1b Stats are not abilities. A unit that has lost its abilities keeps its stats, its counters and its stat changes; Tough and Balanced stop changing its stats only because they are attributes. It can still be targeted, block, die, and be grafted onto.
title: CR 712.1b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
(continues 712.1: Some effects make a unit lose all its attributes, all its abilities, or both ("loses all attributes and abilities"). While the unit has lost them, they do not apply.)
712.1c Erasing a unit's mods is a separate instruction from making it lose its abilities. Losing abilities silences the text its mods give it; erasing the mods removes them.
title: CR 712.1c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
712.2 A strip takes what the unit has when the strip applies. An attribute or ability the unit gains afterwards (a mod attached later, an attribute or ability granted later, a static ability that starts applying later) is not taken. See rules 113.3, 113.3a, 113.3b.
 Example: after Suppression Field resolves on Bubb, Protective Adaptations gives Bubb Piercing, and it has it.
 Example: a virus applied after Monke still gives its attribute.
 Example: A continuous strip takes a mod attached before it began, and leaves one attached after.
title: CR 712.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
712.3 When an effect that removes attributes (Formless, Suppression Field) is aimed at a unit in a formation, every unit in that unit's column loses its attributes, whichever unit they came from. Only the loss of attributes reaches the column: the rest of the effect, such as the loss of abilities or Formless's "base 4/4", applies to the target alone. See rule 712.8.
 Example: Formless takes Blessed off the whole column, not just its target.
 Example: Suppression Field aimed at either unit of a column takes both Unaware and Flying from both.
 Example: Formless's base 4/4 still hits the target alone.
title: CR 712.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
(continues 712.3: When an effect that removes attributes (Formless, Suppression Field) is aimed at a unit in a formation, every unit in that unit's column loses its attributes, whichever unit they came from. Only the loss of attributes…)
712.3a A target that is not in a column (outside battle, or out of formation) loses only its own attributes.
712.3b Each unit in the column loses its attributes as its own state, until the effect ends. A unit that leaves the column does not get them back, and a unit that joins the column afterwards keeps its own. See rule 113.3b.
 Example: Formless is aimed at a unit whose column-mate is Blessed. The column-mate loses Blessed, stays without it for the rest of the battle after combat damage is over, and gets it back at regroup.
title: CR 712.3a–712.3b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
(continues 712.3: When an effect that removes attributes (Formless, Suppression Field) is aimed at a unit in a formation, every unit in that unit's column loses its attributes, whichever unit they came from. Only the loss of attributes…)
712.3c A unit that has lost its attributes can still get attributes from a column it joins later, by sharing. It does not share the attributes it lost.
 Example: a stripped Bubb that later joins a Balanced unit's column is Balanced, and the column is not Unaware.
title: CR 712.3c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
712.4 An effect that switches off one named behaviour stops only that behaviour; it does not take the unit's other abilities. Only "loses all abilities" takes them all.
 Example: Infernal Wispweaver stops a Wisp sacrificing itself after combat, and the Wisp keeps an ability it was given.
title: CR 712.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
712.5 Two continuous strips whose sources each fall under the other do not both apply: the newer one applies, and the source of the older one loses its abilities, so the older strip does not apply. If the newer source leaves play, the older strip applies again. Where only one of the two sources falls under the other's strip, that source loses its abilities, even if it came into play later (rule 113.3a).
 Example: With two Transmogrifants in play, a 1/1 token is a 3/3: only the newer Transmogrifant's +2/+2 applies. The older one gets the newer one's +2/+2 and has lost its abilities; when the newer one leaves play, the older one applies again.
 Example: Two Monkes in battle: the newer Monke keeps its abilities, and the older one loses them.
 Example: The Everywhere comes into play under its controller's Transmogrifant: it loses its abilities, so the card it names keeps its abilities.
title: CR 712.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
712.6 The Everywhere's controller names a card during the haste step. Every unit with that name in The Everywhere's region loses all abilities, for as long as The Everywhere is in that region. Naming another card replaces the first, and a card that is not in play may be named. A token's name is not a card's name and cannot be named, even while a token with that name is in play (see rule 108.2a).
 Example: an enemy copy is silenced only once The Everywhere attacks into its region.
 Example: With Unit Tokens in play, Unit Token is not among the names The Everywhere offers.
712.6a The Everywhere may name The Everywhere. Every The Everywhere in its region then loses all abilities, the one that named it included, and the naming keeps applying: the namer losing its abilities does not end its own strip. See rule 712.5.
 Example: A player names The Everywhere with The Everywhere. Every copy in the region loses its abilities, the namer too, and the silence stays on.
title: CR 712.6–712.6a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
712.7 Text a copy has from the mods of the unit it copied is part of the copy's own card text. An effect that makes the copy lose all attributes and abilities takes it, and "erase all of its mods" finds no mod to erase. See rule 710.2a.
 Example: Suppression Field strips the augment text a Borrower of Forms copied.
title: CR 712.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
712.8 Units in the same column of a formation share their combat attributes: each unit in the column has every combat attribute any unit in it has. See rules 204.5, 802.
title: CR 712.8

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
(continues 712.8: Units in the same column of a formation share their combat attributes: each unit in the column has every combat attribute any unit in it has.)
712.8a A unit in a column has the column's attributes for everything it does while it is in the column, not only for combat damage. An ability it activates, or damage it deals by an effect, uses them too.
 Example: an ability fired by a unit in a Blessed column gains its controller life.
 Example: Powerful from the column doubles that damage too.
712.8b Columns exist only in battle. Outside battle a unit shares no attributes with anything.
title: CR 712.8a–712.8b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
(continues 712.8: Units in the same column of a formation share their combat attributes: each unit in the column has every combat attribute any unit in it has.)
712.8c Attributes are shared only within a column, never with the units to the left or right.
 Example: Good Whale attacks with a unit behind it in its column and another unit in the next column. The unit behind it has Piercing; the unit in the next column does not.
712.8d When a unit leaves a column, the other units in it lose at once the attributes it was sharing with them.
 Example: once the Deadly unit leaves Bellowing Boulder's column, the Boulder's ping is not Deadly.
712.8e Non-combat attributes, such as Unstable, Burst and Modular, are not shared. A modded unit is Unstable, but the units in its column are not. See rules 204.5, 803.
title: CR 712.8c–712.8e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 712. Stripping and Suppression
(continues 712.8: Units in the same column of a formation share their combat attributes: each unit in the column has every combat attribute any unit in it has.)
712.8f Two questions are each unit's own, whatever its column shares: a unit with Feeble cannot block even in a column with other units, and an Alluring trigger comes from the unit that has Alluring. See rule 802.
title: CR 712.8f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
713.1 State checks are made by the game itself, at safe points. In a state check, every unit that should be dead dies, and every token that is in a zone where it cannot exist ceases to exist. See rules 713.2, 713.5.
 Example: a lethally damaged unit and a dead unit token both go at the next safe point; the card reaches the bin, the token is erased, and a token recalled to a hand is erased from it.
title: CR 713.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
713.2 A unit dies in a state check if its defense is 0 or less, or if the damage marked on it is greater than or equal to its defense. See rules 112.5, 206.
 Example: the turn's draw takes Dreadspawn Horror ("I gain -1/-1 for each card in your hand") to 0 defense, and it dies.
title: CR 713.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
713.3 The end of every action is a safe point, so no action ends with a unit standing that should have died: not a draw, a draft, a recycle or a resource activation. An action that is waiting on a player's decision has not ended and is not at a safe point; it is checked when the answer comes and the action finishes. The one exception is Constructed's draw phase, where drawing 4 and putting 2 back are judged as one step: a player's units are not checked while that player still has the 2 cards to put back. See rules 503.5, 503.5b, 112.8, 713.3a.
 Example: in Constructed, Dreadspawn Horror with 3 cards in hand is still in play after the draw of 4, and dies once its controller has put 2 back (5 cards in hand).
 Example: in Constructed, Dreadspawn Horror with 1 card in hand is a 4/2 after the draw phase and lives.
713.3a Deaths are also checked while an effect is still resolving, not only at safe points. Each time an effect puts counters on a unit, and after each part of an effect made of several parts, units that should be dead die at once, before the rest of the effect happens. See rules 713.3, 713.6.
 Example: Pestilent Titan attacks and its trigger puts a -1/-1 counter on each unit. A 1/1 token dies as soon as it gets its counter, before the next unit gets one.
title: CR 713.3–713.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
713.4 A unit can die in a state check from a change no damage caused: a new base, a stat change, a mod it loses, or a combination of attributes (Tough and Inverted) that leaves its defense at 0 or less. See rules 709.4d, 802.
 Example: Rampart Guardian makes a unit Tough, then Reality Bender makes it Inverted, and it dies with no damage on it.
title: CR 713.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
(continues 713.4: A unit can die in a state check from a change no damage caused: a new base, a stat change, a mod it loses, or a combination of attributes (Tough and Inverted) that leaves its defense at 0 or less.)
713.4a Pure does not change a unit's printed stats, so it does not by itself save a unit from a state-check death: a Pure 2/3 dealt 3 damage dies. But a Pure unit ignores its own other attributes, the stat-changing ones included (rule 802.25a), so a combination of its own attributes cannot kill it in a state check. See rule 802.
 Example: A Pure 1/3 that is also Tough and Inverted ignores both, reads 1/3, and lives through the state check.
title: CR 713.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
713.5 In a state check, a token that is in any zone other than play or the stack (a hand, a bin, a cache) ceases to exist. This happens before anything its arrival there caused to trigger is put on the stack. See rules 410.5, 407.3.
 Example: A Hooba-Mon token is exchanged out of play by Skittering Blight. It goes to the bin, and the state check then erases it from there.
title: CR 713.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
713.6 Units that die in the same state check die together. Each of them still sees the others leave: an ability of one that triggers when another unit dies, or when a card is trashed, triggers for the others in the same batch. See rules 112.8, 706.
 Example: Muck Rummager dies from combat damage in the same batch as an ally, and still triggers on that ally being trashed.
713.6a A unit that dies in the batch does not see its own departure that way, and it is not a legal target or an ally for a count while the batch is dealt with.
 Example: Cthyrian Culler dying alone makes nobody lose life for its own trash; dying beside an ally, it triggers once, for the ally.
 Example: Splort dies in the same batch as an ally; its trigger for the ally cannot target either dead unit.
title: CR 713.6–713.6a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
(continues 713.6: Units that die in the same state check die together. Each of them still sees the others leave: an ability of one that triggers when another unit dies, or when a card is trashed, triggers for the others in the same batch.)
713.6b Units that one effect deletes all at once ("delete all units …") die together in the same way: they are one batch, and each of them still sees the others leave (706.8c). See rules 706.8c, 801.5.
 Example: After combat Ruinbringer deletes a row of three units: an Ancient One between two units that have "when I die" abilities. The three die in one batch, so the Ancient One borrows both of its neighbours' "when I die" abilities.
title: CR 713.6b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
713.7 A unit sent out to counterattack, which does not exist until round 1 ends, is not checked for death while it is away. It is checked as it comes back. See rules 505.3b, 610.
 Example: Prickly Protector, alive only through its own static, survives being declared as a counterattacker.
 Example: a counterattacker sent out alone survives the send and dies on arrival.
713.7a A unit that stays home does not count a unit that has gone to counterattack as an ally. See rule 102.7.
 Example: Prickly Protector, carrying a -1/-1 counter, is alive only because it has one other ally. When that ally is sent to counterattack, the Protector stays home, no longer counts it, and dies.
title: CR 713.7–713.7a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 713. State Checks
713.8 A unit that is destroyed dies: by a state check, by being sacrificed, or by being deleted. An {Unstable} unit that is destroyed still dies. A unit that leaves play any other way, by being recalled, cached, exchanged or erased, does not die. See rules 410.2, 407.1c.
 Example: Banishment erases a unit, and no death is recorded.
title: CR 713.8

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 714. Last-Known State
714.1 A unit's last-known state is what it was at the instant it left play: its card and the face it showed, its controller, its region, its attributes (including those its column shared with it), its power and defense, and the formation it stood in. See rule 704.7.
 Example: Deathglow Strider, sharing Piercing in a Good Whale column with a +1/+1 counter, is destroyed before its after-combat trigger resolves; the trigger remembers a 3/4 Piercing Deathglow Strider of its controller, in that region and formation.
title: CR 714.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 714. Last-Known State
714.2 An effect whose source has left play has the attributes its source had when it left, including attributes shared with it by its column then. See rule 704.7a.
 Example: Bellowing Boulder dies with a Deadly unit beside it and its ping on the stack; the ping is still Deadly.
title: CR 714.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 714. Last-Known State
714.3 An effect whose source has left play that uses its source's power or defense uses the power or defense the source had when it left.
 Example: Deathglow Strider (printed 2/3) with a +1/+1 counter is a 3/4. It leaves play before its after-combat trigger resolves; the trigger deals 4 to each opponent, its last-known defense, not its printed 3.
 Example: Spewing Mushroom (printed 1/3) gets +2/+0 and leaves play before its attack trigger resolves; the trigger creates a Poison 3, from its last-known power 3.
title: CR 714.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 714. Last-Known State
714.4 An effect whose source has left play that refers to the source's formation ("in my formation", "attacking units in my formation") uses the formation the source stood in when it left, for the rest of that battle. See rules 602, 704.7a.
 Example: Hooba-Lin, killed under its own attack trigger, remembers its formation and the 1/1 joins it.
 Example: Embermaw Fledgling, gone before its trigger resolves, still counts the attackers it stood with.
title: CR 714.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 714. Last-Known State
714.5 A count of the allies adjacent to a source that has left play is 0.
 Example: Flamebreath Initiate removed before its trigger resolves still makes a Fireball 1 (X = 0).
title: CR 714.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 714. Last-Known State
714.6 An effect whose source has left play that makes a copy of the source copies what the source was when it left. See rule 710.5.
 Example: Echo of Despair, gone before its after-combat trigger resolves, still makes its copy.
title: CR 714.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 714. Last-Known State
714.7 While its source is still in play, an effect reads the source as it is when the effect resolves, not as it was when the effect was put on the stack. See rules 107.8, 109.3b.
 Example: Deadly given back to Bellowing Boulder before its ping resolves makes the ping Deadly again.
title: CR 714.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 714. Last-Known State
714.8 A source that is still in play but out of formation (for example, a unit stolen mid-battle, rule 711.3) stands in no formation. An effect that places units in its formation, or counts it, does nothing. See rule 711.3.
 Example: a Hooba-Lin alive but out of the formation makes no token.
title: CR 714.8

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 714. Last-Known State
714.9 The facts of how a unit left play are fixed as it leaves: the region it left from, the counters it carried, whether it was a token, how it left, and where its card went. Abilities that trigger on its leaving use those facts.
714.9a An ability that triggers on its own source leaving play ("when I die") resolves in the region the source left from, not in its controller's home region. See rule 101.6.
title: CR 714.9–714.9a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.1 A modification (mod) changes a card's abilities by combining cards together. A card that can be a mod carries one of two mod symbols: the augment symbol (721) or the graft symbol (722). See rules 721, 722, 305.
 Example: Aetherflux Golem (augment) and Flame Juggle (graft) are offered as mods; The Foretold, with neither symbol, is not.
720.1a Virus and Modular are not further kinds of mod. A Virus is a card that can also be applied as an augment during battle (723). Modular lets mods be applied to a card as it is played (724). See rules 723, 724.
title: CR 720.1–720.1a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.2 Applying a mod is a special action, which a player may perform during the deployment phase. See rule 507.2.
720.2a A timing icon other than Virus does not change when a card can be applied as a mod. A Battle card cannot be applied as a mod during battle, except under a card that lets cards be augmented as if they were Viruses (723.5) or to a Modular card as it is played (724). See rules 207.6, 723.5, 724, 720.2b.
 Example: Burning Vengeance, a Battle card, is not offered as a mod during battle, but it is offered to Spellbind, a Modular card, played in battle.
 Example: Hooba-Lin, a Haste augment card, cannot be applied as a mod in the haste step when no card such as Slurpr allows it.
720.2b A mod can be applied outside deployment only where a rule or a card says so: a Virus during battle (723.2); a card augmented in battle under a card that lets it be augmented as if it were a Virus, such as Rook (723.5); a mod applied in the haste step under a card that allows it, such as Slurpr (504.8a); and a mod applied to a Modular card as it is played (724). No other card widens the window. See rules 723, 504.8a, 724.
