720.2c An effect that lets a player play cards does not let them apply mods. Tides of the Cosmos cannot graft a card or apply a non-Virus augment; it may only put a Virus card onto a unit as a Virus. See rule 701.2c.
title: CR 720.2–720.2c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.3 Applying a mod is not playing a card, from whatever zone the mod comes. An ability that triggers when a player plays a unit, a spell or a card does not trigger when a mod is applied. See rules 701.2, 701.2a.
 Example: Stalwart Sentinel counts a spell played from the bin, but not a mod applied from the bin.
 Example: A Virus applied during battle is not a spell: Origon does not negate it, and it does not count as a spell played.
title: CR 720.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.4 To apply a mod, a player must meet the mod card's affinity requirement and pay its mana cost, wherever the mod comes from. See rules 105.8, 720.4b.
title: CR 720.4

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
(continues 720.4: To apply a mod, a player must meet the mod card's affinity requirement and pay its mana cost, wherever the mod comes from.)
720.4a A modifier to the cost of playing cards or spells does not change the cost of applying a mod, and a modifier to the cost of activating or triggering abilities does not apply to applying a mod either. See rules 701.2b, 111.10.
 Example: Under Crevice Lurker, applying an augment during battle costs only its own mana.
720.4b A mod applied from the cache is priced by the permission that lets it be used. Under a fulfilled prophecy it costs nothing and ignores affinity. Under a glimpse this turn it costs its mana but ignores affinity. See rules 403.3c, 720.5a.
title: CR 720.4a–720.4b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.5 A mod may be applied from the player's hand or from their bin. See rule 405.8.
720.5a A mod may also be applied from the cache, but only while a permission to use that card is live: a fulfilled prophecy, or a glimpse this turn. A cached card with no live permission cannot be applied as a mod. See rules 403.3b, 720.4b.
title: CR 720.5–720.5a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.6 A mod becomes part of the card it is applied to, its host. A modified card is treated as a single card with all of the additional text from its mods; the mods are not separate from it. See rule 305.1.
 Example: Aetherflux Golem augmented onto a unit gives that unit +2/+2 and is not a unit of its own.
720.6a A mod is controlled by its host's controller. A player who augments a card onto an opponent's unit gives that opponent control of the mod and all of its text. See rule 102.6a.
 Example: In battle, a player applies Corrupting Blight as a Virus to an opponent's Bubb. The opponent now controls the Blight, so its "you" is the opponent: after combat, a player who doesn't control Bubb gains control of it, and Bubb ends up with the player who applied the Blight.
title: CR 720.6–720.6a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
(continues 720.6: A mod becomes part of the card it is applied to, its host. A modified card is treated as a single card with all of the additional text from its mods; the mods are not separate from it.)
720.6b On a mod's text, "you" means the host's controller. See rule 102.6a.
 Example: Oorblak applied as a Virus to an opponent's unit: the combat damage that would be dealt to that opponent is dealt to their own unit instead.
720.6c On a mod's text, "I", "me" and "my" mean the host.
 Example: Life Leech applied as a Virus gives its host, not the Leech, +3/+3 when its controller pays 5 life.
720.6d On a mod's text, "other" and "another" exclude only that mod itself, not other mods made from copies of the same card.
 Example: A host wearing two Rotbeast augments: each Rotbeast moves the other.
720.6e When a unit changes controller, its mods change controller with it. See rule 711.
 Example: Download steals a unit token that carries an augment; the augment changes controller with it.
title: CR 720.6b–720.6e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
(continues 720.6: A mod becomes part of the card it is applied to, its host. A modified card is treated as a single card with all of the additional text from its mods; the mods are not separate from it.)
720.6f There is no limit to the number of mods a card can have.
 Example: Six Aetherflux Golems augmented onto one unit give it +12/+12.
title: CR 720.6f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.7 As long as a card is modded, it has {Unstable}: when it dies or is erased, it and all of its mods are erased. See rules 410.4b, 803.
 Example: A unit carrying Ephemeral Skywalker as an augment dies; both cards are erased and neither reaches the bin.
720.7a If a modded card leaves play without dying or being erased, for example when it is returned to a hand, its mods are put into the bin and the card goes on alone. See rules 410.4, 410.4a.
title: CR 720.7–720.7a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
(continues 720.7: As long as a card is modded, it has {Unstable}: when it dies or is erased, it and all of its mods are erased.)
720.7b When a modded unit is cached, its mods do not follow it into the cache; they go to the bin. See rule 403.7.
720.7c A token mod has no card of its own. It never enters a bin: however its host leaves play, the token mod is erased, and it is not recorded on the erased pile (rule 407.3a). See rules 410.4c, 407.3a.
 Example: A unit carrying a Wraith token as an augment is recalled, cached or killed. Whichever way it leaves, the Wraith goes to no bin, is not trashed and is not recorded on the erased pile: it is erased.
720.7d The {Unstable} that a mod gives goes with the mod. A unit stops having {Unstable} for this reason when its last mod leaves it, and a unit a mod is moved onto has it from then on. See rule 720.10.
 Example: Rotbeast moves its host's other augments onto an enemy; the enemy becomes Unstable and the augment's static goes with it.
title: CR 720.7b–720.7d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
(continues 720.7: As long as a card is modded, it has {Unstable}: when it dies or is erased, it and all of its mods are erased.)
720.7e A copy of a modded unit (Borrower of Forms) is not itself modded and does not have {Unstable} for that reason. A mod applied to the copy afterwards makes it {Unstable} in the ordinary way. See rule 710.
 Example: A Borrower of Forms that has resolved becomes Unstable when a mod is attached to it.
title: CR 720.7e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.8 When a host is recalled or cached and its nontoken mods are left in a bin, each of those mods is trashed, and the host's controller is the player who trashes it. See rule 405.4.
720.8a A nontoken mod erased together with its {Unstable} host is not trashed. The host's single trash counts for the whole unit. See rule 405.4.
title: CR 720.8–720.8a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.9 An effect or a cost can erase a mod off a host that stays in play. The mod card goes to the erased pile of the mod's controller. The host stays in play, and can die if losing the mod leaves it unable to survive. See rules 407.2, 407.2a.
 Example: Return to Nature negates everything on the stack and erases all mods in the region.
 Example: A mod on a stolen unit is erased off it; it goes to the erased pile of the player who stole the unit, not its owner's.
 Example: Return to Nature erases the mods on a stolen unit. Each goes to the erased pile of the player who stole the unit, its mods' controller.
720.9a A token mod erased off a host that stays in play is not recorded on the erased pile either, because a token is not a card (rule 407.3). See rule 720.7c.
 Example: A Wraith token mod erased off a host that stays in play, as the payment of a cost, is not filed on the erased pile.
 Example: Return to Nature erases a Wraith token mod with the other mods in the region. The Wraith is not recorded on the erased pile.
title: CR 720.9–720.9a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.10 An effect can move a mod from one host to another (Reconfigure, Rotbeast). Moving a mod is not a zone change: the mod never leaves play, and nothing despawns. See rules 410.1b, 721.5.
 Example: Reconfigure moves Bubb and its Growing Plague onto a Robot; Growing Plague's "when I despawn" does not trigger.
title: CR 720.10

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
(continues 720.10: An effect can move a mod from one host to another (Reconfigure, Rotbeast). Moving a mod is not a zone change: the mod never leaves play, and nothing despawns.)
720.10a A moved mod is controlled by its new host's controller. See rule 720.6a.
 Example: Rotbeast moves augments onto an enemy unit; the enemy now controls them, along with their text.
title: CR 720.10a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
(continues 720.10: An effect can move a mod from one host to another (Reconfigure, Rotbeast). Moving a mod is not a zone change: the mod never leaves play, and nothing despawns.)
720.10b Moving a mod does not refresh it. A once-per-turn ability on the mod that was already used this turn stays used on the new host. See rule 109.9e.
 Example: A Graxxlid used this turn and moved by Reconfigure cannot be used again this turn.
title: CR 720.10b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
(continues 720.10: An effect can move a mod from one host to another (Reconfigure, Rotbeast). Moving a mod is not a zone change: the mod never leaves play, and nothing despawns.)
720.10c Moving a mod is not applying it. An ability that triggers when a mod is applied does not trigger when a mod is moved, unless the moving effect says the mods are augmented (721.5a). See rule 721.5a.
 Example: Rotbeast moves its Curio Drifter augment onto an enemy Perpetual Construct, which makes no unit.
title: CR 720.10c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.11 A mod's effects take their timestamp from when the mod was applied. A mod applied after an effect that removes attributes and abilities on the same layer (Monke) still gives its attribute and ability. See rules 709, 113.2.
 Example: A Virus applied after Monke's effect began still gives its attribute.
title: CR 720.11

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 720. Modifications, General
720.12 An ability that triggers when a mod is applied to its unit triggers once for each mod applied. See rule 721.5a.
 Example: Perpetual Construct makes an X/X for an applied mod, X the mod's cost.
 Example: Reconfigure moves three mods onto Perpetual Construct: three triggers, a 1/1, a 3/3 and a 4/4.
title: CR 720.12

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
721.1 Augment is a modification. An augment adds the text that follows its augment symbol to the card it is applied to. See rule 208.
 Example: Aetherflux Golem, a 1/1 whose augment text is "I gain +2/+2", gives its host +2/+2.
721.1a An augment symbol at the start of a paragraph in the text box gives the host that whole paragraph. See rule 208.2.
 Example: Growing Plague applied as an augment gives its host "When I despawn, each other player draws two cards."
721.1b An augment symbol on the type line gives the host the attributes on that type line. It gives no stats. See rule 208.3.
 Example: Bubb ([Augment] {Unaware}) gives its host Unaware, and not its 5/6.
title: CR 721.1–721.1b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
(continues 721.1: Augment is a modification. An augment adds the text that follows its augment symbol to the card it is applied to.)
721.1c On a host, only the augment's own augment text works. The rest of the augment card's text, including body text printed outside the augment paragraph and attributes printed before a text-box augment symbol, does nothing for the host. See rule 208.1.
 Example: Infernal Wispweaver played as a unit gives your wisps +2/+1. Applied as an augment, it gives its host only "At the end of turn, create a wisp"; the +2/+1 for your wisps, printed outside the augment paragraph, does nothing.
 Example: Smouldering Inferno has {Piercing} on its type line and "[Augment] After combat, sacrifice me" in its text box. Applied as a Virus to an attacking Rune Channeler, it does not give the Channeler Piercing, and after combat the Channeler sacrifices itself.
title: CR 721.1c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
(continues 721.1: Augment is a modification. An augment adds the text that follows its augment symbol to the card it is applied to.)
721.1d A card that is played normally reads its whole text, its augment text included. See rules 305.4, 109.7.
title: CR 721.1d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
(continues 721.1: Augment is a modification. An augment adds the text that follows its augment symbol to the card it is applied to.)
721.1e Augment text keeps its kind on the host. A static ability given by an augment ("I gain +2/+2") is a continuous effect on the host for as long as the mod is attached; it is not a triggered ability and does not use the stack. See rule 707.
721.1f Augment text that triggers on the host's own departure ("When I despawn") triggers whichever way the host leaves play: when it dies, is recalled or is cached. See rule 410.
title: CR 721.1e–721.1f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
721.2 A card can be applied as an augment if it prints the augment symbol, in its text box or on its type line, whether or not its augment text does anything. See rule 208.4.
 Example: Chitin Shredder prints the augment symbol only on its type line and has no text box, and it can be applied as an augment.
title: CR 721.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
721.3 To apply an augment, the player takes these steps in order: (1) meets the augment's affinity requirement; (2) pays its mana cost; (3) selects a target to apply it onto; (4) places the augment card beneath the target, with its text box visible beneath the target's. See rules 720.4, 110.10.
title: CR 721.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
721.4 During deployment a player can augment only their own units. An opponent's unit can be augmented only with a Virus during battle (723.2), or under a card that lets cards be augmented as if they were Viruses (723.5). See rules 723.2, 723.5.
 Example: In deployment Curio Drifter can augment your own unit but not an opponent unit; in battle Aetherflux Golem (a Virus) can augment the attacking enemy.
721.4a During deployment a player may also augment a spell token they have in play, with any augment, not only a Virus. During a battle, a Virus may also be applied to a spell token in play in the battle's region, either player's (723.2). The token gains only the augment's attributes. See rules 305.6, 507.2b.
 Example: An augmented token deals {Powerful} damage when cast.
 Example: In battle a Virus is offered onto either player's spell token in play in the battle region.
title: CR 721.4–721.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
(continues 721.4: During deployment a player can augment only their own units. An opponent's unit can be augmented only with a Virus during battle (723.2), or under a card that lets cards be augmented as if they were Viruses (723.5).)
721.4b An augment applied to a spell, on the stack (723.4) or as it is played through Modular (724), gives the spell only its type-line attributes. Augment text and static abilities give a spell nothing, but applying such an augment is still legal. See rules 723.4, 724.4.
 Example: An augment-text mod applied to Spellbind is accepted and does nothing.
title: CR 721.4b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
721.5 Reconfigure augments a unit and all of its mods onto another unit. Its first target must have the augment symbol. See rule 720.10.
721.5a Each mod Reconfigure moves is applied to the new host. An ability that triggers when a mod is applied to that unit triggers once for each moved mod. See rule 720.12.
 Example: Bubb with two mods reconfigured onto Perpetual Construct makes three tokens, one per mod applied.
721.5b A unit that has become a copy of a card with the augment symbol does not have that symbol, so it cannot be Reconfigure's first target. See rules 208.5, 710.
 Example: A Borrower of Forms that copied an augment unit cannot be chosen as Reconfigure's first target.
title: CR 721.5–721.5b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 721. Augment
721.6 An effect can augment a card onto a unit when it resolves. When the effect augments a token ("Augment a Wraith onto an ally"), the token is created directly as a mod of that unit. See rule 304.
 Example: An augmented Wraith gives its host its first line: at the start of deployment the host puts a -1/-1 counter on an ally, here itself, its only ally, so a 4/4 host becomes 3/3.
title: CR 721.6

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
722.1 Graft is a modification that combines several effects under a single cause. It is marked by the graft symbol, written [Switch] (unbounded) or [Switch1] (bounded) in the card text this document quotes. See rule 205.4.
 Example: Flame Juggle grafted onto Oracle of the Flame: one sacrifice of the Oracle creates its own Fireball 1 and Flame Juggle's three Fireball 1s.
722.1a A graft card's ability has a cause, before the graft symbol, and an effect, after it. Oracle of the Flame's cause is "Sacrifice me" and its effect is "Create a Fireball 1". See rule 205.4.
722.1b When a card is grafted, only what follows its graft symbol is added to the host. Everything printed before the symbol, its cost and cause included, is ignored. See rule 205.4.
 Example: A grafted Omniwield Evoker adds "Put a +1/+1 counter on me" to the host's ability; its own cost of three, printed before the graft symbol, is not paid.
722.1c A graft card still works as written when it is played normally. A spell or spell unit with a graft symbol resolves normally when it is played, and can later be grafted from the bin. See rules 305.5, 305.4.
 Example: Once Leaping Lillik has died, it can be grafted from the bin.
title: CR 722.1–722.1c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
722.2 Both cards must have the graft symbol. The host must be a unit in play with a graft cause of its own.
title: CR 722.2

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
722.3 Applying a graft follows the same cost and timing as an augment: from the hand or the bin, during deployment, paying the card's cost and meeting its affinity. See rules 720.4, 720.5.
722.3a A graft is applied only in deployment, never in the haste step or in battle, even when the graft card has Haste. The exceptions are a card that allows mods in the haste step, such as Slurpr (504.8a), and a Modular card, to which a graft card may be applied as the Modular card is played, in battle too (724). See rules 504.8a, 507.2a, 724, 720.2b.
 Example: With Slurpr in play, a graft can be applied during the haste step.
722.3b A card that lets cards be augmented in battle as if they were Viruses (Rook) does not let a card be grafted in battle. See rule 723.5.
 Example: With Rook in play, Curio Drifter is offered as an augment in battle, but Flame Juggle is not offered as a graft.
722.3c Applying a graft targets the host. An ability that triggers when its unit becomes targeted (Mohruung) triggers first, before the graft is attached. See rules 110.10, 110.11.
 Example: Grafting onto Mohruung targets it, so it makes its Crystal.
722.3d A player applying a new graft may insert it at any position below the host's own card, but may not re-order the grafts already applied.
 Example: A new graft slides between two already applied, whose order stays fixed.
title: CR 722.3–722.3d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
722.4 Each grafted effect is added to the cause of the host's own card. The host's ability then reads "cause: effect 1 AND effect 2 AND effect 3 …", in the order the grafts sit.
 Example: Accelerated Germination grafted onto Oracle of the Flame reads "Sacrifice me: Create a Fireball 1 AND (once per turn) create two 1/1 units."
 Example: An Ancient One activating an adjacent ally's grafted cause runs the graft too.
722.4a The host's own graft cause decides when the whole composite triggers or can be activated.
722.4b The composite is a single ability. It goes on the stack as one item, resolves all at once, and a single negation stops all of it. See rule 703.
722.4c The composite resolves from top to bottom: the host's own effect first, then each graft in the order it sits. See rule 704.
 Example: On a Mohruung host, Overbloom grafted above Spewing Mushroom makes a Poison 8; grafted below it, a Poison 1.
722.4d Every target of the composite is declared when it is put on the stack. A part that requires a target must take one if any is legal, even one of the player's own units. See rules 110, 702.8b.
 Example: Plodding Pebble, with Leaping Lillik ("Delete target unit") grafted under it, attacks into an empty region and is hit by a Fireball 1. As its trigger goes on the stack, the delete must take a target: with no enemy unit there, Plodding Pebble itself is legal, and the player cannot choose no target.
722.4e A triggered composite with a part that requires a target, when that part has no legal target, is not put on the stack at all. Its untargeted parts do not happen either. See rule 702.8b.
 Example: Megadeath with Resurrect grafted attacks with no cheap unit in the bin: no Poison 5 either.
 Example: The same composite is never put on the stack at all.
title: CR 722.4–722.4e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
(continues 722.4: Each grafted effect is added to the cause of the host's own card. The host's ability then reads "cause: effect 1 AND effect 2 AND effect 3 …", in the order the grafts sit.)
722.4f A composite fizzles when it has lost all of its targets, and then none of it happens, its untargeted parts included. While at least one target remains, every part resolves as far as it can. Only a composite that was never targeted cannot fizzle: one with no part that calls for a target, or one whose only target was optional ("up to one") and none was chosen (see rule 704.6g). See rule 704.
 Example: Spewing Mushroom carries Biotoxicity and Technological Superiority as grafts. It attacks, and its composite trigger targets Spewing Mushroom, the only target it declares. The opponent deletes the Mushroom with Leaping Lillik in response: the composite fizzles, and Biotoxicity's untargeted Poisons are not created either.
title: CR 722.4f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
(continues 722.4: Each grafted effect is added to the cause of the host's own card. The host's ability then reads "cause: effect 1 AND effect 2 AND effect 3 …", in the order the grafts sit.)
722.4g A graft composite is a triggered or activated ability like any other. A modifier to the cost of activating or triggering abilities (Crevice Lurker) applies to it. See rule 111.10f.
title: CR 722.4g

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
722.5 A graft is either unbounded ([Switch]) or bounded ([Switch1]). An unbounded graft can trigger any number of times; a bounded graft can trigger only once per turn. See rule 109.9.
 Example: Plodding Pebble's bounded graft gives one counter per turn.
722.5a Under an unbounded cause, the composite can fire any number of times, but each bounded graft in it is included only the first time in a turn. See rule 109.9i.
722.5b Under a bounded cause, the whole composite fires only once per turn, its unbounded grafts included. See rule 109.9h.
722.5c Each grafted card has its own use. Two copies of the same bounded graft on one host each have one use. A unit that has a grafted cause through Ancient One has a use of its own of each bounded graft in it, apart from the host's (rule 722.8). See rule 109.9k.
 Example: An Ancient One borrowing a grafted triggered cause runs the graft with its own use.
722.5d A unit that leaves play and comes back is a new object, so its bounded graft can be used again the same turn. See rule 410.
 Example: A recalled and replayed Engorged Caudex draws from its bounded graft again the same turn.
title: CR 722.5–722.5d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
722.6 A graft printed "{graft} [cost]: effect" adds a cost to the composite. That cost must be paid; it cannot be declined. See rule 111.15.
 Example: A grafted Immolate's sacrifice is paid as the composite goes on the stack, and the player cannot decline it.
722.6a If a grafted cost cannot be paid, the whole composite stays off the stack: the host's own effect and every other graft with it. See rule 111.15.
722.6b The cost is paid as the composite goes on the stack. No player can respond to the payment, and units the composite itself would create cannot pay it. See rule 111.
title: CR 722.6–722.6b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
722.7 Some graft causes trigger several copies of the graft ability as one single trigger: Lost Guardian two, Amphivore and Witness of the Crossing three. The copies are one effect on the stack. See rule 111.14.
 Example: Amphivore's combat damage to an opponent triggers its grafts three times, in one trigger.
 Example: Lost Guardian's after-combat trigger runs each graft twice as one trigger.
722.7a The copies run top to bottom, then top to bottom again, once for each copy. See rule 722.4c.
 Example: Amphivore with Plodding Pebble and Bellowing Boulder goes counter, damage, counter, damage, counter, damage.
722.7b A bounded graft under a multiplier is repeated too. See rule 109.9j.
 Example: Amphivore triples a bounded "Create three" graft into nine Fireballs.
title: CR 722.7–722.7b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
(continues 722.7: Some graft causes trigger several copies of the graft ability as one single trigger: Lost Guardian two, Amphivore and Witness of the Crossing three. The copies are one effect on the stack.)
722.7c Each copy of a targeted graft chooses its targets separately. See rule 110.
title: CR 722.7c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
(continues 722.7: Some graft causes trigger several copies of the graft ability as one single trigger: Lost Guardian two, Amphivore and Witness of the Crossing three. The copies are one effect on the stack.)
722.7d A cost in a repeated graft is paid once for each copy. If the multiplied cost cannot be paid in full, none of it is paid, and the composite stays off the stack (722.6a). See rules 111.14, 722.6a.
 Example: With one card in hand, a doubled [Discard a card] cannot be paid: nothing is paid and nothing happens.
722.7e A copy that cannot do part of its effect does the rest. Ralph grafted under a multiplier gives the host away and makes three 1/1s on the first pass only; the later passes cannot give it away, and the rest of the composite still runs every time. See rule 101.
 Example: Amphivore with Ralph grafted: the first pass gives the host away and makes three 1/1s, the later passes give nothing, and the other graft runs three times.
title: CR 722.7d–722.7e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 722. Graft
722.8 A unit that has become a copy of a grafted unit runs the whole copied composite. More grafts may be added to it, but only below the copied grafts. A unit that has the abilities of a grafted unit (Ancient One, rule 710.7) likewise has the whole composite, its grafts included, and each bounded graft in it has a use of its own on that unit. See rule 710.
 Example: A Borrower that copied a Bellowing Boulder with Flame Juggle grafted runs the whole copied composite.
 Example: A graft added to that Borrower resolves below the copied grafts.
 Example: An Ancient One borrowing a grafted triggered cause runs the graft too, with its own use.
 Example: Amphivore with Astral Painseeker grafted, Ancient One behind it, Bloodwind Revenant beside: the designer's board.
title: CR 722.8

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
723.1 Virus is a timing icon. A Virus card can be applied as an augment from the hand during battle, as well as being played and augmented normally during deployment. See rule 207.5.
 Example: Aetherflux Golem augments the attacker from hand during battle; in deployment it may be played as a unit or augmented.
723.1a A Virus applied in battle is an augment: it gives its host its augment text or its type-line attributes (721.1), and an ability that triggers when a player applies an augment triggers on it. See rule 721.1.
 Example: Morphic Mentor's controller applies an augment in battle and the Mentor gets +2/+2; an enemy's augment does not count.
723.1b Virus changes when a card may be augmented, not what it may be augmented onto. In deployment a Virus is applied like any other augment. See rule 721.4.
 Example: In deployment Aetherflux Golem, a Virus, can augment your own unit but not an opponent unit.
title: CR 723.1–723.1b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
723.2 During a battle, a player who has priority may apply a Virus from their hand onto any unit, or any spell token in play, in the battle's region, their own or an opponent's. See rule 703.
 Example: A player applies Smouldering Inferno from hand to the opponent's attacker; the Virus goes on the stack and the host is modded when it resolves.
 Example: In battle a Virus is offered onto a spell token in play in the battle region, the player's own or the opponent's.
723.2a A Virus may also be applied in battle from the cache, while a permission to use it is live, at the cache's price (720.4b). With no live permission it cannot. See rules 403.3b, 720.4b.
 Example: A glimpsed Virus in the cache goes onto an enemy unit in battle, ignoring affinity.
723.2b A Virus in a bin cannot be applied during battle by its Virus ability. From the bin it can be applied as an ordinary mod during deployment, and outside deployment only where another card opens a window: augmenting in battle under a card such as Rook (723.5), applying to a Modular card as it is played (724), or applying in the haste step under a card such as Slurpr (504.8a). See rules 405.8a, 723.5, 724, 504.8a, 720.2b.
 Example: Bumblecrab, a Virus, is offered from the hand in battle but not from the bin; in deployment it is offered from the bin.
 Example: With a Rook in the battle's region, a card is augmented out of the bin during battle.
723.2c A Virus applied to an opponent's unit is controlled by that opponent, with its ability (720.6a). A Virus whose text works against its host's controller therefore works against the opponent. See rule 720.6a.
 Example: Smouldering Inferno augmented onto an opposing unit forces it to sacrifice itself after combat.
title: CR 723.2–723.2c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
723.3 Applying a Virus in battle uses the stack. The Virus goes on the stack as an effect that targets its host, and it can be responded to, redirected and negated. See rules 110.10a, 703.
 Example: A Virus being applied to Graxxlid is an effect targeting Graxxlid, which Graxxlid can negate.
723.3a A Virus that is negated, or whose target has become invalid, is put into the bin and cannot be used as a Virus again. See rules 704.4a, 704.6f.
 Example: A Virus aimed at a spell on the stack: the spell leaves the stack first, so the Virus fizzles and goes to the bin.
723.3b A Virus being applied is not a spell. An effect that negates spells, or counts the spells played, does not see it. See rule 700.1b.
 Example: Origon does not negate a Virus applied in battle, and its first-spell count is untouched.
title: CR 723.3–723.3b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
723.4 During battle a Virus may be augmented onto a spell on the stack, the player's own or an opponent's. The spell gains only the Virus's attributes (721.4b). See rule 721.4b.
 Example: Chitin Shredder on Arc Lightning doubles its damage.
723.4a Spells, spell units and spell tokens on the stack are legal hosts for a Virus. See rule 723.4e.
title: CR 723.4–723.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
(continues 723.4: During battle a Virus may be augmented onto a spell on the stack, the player's own or an opponent's. The spell gains only the Virus's attributes (721.4b).)
723.4b A spell carrying a Virus is modded, so it is {Unstable}: the spell and the Virus are erased instead of going to a bin, whether the spell resolves, fizzles or is negated. See rule 704.2c.
title: CR 723.4b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
(continues 723.4: During battle a Virus may be augmented onto a spell on the stack, the player's own or an opponent's. The spell gains only the Virus's attributes (721.4b).)
723.4c A spell unit carrying a Virus is not erased when it resolves. It enters play with the Virus attached as an augment, and so has {Unstable}. See rule 303.
723.4d A spell that has begun to resolve cannot have a Virus applied to it. See rule 703.6.
723.4e Triggered and activated abilities, Viruses, units being cast and Ambushes on the stack are not legal hosts for a Virus. See rule 723.4a.
title: CR 723.4c–723.4e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
723.5 A card can let other cards be augmented during battle as if they were Viruses. Rook: "You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus]." See rule 720.2b.
 Example: Applying a non-Virus augment from hand during battle is not allowed without Rook, and is with it.
title: CR 723.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
(continues 723.5: A card can let other cards be augmented during battle as if they were Viruses. Rook: "You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus].")
723.5a Such a card gives the augmented card the Virus ability itself, so the augment may go onto an opponent's unit or onto a spell on the stack. See rule 723.4.
title: CR 723.5a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
(continues 723.5: A card can let other cards be augmented during battle as if they were Viruses. Rook: "You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus].")
723.5b Such a card reaches only the zones it names. Rook names the hand and the bin, so a non-Virus card in the cache cannot be augmented in battle through Rook. See rule 723.2a.
title: CR 723.5b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 723. Virus
(continues 723.5: A card can let other cards be augmented during battle as if they were Viruses. Rook: "You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus].")
723.5c Such a permission belongs to the controller of the card that grants it (the host's controller, when it is a mod), and works only in that card's region. See rule 720.6b.
title: CR 723.5c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 724. Modular
724.1 Modular is an attribute. A player may apply mods from their hand and/or bin to a Modular card as it is played, paying their costs. See rule 802.26.
724.1a Spellbind is the only card that prints Modular.
title: CR 724.1–724.1a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 724. Modular
724.2 Any card in the player's hand or bin whose cost they can pay may be applied to a Modular card: a graft, an augment, a Virus, or a card that can do nothing on a spell.
724.2a A mod that does nothing on a spell is still a legal choice, and its cost is still paid. See rule 721.4b.
 Example: Sparkwraith's augment text applied to Spellbind is accepted and does nothing.
title: CR 724.2–724.2a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 724. Modular
(continues 724.2: Any card in the player's hand or bin whose cost they can pay may be applied to a Modular card: a graft, an augment, a Virus, or a card that can do nothing on a spell.)
724.2b Each mod's cost is paid as it is applied, while the Modular card is cast. Applying it is not playing it. See rule 720.3.
title: CR 724.2b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 724. Modular
724.3 The mods are chosen and paid for while the Modular card is being cast, before it reaches the stack, and they go on the stack with it. The caster may apply none. See rule 702.3b.
title: CR 724.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 724. Modular
724.4 A graft applied to a Modular spell adds its effect to the spell's ability as an extra part. See rule 722.4.
 Example: A player casts Spellbind and applies Primordial Coalescence from their bin to it. When Spellbind resolves, Primordial Coalescence's graft effect happens too: three Wraiths, and its 2 Rot on top of Spellbind's one.
724.4a A type-line augment applied to a Modular spell gives its attributes to the spell's effect. See rule 721.4b.
 Example: {Powerful} turns a Spellbind-carried Twin Flame from 2 damage into 4.
724.4b Augment text and static abilities applied to a Modular spell do nothing, because a spell has no body for them to work on. See rule 721.4b.
 Example: Sparkwraith on Spellbind: a spell played while it rides the stack puts no counter anywhere.
724.4c A grafted cost on a Modular spell's graft part must be paid if it can be. If it cannot, only that part is skipped, and the spell still resolves. See rule 722.6.
 Example: Spellbind carrying a grafted Immolate with no unit to sacrifice: the Immolate part is skipped, and Spellbind still gives its rot.
 Example: Spellbind carrying a grafted Immolate, with a unit to sacrifice: the cost is paid, the unit is sacrificed and a card is drawn. Declining is not offered.
title: CR 724.4–724.4c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 724. Modular
724.5 A Modular card with any mod applied is modded, so it has {Unstable}: it and all of its mods are erased instead of going to a bin, whether it resolves, fizzles or is negated. See rules 720.7, 723.4b.
 Example: A graft card replayed from the bin by Spellbind is erased, so it cannot be used that way twice.
title: CR 724.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects › 724. Modular
(continues 724.5: A Modular card with any mod applied is modded, so it has {Unstable}: it and all of its mods are erased instead of going to a bin, whether it resolves, fizzles or is negated.)
724.5a A Modular card with no mod applied does not have {Unstable}, and goes to the bin like any other spell.
title: CR 724.5a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.1 Card text uses some verbs with a fixed game meaning: these are keyword actions, defined in this section. Where a card prints reminder text for a keyword action, the printed reminder states its meaning, and it wins over any paraphrase of it. See rules 802, 803.
title: CR 801.1

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.2 A card is trashed when it enters a bin from any zone except the stack. See rule 405.4.
 Example: A card discarded from a hand enters a bin from the hand, so it is trashed.
 Example: A card that leaves a cache for a bin is trashed.
801.2a Discarding a card, sacrificing it, milling it and a card dying into a bin are all ways of trashing it. See rules 801.3, 801.4, 801.5.
801.2b A card that goes to a bin from the stack is not trashed, whether it resolved, was negated or failed to resolve. A card played for free during another effect's resolution and then put into the bin counts as coming from the stack. See rules 405.4a, 704.2a.
 Example: A spell Tides of the Cosmos plays for free off the deck goes to the bin afterwards and is not trashed.
801.2c Erasing a card is not trashing it: an erased card never enters a bin. See rules 407.1c, 801.6.
 Example: Banishment erases a unit: no death and no trash happen.
801.2d A token is never trashed, because only a card can be trashed. A unit token that dies still enters the bin and still dies, but its trip through the bin is not a trash: no "when I am trashed" ability triggers for it, its own included. See rules 108.2e, 304.10a.
 Example: A token copy of Dropslime that dies does not trigger its own "When I am trashed".
801.2e The player whose bin the card enters is the player who trashes it. A unit that dies goes to its controller's bin, so its controller trashes it; when an effect sends the card to another player's bin, that player trashes it. See rules 405.3, 711.
 Example: A stolen unit that dies goes to the bin of the player who controls it, and that player trashes it.
 Example: Pull Under deletes an enemy unit and puts it into the caster's bin: the caster trashes it.
801.2f When a modded unit is recalled or cached, each nontoken mod it carried is left behind in a bin and is trashed there. The host's controller trashes it, not the mod's owner. See rules 410.4, 403.7.
801.2g A nontoken mod that is erased together with its {Unstable} host is not trashed. The host's departure is the whole unit's; the mod has no trash of its own. See rules 405.4, 720.
title: CR 801.2–801.2g

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.2: A card is trashed when it enters a bin from any zone except the stack.)
801.2h An {Unstable} card that dies in play is still trashed: trashing is part of its death, not something entering a bin causes, and Unstable changes where the card goes, not its death (rule 803.8i). It does not stay in a bin: it is erased, and ends on the erased pile. An {Unstable} card that goes to a bin from an inactive zone (a hand, the deck or a cache) enters the bin and is trashed. See rules 405.5, 400, 803.
 Example: Aberrant Statweaver (printed {Unstable}) discarded from a hand goes to the bin and is trashed: the hand is inactive.
801.2i An effect that counts cards trashed counts only cards. A token dying never adds to the count.
 Example: Dropslime deals damage equal to the cards trashed this battle, and the tokens that died in it do not count.
title: CR 801.2h–801.2i

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.3 To discard a card is to put it from a hand into the bin. A discarded card is trashed. Discarding is not playing the card, and a cached card cannot be discarded. See rules 402.5, 403.4, 801.2.
title: CR 801.3

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.4 To sacrifice a unit is for a player to choose a unit they control and put it into their bin. A sacrificed unit dies. See rules 111.3, 111.8.
 Example: Immolate sacrifices a unit to draw a card.
801.4a A player can sacrifice only something they control. An effect may make an opponent sacrifice something; that opponent sacrifices one of their own units and chooses which.
 Example: General Smof: after combat each present player sacrifices a unit of their own choice.
801.4b A player can sacrifice only a unit in the region where the effect or cost happens, never one of their units in another region. See rules 601.1e, 111.3.
 Example: Ghord's sacrifice makes each opponent in Ghord's region sacrifice a unit there, and reaches no other region.
801.4c A player told to sacrifice a unit who has no unit in the region sacrifices nothing. See rule 101.5.
 Example: Cull's "each player sacrifices a unit" with nobody holding a unit in the region kills nothing.
title: CR 801.4–801.4c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.5 To delete a unit is one way for it to die: the unit dies, and it is removed from play into the bin. Abilities that trigger when a unit dies, its own "When I die" included, trigger. Unless the effect names another bin, it goes to the bin a dying unit would go to. See rules 301.5, 405.2, 405.3.
 Example: Throw off a Cliff deletes a unit with 4 or more defense: it goes to the bin, as a death.
801.5a An effect that deletes a unit and names where it goes overrides the usual bin. Pull Under puts the deleted unit and all of its mods into its caster's bin, where they stay. See rule 801.2e.
title: CR 801.5–801.5a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.6 To erase a card is to take it out of the game: it goes to the erased pile. When card text says "erase", the erased pile is where the card goes. See rules 407.1, 407.2, 410.2.
 Example: Celestial Purge erases its target unit: it goes to no bin.
801.6a Erasing a unit is neither a death nor a trash. It is a despawn. See rules 407.1c, 410.2.
 Example: Banishment erases a unit: it does not die and is not trashed, but it does despawn.
title: CR 801.6–801.6a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.7 To recall a card is to put it into a hand. Printed recalls take a card from play, from a bin, from the stack or from a cache. See rules 402.4, 410.2.
 Example: Vaporweave Eidolon recalls itself from play to its controller's hand, at no cost.
 Example: Eldritch Reclaimer recalls a unit from its controller's bin to their hand.
 Example: Prismatic Observer recalls an enemy's cached card to its owner's hand.
title: CR 801.7

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.7: To recall a card is to put it into a hand. Printed recalls take a card from play, from a bin, from the stack or from a cache.)
801.7a A unit recalled from play goes to the hand of the player who controls it, not necessarily its owner, unless the effect names another hand. Recalling does not change who owns the card. See rules 102, 711.
 Example: A stolen unit that is recalled goes to the thief's hand, not its owner's.
 Example: Cosmic Reversal recalls a stolen spell unit to the hand of the player who controls it.
title: CR 801.7a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.7: To recall a card is to put it into a hand. Printed recalls take a card from play, from a bin, from the stack or from a cache.)
801.7b A recalled {Unstable} unit goes to the hand as a card. {Unstable} changes only a move into a bin, so a recall is not affected by it. See rules 803, 410.4.
801.7c Recalling a card from a bin moves it from that bin to its player's hand. "Recall target unit in your bin" can reach only a card in that player's own bin. See rule 405.7.
 Example: Delver of Mysteries recalls a chosen spell from its controller's bin.
 Example: Eldritch Reclaimer, cast with both players in the battle, can pick a unit in its caster's own bin, never one in the opponent's bin.
801.7d Recalling a spell effect on the stack negates it and puts the card into its controller's hand. A recalled spell token enters its controller's hand and is then erased. See rules 704.4, 410.5b.
 Example: Cosmic Reversal recalls the other spell effects on the stack to their controllers' hands.
 Example: Dream Lapse recalls a cast Fireball token: it enters its controller's hand, so Rider of the Tides grows, and then it is erased.
801.7e When an effect tells a player to recall a unit and they have none to recall, the recall does nothing, but the rest of the effect still happens unless it depends on the recall ("If you do"). See rule 101.5.
 Example: Recall ("Each player recalls a unit and loses 2 life"): a player with no unit to recall still loses 2 life.
 Example: Shoreline Specter: if the recall is declined, the life drain that follows "If you do" does not happen.
title: CR 801.7b–801.7e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.8 To cache a card is to put it into a player's cache. A unit cached from play goes to its controller's cache unless the effect names another, and its mods go to the bin. See rules 403.1, 403.7, 410.5c.
 Example: A stolen unit that is cached goes to the thief's cache.
 Example: Grob caches a stolen unit into its controller's cache, as its text says.
801.8a Caching a card does not by itself let anyone use it. A cached card can be played or used as a mod only while a permission on it is live: a glimpse that cached it this turn, a fulfilled prophecy, or the text of the effect that cached it. See rules 403.3, 403.3a, 801.9.
 Example: Murkdrop Distiller caches a trashed card; its own text then lets its controller play it until end of turn.
title: CR 801.8–801.8a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.9 Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest. See rules 403, 408.2a.
 Example: Oracle of Foretelling's Glimpse 5 caches one of the five revealed cards.
title: CR 801.9

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.9: Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest.)
801.9a The player who glimpses chooses which of the revealed cards to cache.
 Example: In a Glimpse 3, choosing the last revealed card caches it and recycles the two above it.
title: CR 801.9a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.9: Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest.)
801.9b Glimpse 1 reveals the top card of the deck and caches it. There is no choice to make and nothing to recycle.
801.9c "Glimpse 1, X times" is X separate glimpses of one card each, not one Glimpse X.
 Example: Glook discards X cards when activated and then glimpses 1, X times.
801.9d A glimpse reveals from the glimpser's own deck. When an effect makes another player glimpse ("Its controller Glimpses 3"), that player reveals from their own deck, not from the deck of the player who controls the effect. In live draft every player's deck is the one shared deck. See rules 401, 902.
 Example: Celestial Purge cast by one player erases an enemy unit; that unit's controller glimpses, chooses the card to cache and caches it in their own cache.
 Example: In constructed, a player who glimpses reveals the top of their own deck, caches from it and recycles the rest into their own pile; the other player's deck is untouched.
801.9e Until end of turn, the glimpser may play the cached card as if it were in their hand, ignoring affinity. See rules 403.3a, 403.3b.
 Example: A card with affinity its glimpser cannot meet can be played from the cache, for its mana only.
title: CR 801.9b–801.9e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.9: Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest.)
801.9f A card played under a glimpse permission still costs its mana, and still obeys its printed timing. Only the affinity requirement is waived. See rules 403.3c, 403.3d.
 Example: A glimpsed {Battle} card cannot be played in deployment.
title: CR 801.9f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.9: Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest.)
801.9g The same permission lets the glimpser apply the cached card as a mod, on the same terms (its mana, ignoring affinity): an augment or graft during deployment, and a {Virus} during battle. See rules 403.3b, 721, 722, 723.
 Example: A glimpsed {Virus} in the cache goes onto an enemy unit in battle.
title: CR 801.9g

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.9: Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest.)
801.9h While the permission is live, a glimpsed card with a prophecy banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache, in the same window and for the same cost as from the hand. Doing so uses up the glimpse permission. See rules 403.8, 801.14, 803.
title: CR 801.9h

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.9: Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest.)
801.9i The permission ends at end of turn. The card stays in the cache, and it can no longer be played, prophesied or applied as a mod there. See rule 403.5.
 Example: Premonition's permission dies with the turn; the card stays cached.
title: CR 801.9i

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.10 To recycle a card is to put it on the bottom of the deck. A recycled card goes past the deck's mark into the recycle pile. See rules 408.1, 408.2, 106.6.
 Example: Tides of the Cosmos recycles the revealed cards it did not play.
title: CR 801.10

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.11 When two units fight, each deals damage equal to its power to the other. See rule 112.
 Example: The spell Battle makes two target units fight: each deals damage equal to its power to the other.
801.11a Each fighting unit is the source of the damage it deals, with its own current attributes. Attributes the fight spell itself has do not apply to that damage. See rules 112.6, 802.
 Example: A fighter that gained {Powerful} deals double damage.
 Example: A {Powerful} virus on the Fight spell does not double either fighter's damage.
801.11b Damage dealt in a fight is dealt by the units, not by the spell or ability that made them fight. Abilities that look for damage dealt by a spell effect do not see it. See rule 112.6.
 Example: Squish's damage is dealt by the unit, so Ember of Life does not trigger; Fight and Battle work the same way.
 Example: Fight makes a 3-power unit deal 3 damage, and Ember of Life does not trigger; a spell dealing damage in the same setup does trigger it.
801.11c A fight needs both of its units. If one of them is gone when the fight would happen, nothing happens: the remaining unit deals and is dealt no damage. The effect does not fizzle. See rules 704.6c, 101.5.
title: CR 801.11–801.11c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.12 Rockfall N means: each player chooses one of their units, and the source of the rockfall deals N damage to each chosen unit. See rule 112.
 Example: A Fast Pile of Rocks dies and rockfalls 4: each player picks one of their own units, and each takes exactly 4.
801.12a Rockfall chooses; it does not target. No targets are declared when it goes on the stack, and an effect that stops targeting cannot stop it. See rule 110.
 Example: Boon of Protection has nothing to negate when a Meteor Shower falls on its unit.
801.12b Each player must choose a living unit of theirs in the region. A player with no unit there chooses none, and takes no part in that rockfall. See rule 601.1b.
title: CR 801.12–801.12b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.13 "Exchange" is printed in four senses, each read from its card: exchanging a unit in play for a unit card in a bin (Hooba-Mon, Necromorph), exchanging control of two units (Organic Exchange), exchanging control of a unit for a spell another player played (Hexbane Shiitake), and exchanging the base stats of two units (Body Swap). See rules 711, 106.8.
 Example: Hexbane Shiitake gives itself away and takes control of an enemy spell.
title: CR 801.13

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
(continues 801.13: "Exchange" is printed in four senses, each read from its card: exchanging a unit in play for a unit card in a bin (Hooba-Mon, Necromorph), exchanging control of two units (Organic Exchange), exchanging control of a unit…)
801.13a When a unit in play is exchanged for a unit card in a bin, the unit leaving play despawns and goes to the bin, where it is trashed, but it does not die. See rules 410.2a, 410.4d, 704.6c.
 Example: Necromorph's exchange fires no death trigger, but the unit despawns and is trashed.
 Example: Hooba-Mon exchanging an unmodded host: the host goes to the bin and stays there.
title: CR 801.13a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 801. Keyword Actions
801.14 To prophesy a card is to pay the cost on its prophecy banner and put it into the cache with its prophecy attached. Prophecy itself is 803. See rules 803, 403.8.
title: CR 801.14

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
802.1 General. Attributes are qualities that a card or a token can have (see rule 204). An attribute applies whenever the card or token has it, in combat or not. Some attributes change how a unit engages in combat; others change the card in other ways (see rule 802.1b). See rule 204.
802.1a Cards with attributes carry reminder text, in italics, to help players remember what each attribute does.
802.1b Attributes are combat attributes or non-combat attributes. Combat attributes are printed in gold. Non-combat attributes, such as Burst and Unstable, are printed in purple and generally have nothing to do with combat. See rules 204, 803.
802.1c Combat attributes are shared by the units in the same column of a formation: while a unit is in a column, it has every combat attribute that any unit in that column has. See rules 603.1a, 602.
 Example: A token attacking in a column behind a Flying unit has Flying too.
802.1d Attributes are not shared with the units to the left or right of a unit. They are shared only within its column. See rule 603.1a.
 Example: A unit attacking in the next column beside a Flying unit does not have Flying.
802.1e A unit has the attributes of its column for everything it does while it is in the column, not only for combat damage. Damage it deals with its abilities has those attributes too. See rule 112.6.
 Example: Lithoghul stands in a battle column with Flzzz, which is Blessed. An ability of Lithoghul deals 3 damage to an enemy unit: Lithoghul has Blessed from its column, so its controller gains 3 life.
 Example: Bellowing Boulder, in a column with a Deadly unit, pings with Deadly.
title: CR 802.1–802.1e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.1: Attributes are qualities that a card or a token can have (see rule 204). An attribute applies whenever the card or token has it, in combat or not. Some attributes change how a unit engages in combat; others change the…)
802.1f Columns exist only during a battle. Outside a battle no unit is in a column, so no attribute is shared. See rules 602, 603.
 Example: Outside battle, a unit standing beside a Blessed unit gains nothing from it.
title: CR 802.1f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.1: Attributes are qualities that a card or a token can have (see rule 204). An attribute applies whenever the card or token has it, in combat or not. Some attributes change how a unit engages in combat; others change the…)
802.1g When a unit leaves a column, the other units in that column immediately lose the attributes it was sharing with them. See rules 603.1a, 608.2b.
 Example: Once the Deadly unit leaves Bellowing Boulder's column, the Boulder's ping is not Deadly.
802.1h Non-combat attributes are not shared in formation. A unit that is Unstable, or has Burst or Modular, does not give that attribute to the other units in its column. See rule 803.
 Example: A modded (and so Unstable) unit does not make its column-mate Unstable.
title: CR 802.1g–802.1h

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.1: Attributes are qualities that a card or a token can have (see rule 204). An attribute applies whenever the card or token has it, in combat or not. Some attributes change how a unit engages in combat; others change the…)
802.1i A card either has an attribute or does not. Having the same attribute from more than one source has no extra effect.
 Example: Two sources granting Inverted to one unit invert its stat changes once, not twice.
title: CR 802.1i

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.1: Attributes are qualities that a card or a token can have (see rule 204). An attribute applies whenever the card or token has it, in combat or not. Some attributes change how a unit engages in combat; others change the…)
802.1j Four attributes change a unit's stats. Tough and Balanced apply in the fourth stat layer, Inverted in the fifth and Unaware in the sixth and last (see rule 206.4). See rules 206.4, 709.
 Example: A 1/4 with Tough, Balanced and Inverted is a -6/0.
 Example: A unit with both Inverted and Unaware is read at its printed stats: Unaware applies last.
title: CR 802.1j

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.1: Attributes are qualities that a card or a token can have (see rule 204). An attribute applies whenever the card or token has it, in combat or not. Some attributes change how a unit engages in combat; others change the…)
802.1k A unit's stats are worked out through all the stat layers before it is checked for death. A unit whose defense would be 0 or less part-way through the calculation, but not at the end of it, does not die. See rules 206.4, 713.
 Example: A 1/1 with a -1/-1 counter and Inverted is a live 2/2, never a dead 0/0.
 Example: Child of Aether, a 2/0 with Balanced, is a 2/2 and survives.
title: CR 802.1k

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.1: Attributes are qualities that a card or a token can have (see rule 204). An attribute applies whenever the card or token has it, in combat or not. Some attributes change how a unit engages in combat; others change the…)
802.1m When Tough and Balanced both apply to a unit, Tough applies first and Balanced after it, whatever gave the unit each of them: printed on it, its augments in either order of attachment, an effect, or its column. So Tough doubles the unit's defense, then Balanced makes its power and defense equal. Inverted and Unaware apply after both (see rule 206.4). See rules 206.4, 721.
 Example: A 3/1 augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough) and Child of Aether (Balanced) is a 3/3, whichever was augmented first.
 Example: Child of Aether prints Balanced and is a 2/0. Augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough), its defense is doubled (still 2/0), then its stats balanced: it is a 2/2.
 Example: Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) attacks with Child of Aether (Balanced) behind it: its defense is doubled (0/8), then its stats balanced, and it is an 8/8.
 Example: Child of Aether given Tough by an effect is doubled first (still 2/0), then balanced: a 2/2.
 Example: Crumbling Ancient (3/8) augmented with Child of Aether and then with Rampart Guardian is doubled (3/16), then balanced: a 16/16.
802.1n A Pure card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all its other attributes in that interaction (see rule 802.25). This includes the attributes that change stats: in an interaction with a Pure card, Tough, Balanced, Inverted and Unaware do not apply. A column striking a player with a Pure card in it ignores its other attributes too (see rule 802.25b). See rule 802.25.
 Example: Rampart Guardian (a 0/4 with Tough) is dealt 5 damage by a Pure source. In that interaction it ignores Tough, so its defense is 4 and it dies.
 Example: A Balanced 4/1 dealt 3 by a Pure source dies: Balanced does not apply in that pairing.
 Example: An Unaware source dealing 3 damage to a Pure unit pumped from 2/3 to 4/5 does not read it at its printed 2/3: it survives, where a pumped non-Pure 2/3 dies.
 Example: An unblocked Pure column strikes in the normal sub-step and does not double or draw.
title: CR 802.1m–802.1n

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
802.2 Flying. Flying is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Only flying units can block flying units."
 Example: A Flying 3/1 attacks; a ground unit may not block it, and a unit with Flying may.
802.2a An attacking column that has Flying can't be blocked by a unit that does not have Flying. A blocking column has Flying if any unit in it has Flying, so a unit without Flying may block a Flying column together with a Flying unit in the same blocking column. See rule 606.2c.
 Example: A ground 2/2 cannot block a column holding Ephemeral Skywalker (Flying).
 Example: Good Whale cannot block a column holding Ephemeral Skywalker alone, but it can block that column together with another Ephemeral Skywalker in its blocking column.
802.2b Because Flying is shared, a unit attacking in the same column as a Flying unit has Flying too, and the whole column can't be blocked by units that do not have Flying (see rule 802.1). See rule 802.1.
802.2c If the Flying unit leaves an attacking column before blockers are declared, the other units in that column lose Flying, and the column can then be blocked by units without Flying. See rules 802.1, 606.
 Example: Ephemeral Skywalker (Flying) attacks with a 1/1 token in one column; the Skywalker is destroyed before blocks, the token loses Flying, and Rune Channeler, which does not fly, blocks it.
802.2d Flying does not restrict a block when the attacking column or the blocking unit includes a Pure card. A Pure unit can block a Flying column. See rule 802.25.
 Example: Just a Unit (Pure, no Flying) blocks a column holding Ephemeral Skywalker (Flying) and kills it.
title: CR 802.2–802.2d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.2: Flying is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Only flying units can block flying units.")
802.2e A unit without Flying is not able to block a Flying column, so an Alluring trigger cannot compel it to block that column (see rules 606.2e and 802.15). See rules 606.2e, 802.15.
 Example: A lured unit with no Flying, facing a Flying Alluring column, may leave that column unblocked.
title: CR 802.2e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
802.3 Deadly. Deadly is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Any damage from a deadly source will kill a unit."
 Example: Tidepool Terror (1/2 Deadly) is blocked by a 5/9; its 1 damage kills the blocker.
802.3a A unit dealt any nonzero amount of damage by a Deadly source is destroyed, whatever its defense. A Deadly source that deals 0 damage destroys nothing.
 Example: A Deadly source dealing 2 noncombat damage destroys a 5/6.
title: CR 802.3–802.3a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.3: Deadly is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Any damage from a deadly source will kill a unit.")
802.3b Deadly does not reduce the damage its source deals. A Deadly source deals all of its damage; Deadly changes only how much of it is lethal. See rule 608.6d.
 Example: A 10-power Deadly column blocked by a 1/1 deals all 10 to it.
title: CR 802.3b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.3: Deadly is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Any damage from a deadly source will kill a unit.")
802.3c In combat damage assignment, lethal damage for each unit a Deadly half-column deals damage to is 1 (see rule 608.6e). Once the front unit has been assigned at least 1, the dealing player may assign damage to the unit behind it. See rules 608.6e, 608.6b.
 Example: A Deadly and Piercing column over two blockers assigns 1 to each, and the rest may go to the player.
802.3d A unit dealt combat damage by a Deadly source is destroyed in the same damage sub-step, before the next sub-step begins (see rule 608.7b). See rule 608.7b.
 Example: Paired with a Swift unit in its column, a Deadly unit kills what it hits before that unit can strike back.
title: CR 802.3c–802.3d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.3: Deadly is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Any damage from a deadly source will kill a unit.")
802.3e Deadly applies to all damage its source deals, not only combat damage, including damage dealt through spells and abilities. See rule 112.7.
802.3f A spell or a spell token can have Deadly. Damage it deals is then Deadly damage. See rules 302, 304.
 Example: With Rotspore Herald in the region, a Fireball 1 kills any unit it hits.
802.3g A source with both Deadly and Poisonous that deals damage to a unit both destroys it and puts the -1/-1 counters on it (see rule 112.10). See rules 112.10, 802.18.
802.3h If all the damage a Deadly source would deal to a unit is prevented, no damage is dealt, and Deadly does not destroy the unit (see rule 112.11). See rules 112.11, 608.7a.
 Example: A shielded blocker dealt combat damage by a Deadly column is not destroyed.
802.3i Deadly has no effect on damage dealt to a player. See rule 112.5.
 Example: An unblocked Carapace Devourer (3/3, Deadly) costs the defending player exactly 3 life.
title: CR 802.3e–802.3i

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.3: Deadly is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Any damage from a deadly source will kill a unit.")
802.3j Deadly does not apply in an interaction with a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rules 802.25, 608.6e.
 Example: Just a Unit (Pure) blocking a Deadly unit is not killed by 1 damage.
title: CR 802.3j

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
802.4 Swift. Swift is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Swift units deal combat damage first."
 Example: Dune Drifter (2/1 Swift) is blocked by a 2/2; the blocker dies before it strikes, and the Drifter survives undamaged.
802.4a A half-column that has Swift deals its combat damage in the Swift sub-step, before the normal and Sluggish sub-steps (see rule 608.2a). See rules 608.2, 608.2a.
802.4b A unit destroyed by Swift damage in the Swift sub-step deals no combat damage in the later sub-steps. See rule 608.7b.
 Example: A Swift attacker kills a 2/2 blocker, which never strikes back.
802.4c A half-column with both Swift and Sluggish deals combat damage twice: once in the Swift sub-step and once in the Sluggish sub-step, with normal damage from other units in between (see rule 608.2c). See rules 608.2c, 802.5.
802.4d A half-column that has dealt combat damage in the Swift sub-step does not deal combat damage in the normal sub-step, even if it has since lost Swift (see rule 608.2e). See rule 608.2e.
802.4e When a Swift half-column strikes and another half-column will strike in a later sub-step, the combat damage step is split: the abilities that triggered on the Swift damage go on the stack and resolve, with priority, before normal damage is dealt (see rules 608.3b and 608.9c). See rules 608.3b, 608.9c.
 Example: Dune Drifter (Swift) and Lithoghul attack in separate columns and are not blocked. The damage step splits once: Dune Drifter strikes, then there is a window to respond, then Lithoghul strikes. No Sluggish unit is in the battle, so there is no second split.
 Example: Flowstone Arcanite's counters from the Swift step land at the boundary, in time to save an ally.
802.4f In an exchange involving a Pure card, Swift does not apply, so the exchange strikes in the normal sub-step (see rule 608.2d). See rules 608.2d, 802.25.
 Example: Dune Drifter (2/1, Swift) is blocked by Just a Unit (2/3, Pure): both strike in the normal sub-step, and the Drifter dies.
title: CR 802.4–802.4f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
802.5 Sluggish. Sluggish is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Sluggish units deal combat damage last."
 Example: Ambling Mountaintop (4/5 Sluggish) is blocked by a 5/4; the blocker strikes first and kills it, and is never struck.
802.5a A half-column that has Sluggish deals its combat damage in the Sluggish sub-step, after the Swift and normal sub-steps (see rule 608.2a). See rules 608.2, 608.2a.
802.5b Because a Sluggish half-column strikes in a later sub-step of a split step, abilities that triggered on the earlier sub-steps' damage resolve before it deals its damage (see rule 608.9c). See rules 608.9c, 608.3b.
 Example: Adversary of the Deep (Sluggish) grows from the 6 life lost in the normal sub-step before it strikes, and deals 8.
802.5c A half-column that has dealt combat damage in the normal sub-step does not deal combat damage in the Sluggish sub-step, even if it has since gained Sluggish. A half-column that dealt damage in the Swift sub-step and has gained Sluggish deals damage again in the Sluggish sub-step (see rule 608.2e). See rule 608.2e.
802.5d In an exchange involving a Pure card, Sluggish does not apply, so the exchange strikes in the normal sub-step (see rule 608.2d). See rules 608.2d, 802.25.
 Example: Ambling Mountaintop (4/5, Sluggish) is blocked by Just a Unit (2/3, Pure): both strike in the normal sub-step.
title: CR 802.5–802.5d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
802.6 Tough. Tough is an attribute. A Tough unit's defense is doubled.
 Example: Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) is a 0/8, and a unit it is augmented onto has its defense doubled.
802.6a Tough doubles a unit's defense after counters and other +X/+X changes to it have been applied. See rules 206.4, 802.1.
 Example: Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) with a +1/+1 counter is a 1/10.
 Example: Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) with a -1/-1 counter has defense 6: the counter makes it 3, then Tough doubles it.
802.6b Tough does not change a unit's power.
 Example: A 0/4 Tough unit with a -1/-1 counter is a -1/6: its power is not doubled.
802.6c If an effect doubles a Tough unit's defense, the defense the unit then has is double what it had. The doubling is a stat change applied before Tough doubles the result, so if the unit later loses Tough, that change stays and is no longer doubled. See rules 709, 712.
 Example: Burgeon on a 1/10 Tough unit makes it 1/20 (a +0/+5 under Tough); if Monke then takes its Tough, it is a 1/10.
title: CR 802.6–802.6c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
802.7 Balanced. Balanced is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "The power and defense of balanced units are equal to the greater of the two."
 Example: Child of Aether (2/0, Balanced) is a 2/2.
802.7a Balanced compares the unit's power and defense after its counters and other stat changes, and after Tough, have been applied. Inverted and Unaware apply after Balanced. See rules 206.4, 802.1.
 Example: A 1/4 with Tough and Balanced: Tough makes it 1/8, then Balanced makes it 8/8.
 Example: A 1/3 with two +1/+1 counters and Balanced is a 5/5.
 Example: In a column, Child of Aether (2/0, Balanced) and Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) share their attributes: Child of Aether is doubled (still 2/0), then balanced, a 2/2; Rampart Guardian is doubled (0/8), then balanced, an 8/8.
title: CR 802.7–802.7a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
802.8 Inverted. Inverted is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Invert the stat changes of inverted units. For example, -1/+2 would become +1/-2."
802.8a Inverted inverts the net change to a unit's stats from its printed stats. An Inverted unit's power is its printed power minus the net change to its power, and its defense is its printed defense minus the net change to its defense. It is worked out on the total change, not on each change separately. See rule 206.4.
 Example: Malformed Monstrosity (10/9) with its -7/-7, in a column with Reality Bender, is a 17/16.
title: CR 802.8–802.8a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.8: Inverted is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Invert the stat changes of inverted units. For example, -1/+2 would become +1/-2.")
802.8b The changes Inverted inverts include those that Tough and Balanced make. Inverting Tough removes the defense Tough added; it does not halve the defense. See rules 802.6, 802.7.
 Example: A 1/4 with Tough and Balanced is an 8/8; with Inverted too it is a -6/0.
title: CR 802.8b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
(continues 802.8: Inverted is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Invert the stat changes of inverted units. For example, -1/+2 would become +1/-2.")
802.8c Setting a unit's base stats is a stat change that Inverted inverts: Inverted inverts the difference between the unit's printed stats and its current stats. A unit printed 7/5 that Aberrant Statweaver makes base 3/3 is an 11/7 while it is Inverted. See rule 206.5.
 Example: A unit printed 7/5 that Aberrant Statweaver makes base 3/3 is an 11/7 while it is Inverted.
 Example: Its Dark Bubb (printed 4/6, Inverted) beside Aberrant Statweaver is a 5/9, not a 3/3.
802.8d If a unit has both Tough and Inverted, its defense is minus twice the net change to its defense from its printed defense. So it has 0 or less defense, and dies, unless that net change is a reduction, in which case its defense is twice the reduction. See rules 802.6, 713.
 Example: A 1/4 with Tough and Inverted is a 1/0, in either grant order, and dies.
 Example: A 1/3 with one -1/-1 counter, Tough and Inverted survives as a 2/2.
 Example: Inverted on the front unit of a column and Tough on the back unit: both units have both attributes, and both die.
title: CR 802.8c–802.8d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · 8. Keywords › 802. Attributes
802.9 Unaware. Unaware is an attribute. An Unaware card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all stat changes: each is read at the stats printed on it.
 Example: Bubb with two +1/+1 counters is still a 5/6. A 3/3 with four +1/+1 counters attacks into Bubb: it deals 3 and dies to 5.
