D6.11c The card browser explains every keyword a card names, on its type line or in its text box, and never explains less about a card than the in-game inspector does.
 Example: Brough grants {Balanced} from its text box. The browser explains {Balanced} on Brough.
title: CR D6.11–D6.11c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D6. Reveal Timing of Simultaneous Steps
D6.12 Each item on the stack strip is shown in exactly one state: waiting, resolving, answered (negated), fizzled, or resolved. An item that fizzles is shown as fizzled, never as resolved. See rule 704.
 Example: A spell resolves with no legal target. The strip labels it fizzled.
D6.12a A card on the stack carrying mods is drawn the same way as a unit carrying mods: its mods show beneath it.
 Example: A {Modular} spell with a mod is drawn on the stack with the mod peeking out beneath it, as it would be on a unit.
title: CR D6.12–D6.12a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D6. Reveal Timing of Simultaneous Steps
D6.13 While the other player is building an attack or a block, the live view of it is drawn in the same orientation as the declared one. It differs only in being marked as not yet committed. See rules 604, 606.
 Example: When the opponent confirms their attack, no unit changes side or column on the watching player's screen.
title: CR D6.13

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D6. Reveal Timing of Simultaneous Steps
D6.14 A card in hand is marked by what can be done with it now. A card that can be cast is drawn plainly; a card that can only be used another way, such as grafted, augmented or recycled, is drawn differently and says how.
 Example: During deployment a {Battle} spell can only be grafted. It is not drawn like a castable deployment card.
D6.14a A cached card that can be played right now is also shown at the right of the hand. It stays in the cache as well; clicking either copy plays the same card.
 Example: A card glimpsed this turn is drawn beside the hand and in the cache row.
D6.14b The menu for recycling a card for a resource lists first the elements of the player's own deck in constructed, or the draft's elements in a live draft, then Prismite. Every other element, and the Shard, are behind an expander. The menu changes nothing about what is legal: a resource of any of the seven elements may still be made. See rules 105.9a, 106.6a.
 Example: A mono-Fire constructed deck still has all seven elements legal for recycling; the menu just lists Fire first.
 Example: In a fire-water-earth draft the recycle menu offers fire, water, earth and Prismite, and behind "more elements" wood, metal, light, dark and the Shard.
title: CR D6.14–D6.14b

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D6. Reveal Timing of Simultaneous Steps
D6.15 Right-clicking a card the player can read shows only things about that card. The erased piles, concede and the game log are on the menu of the bare table. Right-clicking a card back opens the bare-table menu. See rule 104.4.
 Example: Right-clicking a unit offers its details and the judge, not concede.
 Example: Right-clicking a card in the opponent's hand opens the table menu.
D6.15a The game log opens from the bare-table menu and shows the whole log.
 Example: A log longer than 80 lines is shown in full.
title: CR D6.15–D6.15a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D6. Reveal Timing of Simultaneous Steps
D6.16 The board shows each player's cache and bin as a small panel. Clicking a panel opens the full cache or bin. A card in the panel that the player can use right now is the exception: one click on it uses the card, as clicking it in the full cache or bin would. Clicking any other card in the panel opens the full cache or bin.
 Example: A cached card that can be played now is played by one click on it in the region's cache panel.
 Example: A cached {Battle} card during deployment cannot be played now, so clicking it opens the full cache.
 Example: A mod in the bin that can be applied now is one click from the bin panel: the click starts applying it.
 Example: A bin card that cannot be used now opens the full bin when clicked.
D6.16a While an open decision stops a player from acting (see rule D2.1), no card in that player's cache panel is used by one click: clicking one opens the full cache. A cached card that is one of the decision's choices is not picked from the panel. A player whom another player's decision does not stop, inside a hidden simultaneous segment (see rule D2.1b), still uses their cached cards from the panel on one click.
 Example: In deployment, a Wraith's start-of-deployment choice is open for one player. That player's castable cached card is not one click from the panel; the other player's castable cached card still is, and playing it leaves the decision open.
title: CR D6.16–D6.16a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D6. Reveal Timing of Simultaneous Steps
D6.17 A scroll hides a card's long-hover tooltip only if the scroll could have moved that card: a scroll of the whole page, or of a panel the card is inside. A scroll of anything else, such as the side rail, leaves the tooltip shown. When no card is hovered, any scroll hides the tooltip.
 Example: The side rail scrolls while the pointer rests on a unit on the board. The unit's tooltip stays.
 Example: The page scrolls while the pointer rests on a unit. The tooltip is hidden.
 Example: A panel holding a different card scrolls. The hovered card's tooltip stays.
title: CR D6.17

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D6. Reveal Timing of Simultaneous Steps
D6.18 An arrow from an effect to its target is aimed at the exact centre of the target. Where the target shows text near its centre (a player's life total, the name on a card drawn without its picture, the label of a stack item with no picture), the arrowhead stops just short of that text, so the text can still be read. On a card whose picture has loaded, the arrowhead is not moved. If the text cannot be cleared without the head stopping more than a head's length outside the target, the head stops where it otherwise would.
 Example: An effect targets a player. The arrow points at their life total, and its head stops short of the number.
 Example: An arrow to a unit whose picture has loaded ends in the usual place.
 Example: A target whose label is too big to clear keeps the usual stopping point.
title: CR D6.18

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D7. Confirmations and Misclicks
D7.1 A warning or a confirmation never makes a legal play illegal. The option stays offered, and going ahead does exactly what the play would have done without the warning.
 Example: Fight aimed at two of the player's own units is still offered and, if confirmed, resolves exactly as it would have.
D7.1a When choosing X = 0 makes an effect certain to do nothing, the option to stop at X = 0 carries a warning saying so. It stays legal (see 107.2b). See rule 107.2b.
 Example: Necromantic Rebuke's option to stop at X = 0 is offered with a warning that it negates nothing.
D7.1b When a spell has one target that must be an ally and another that may be any unit, and the player picks one of their own units for the second, the client asks whether they meant to. Yes sends the pick. No sends nothing and leaves the same pick open.
 Example: Fight's first target is the player's ally; the player then picks another of their own units. The client asks whether they meant to target an ally.
D7.1c A pass that would end the battle phase, and with it erase the player's unused spell tokens at regroup, first asks the player to confirm. It asks on that pass and on no other window of the battle.
 Example: A player holding unused spell tokens passes in the last window of the battle. They are asked to confirm before Regroup erases the tokens.
title: CR D7.1–D7.1c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D7. Confirmations and Misclicks
D7.2 A dial, a stepper or an "All" button only sets an amount. It never sends an answer; only the confirm button does.
 Example: Pressing "All" on a counter-removal cost sets the count to the most it can be, and waits for the player to confirm.
D7.2a A question whose answer is a number, such as predicting a life total, offers a typed box as well as a dial, so any number in range can be entered. The value itself is sent, not a choice from a list.
 Example: Prediction Prophet's prediction can be dialled or typed in as any number in range, and that number itself is sent.
D7.2b A variable cost paid one point at a time, such as paying X life, offers the same typed box and dial. Nothing is paid until the player confirms. The dial cannot go below the points already chosen, and for a life cost its top counts them: the largest X it offers is one less than the player's life.
 Example: Paying X life for Flesh Tithe, the player dials to 5 and back to 3; confirming pays 3.
 Example: With 1 life already chosen, the dial does not go below 1.
 Example: With 3 of 30 life chosen, the pay-X-life dial still tops out at X = 29.
D7.2c The button that ends a variable cost ("That's enough") is drawn as a full button that commits, distinct from the buttons that decline.
 Example: "That's enough — X = 3" is a filled button; "decline" stays a quiet one.
D7.2d A cost that removes counters from allies asks the player to click a unit. One click may take several counters from that unit, up to the most that one unit can give. See rule 111.
 Example: Four counters are spread over two allies, two each. One pick can take at most two.
D7.2e When the dealing player splits combat damage, they are asked one victim at a time, with what is left to assign shown. The client never refuses or forces a split the game would accept. See rule 608.
 Example: A strike of 4 into a column of two: the player chooses how much the front unit takes, and the back unit gets the rest.
title: CR D7.2–D7.2e

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D7. Confirmations and Misclicks
(continues D7.2: A dial, a stepper or an "All" button only sets an amount. It never sends an answer; only the confirm button does.)
D7.2f In an "up to" target choice, the button that stops picking reads "No targets" and is drawn as an ordinary button while nothing has been picked; after a pick it reads "No more targets" and is drawn as the quieter decline button. An "up to N" choice ends by itself at its Nth pick, with nothing more asked about it.
 Example: Minor Kraken, grafted with Fester, attacks: its up-to-one target choice offers "No targets" as an ordinary button, and answering it moves on to Fester.
 Example: Twin Flame (up to two targets): after one pick the stop reads "No more targets"; the second pick ends the choice.
title: CR D7.2f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D7. Confirmations and Misclicks
D7.3 When an effect does nothing, the game says so and says why. A printed clause that promises a per-seat outcome and then resolves over an empty collection of seats or of picks is announced for that clause, even when another clause of the same card is speaking. Saying so never changes what the effect does.
 Example: Bloated Manablub's "Each opponent loses 3 life" resolves in a region with no opponent. The game says so, and no life is lost.
 Example: Cull resolves where no player has a unit. The game says so and nothing dies.
D7.3a A spell that resolves with no legal target fizzles, and the log says "<card>: it has no legal target — nothing happens." (see 704). See rule 704.
 Example: Luminous Arc reaches resolution with no target. It fizzles and the log says so.
D7.3b An "each opponent" effect in a region where no opponent is present says that no opponent is present, and does nothing (see 102.2a). See rule 102.2a.
 Example: Bloated Manablub's "Each opponent loses 3 life" during its controller's own deployment says so and takes no life.
D7.3c A clause that promises something for each player, or each of something, and finds none says so for that clause, even when another clause of the same card has done something.
 Example: Recall takes its life when nobody here has a unit to recall, and says the recall did not happen.
D7.3d An effect that would deal damage to each of a group, and finds nobody in the group, says there was nothing to damage.
 Example: A "deal 2 damage to each enemy unit" effect with no enemy unit on the board announces that there was nothing to damage.
title: CR D7.3–D7.3d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D7. Confirmations and Misclicks
D7.4 An announcement the player is expected to act on, or has lost something by, must be shown somewhere other than the game log. The log is the record, not the notice. See rule D6.15a.
 Example: Spell tokens erased after a declined attack are not announced only in the log: the player who lost them is shown a notice where the prompts appear.
 [Verification of D7.4 was only partial.]
D7.4a When a player's unused spell tokens are erased at regroup without a pass to confirm on, such as after a declined attack, that player is shown a notice in the prompt area. It stays until dismissed or until the next battle. The other player is not shown it.
 Example: The round-2 attacker declines; the defender's unused spell tokens are erased, and the defender sees a notice saying so.
D7.4b Any other announcement that a card or a cost the player spent did nothing is shown briefly near the board, under the label "⚠ this did nothing", with the game's own sentence beside it. Both players see it, and it is also in the log.
 Example: A spell resolves with nothing to aim at. A toast says so on the screen.
D7.4c Identical announcements from one resolution are shown once with a count. At most four are drawn at a time; the rest are counted and pointed to the log. None is dropped silently.
 Example: Three identical "this did nothing" sentences in one batch show as one row marked ×3.
title: CR D7.4–D7.4c

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D7. Confirmations and Misclicks
D7.5 When the server refuses something, the player is told, whatever screen they are on: the connecting screen, a waiting room before the game starts, or the board. Joining with a code for which no game exists says that no game has that code. Joining with the code of a finished game the server no longer holds open says instead that the game is over and who won.
 Example: A player types a room code that no game has. The connecting screen shows the refusal instead of waiting forever.
 Example: An error arriving in the constructed waiting room, where there is no board yet, is shown there.
 Example: The refusal for an unknown code names the code.
 Example: A finished game's link, followed after the server has let the game go, says the game is over and who won, not that no game has that code.
title: CR D7.5

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D8. Tutorial and Single-Card Modes
D8.1 Learn to Play is one learner against the Tutorial Bot in one continuous game, with lessons shown at the moment each rule first matters.
D8.1a Learn to Play is a constructed game with its own deal. Each player's opening hand and draw per turn are set separately, turn 1 included, and there is no bottom step. Decks may be stacked so that a lesson's card arrives on its turn. The learner starts with no cards in hand: the draw of 2 on turn 1 is the whole starting hand. See rule 901.
D8.1b The Tutorial Bot's only card is Training Construct: "Create an X/X unit." It is an X-cost deploy spell with X at least 1, no element and no affinity cost. Training Construct exists only in Learn to Play; it is never in any other deck, pack or deal.
D8.1c The Tutorial Bot gains one Shard each turn, starting on turn 1. It casts Training Construct at the largest X it can pay, attacks with every unit it has, and never blocks. Its hand is hidden from the learner.
D8.1d In a lesson deal, the deal Learn to Play and the Weekly Challenges use, running out of cards ends nothing: a player who has to draw from an empty deck and an empty recycle pile draws the cards there are and plays on. Rule 104.5 does not apply. See rule 104.5.
 Example: A Weekly Challenge deck runs out: the player draws fewer and the run goes on.
title: CR D8.1–D8.1d

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D8. Tutorial and Single-Card Modes
D8.2 In a Single Card Duel, each player picks one card before the game, and their deck is 30 copies of that card. This is the one exception to the two-copy limit. Everything else in the game is the same, except the draw (rule D8.2a). See rule 901.
D8.2a A duel has no draw phase. Each turn's card step is a flat draw of 2, and the draw-4, bottom-2 step never happens. The opening hand is still 4, so turn 1 starts with six cards. See rule 503.
D8.2b Cards are picked blind. Before the game, each player is told only whether the other has picked, not what.
 Example: Ann picks her card first. Bob is told that Ann has picked, and not which card.
D8.2c If neither picked card can make a unit, no game is dealt. It is a draw: both players are told both cards and why, nothing is recorded, and both pick again.
 Example: Both players pick a spell that creates nothing. No game is dealt, each is shown both picks, and both pick again.
D8.2d A card can make a unit if it is a unit or spell unit, or if it is declared to create a unit token. What its printed text says is not read for this.
D8.2e A duel counts toward no player's record, rating or achievements. It counts toward the card duel ladder instead, which rates cards rather than players.
D8.2f The card duel ladder counts any finished duel, except a mirror (the same card on both sides) and a walkover. An early concession counts at reduced weight. A card is ranked once it has five duels that are not mirrors. See rule D8.5.
 Example: A mirror duel and a turn-1 walkover put no game on the ladder. A turn-2 concession moves the card rating by 10, half the 20 of a full game.
title: CR D8.2–D8.2f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D8. Tutorial and Single-Card Modes
D8.3 A live draft may be created with custom rules. Custom rules change the deal, never how a card works. See rule 902.
D8.3a The custom rules are: pack size (3 to 15; standard 10); the number of elements (2 to 7; standard 3, and two elements default to Fire and Wood); opening hand (1 to 15; standard 6); draws per turn after turn 1 (0 to 5; standard 2); starting life (1 to 99; standard 30); simple cards only; banned cards; and a card filter.
D8.3b Simple cards only keeps only cards with the silver complexity symbol in the pool. See rule 209.
D8.3c The pool must hold at least 2 × opening hand + 4 × pack size + 6 × draws per turn cards: 64 for the standard game. Custom rules whose pool is smaller are refused before the game is created.
 Example: The standard game needs a pool of 64 cards; the Beginner preset needs 44.
D8.3d Custom rules left at the standard values are not a custom game: they deal the same game as no custom rules at all.
D8.3e A custom game is kept in the match history, marked as custom, and counts toward no profile total, achievement, deck record, rating or average game length. Matchmaking never makes a custom game.
D8.3f The Beginner preset is two elements, simple cards only and packs of 5. It is this client's softening of the rulebook's Quick Start, not the Quick Start itself: 5-card packs are not in the printed rules.
title: CR D8.3–D8.3f

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D8. Tutorial and Single-Card Modes
D8.4 A scenario room, used to test a single card, is an ordinary game dealt from a declared starting board. It is a test fixture, not a game: it counts toward no player's record.
D8.4a Scenario rooms can be created only on a server configured for the tester. Elsewhere they do not exist.
title: CR D8.4–D8.4a

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Annex D — Digital Play Conventions › D8. Tutorial and Single-Card Modes
D8.5 A conceded game is still a loss for the player who conceded (see 104.4). How much it counts toward records and ratings depends on the turn it was conceded on. See rule 104.4.
 Example: A player concedes on turn 1. The result says it is a walkover, names the conceder and the turn, and says it was not counted.
D8.5a A game conceded on turn 1 or earlier is a walkover. It counts toward nothing for either player: no game, win, loss, streak, statistic or achievement. In a rated game, the player who conceded loses 5 rating points and the winner gains nothing, and the game does not count toward the number of rated games played. It stays in each player's match history, marked "not counted".
D8.5b A game conceded on turn 2 is an early concession. It counts as a game for the record, and in a rated game it moves ratings by half as much as a full game. It does not count toward the fast-game achievements or the match-length statistics.
 Example: A player concedes on turn 2. The post-game screen says half weight, and that it still counts.
D8.5c A game conceded on turn 3 or later counts exactly as if the conceding player had been defeated.
 Example: A player concedes on turn 5: the result is an ordinary loss, with no note attached.
D8.5d Only a rated game moves a rating at all. An unrated walkover moves nobody's rating.
 Example: A player concedes an unrated game on turn 1. Neither player has a rating change.
title: CR D8.5–D8.5d

Ability: Text on a card that describes the card's effects. See rule 109.1.

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary

title: CR glossary: Activated ability

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Active zone: Play or the stack; every other zone is inactive. See rule 400.2.
title: CR glossary: Active zone

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Adjacent: Next to a unit on its left, right, front or back in the same formation. See rule 603.2.
title: CR glossary: Adjacent

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Affinity: A card's elemental requirement, shown as element pips, and a player's count of non-dormant resources of an element. See rules 105.3, 105.4.
title: CR glossary: Affinity

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Afflicting: An attribute whose reminder text reads "When an afflicting source kills one or more units, those units' controllers gain a rot." See rule 802.23.
title: CR glossary: Afflicting

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
After combat step: The last step of a battle round, a priority window that follows the combat damage step. See rules 609.1, 609.2.
title: CR glossary: After combat step

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Alluring: An attribute whose reminder text reads "When an alluring column attacks, target enemy can't attack and must block it this combat if able." See rule 802.15.
title: CR glossary: Alluring

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Ally: A unit under your control in the region where the effect is happening. See rule 102.7.
title: CR glossary: Ally

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Ambush: A keyword that lets a unit card be played during battle with the effect "Recall target ally, put me into their position in play." See rule 803.6.
title: CR glossary: Ambush

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Apply: To put a mod onto a card, a special action that is not playing a card. See rules 720.2, 701.2.
title: CR glossary: Apply

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Archenemy: A player setup, typically 2v1, in which the single player takes 1 or 2 turns before the other two begin. See rule 904.12.
title: CR glossary: Archenemy

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Attack step: The first step of a battle, in which the attacking player declares its attacking formation. See rules 505.2, 604.2.
title: CR glossary: Attack step

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Attack window: The priority window that follows the declaration of an attack, in the region attacked. See rule 605.1.
title: CR glossary: Attack window

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Attacking: Bringing units, and the spell tokens that travel with them, into a neighbouring enemy region for battle. See rule 604.1.
title: CR glossary: Attacking

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Attribute: A quality that a card or a token can have, which applies whenever it has it, in combat or not. See rules 802.1, 204.4.
title: CR glossary: Attribute

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Augment: A modification that adds the text after a card's augment symbol to the card it is applied to. See rules 721.1, 208.1.
title: CR glossary: Augment

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Auto-pass: A client preference that passes priority for a player only in a window where passing is the only thing they could do. See rule D2.3.
title: CR glossary: Auto-pass

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Balanced: An attribute whose reminder text reads "The power and defense of balanced units are equal to the greater of the two." See rule 802.7.
title: CR glossary: Balanced

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Banner: The part of a card that offers another way to play it, for a cost of its own, as Ambush and Prophecy do. See rule 203.1.
title: CR glossary: Banner

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Battle: A timing keyword: a card with Battle can be played only while its player is in battle with another player. See rules 803.3, 207.4.
title: CR glossary: Battle

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Battle phase: The second phase of the turn, and its only interactive one. See rules 505.1, 500.4.
title: CR glossary: Battle phase

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Battle round: One of the two attacks of a 1v1 or team battle phase: the initiative team's attack, then the counterattack. See rule 505.3.
title: CR glossary: Battle round

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Bin: A player's discard pile. See rule 405.1.
title: CR glossary: Bin

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Blessed: An attribute whose reminder text reads "Damage dealt by a blessed source causes its controller to gain that much life." See rule 802.22.
title: CR glossary: Blessed

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Block step: The second step of a battle, in which the defending player may place its units in front of the attacking formation. See rules 505.2, 606.1.
title: CR glossary: Block step

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Block window: The priority window that follows the declaration of blocks. See rule 607.1.
title: CR glossary: Block window

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Blocking: How a player who has been attacked defends, by placing units in front of the attacking formation. See rule 606.1.
title: CR glossary: Blocking

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Bluff haste: A client preference with which the client never finishes the haste step for the player. See rule D2.5b.
title: CR glossary: Bluff haste

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Burst: A non-combat attribute printed on spell tokens: casting one casts every spell token of the same name its controller has in that region at the same time. See rule 803.5.
title: CR glossary: Burst

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Cache: A public zone of each player's, beside the hand, the bin and the deck; to cache a card is to put it there. See rules 403.1, 801.8.
title: CR glossary: Cache

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Card: A physical Algomancy card, one with an Algomancy card back; a token is not a card. See rules 108.1, 304.2.
title: CR glossary: Card

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Cast: To play a spell; casting a spell is playing it. See rule 700.2.
title: CR glossary: Cast

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Clock: A chess clock a game may be played with, in which each player has a bank of time. See rule D3.1.
title: CR glossary: Clock

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Column: One file of the battle line: the attacking units in it and the defending units placed in front of it. See rule 603.1.
title: CR glossary: Column

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Combat attribute: An attribute printed in gold; units in the same column of a formation share their combat attributes. See rules 802.1b, 712.8.
title: CR glossary: Combat attribute

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Combat damage: The damage columns deal to each other and to players in the combat damage step. See rule 112.7.
title: CR glossary: Combat damage

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Combat damage step: The step of a battle in which the units in formation deal combat damage. See rule 608.1.
title: CR glossary: Combat damage step

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Complexity: What is used to choose which cards are in a game, shown by the colour of the set symbol. See rules 209.2, 209.1.
title: CR glossary: Complexity

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Concede: To end the game as a loss, in the same way as being eliminated. See rule 104.4.
title: CR glossary: Concede

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Conjure (Obsolete): Not defined by these rules: the old rules glossary's mechanic that created a spell token to be cast at a set time, which no current card prints. See rule 304.11.
title: CR glossary: Conjure

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary

title: CR glossary: Constructed

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary

text:

Controller: The player who controls a card, who may differ from its owner. See rule 102.5.
title: CR glossary: Controller

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Copy: A copy of a spell is a new effect on the stack, not played; a unit that becomes a copy of a card takes that card's name, printed stats, attributes and text. See rules 108.4, 710.1.

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Cost: Something a player must pay to do something: to play a card, to apply a mod, or to activate an ability. See rule 111.1.
title: CR glossary: Cost

text:

text:

text:

Creature (Obsolete): The old rules glossary's word for what these rules call a unit. See rule 301.1.

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
End of turn: A special step after deployment finishes, in which abilities that trigger "at the end of turn" trigger. See rule 508.1.
title: CR glossary: End of turn

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Enemy: A unit not under your control in the region where the effect is happening. See rule 102.8.
title: CR glossary: Enemy

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Erase: To take a card out of the game, to the erased pile. See rule 801.6.
title: CR glossary: Erase

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Erased pile: The zone where a card goes when an effect erases it. See rules 407.2, 801.6.
title: CR glossary: Erased pile

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Evasive: An attribute whose reminder text reads "Evasive units require two blockers." See rule 802.13.
title: CR glossary: Evasive

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Excess damage: For Piercing, the damage a source deals to a unit beyond that unit's lethal damage. See rule 802.16a.
title: CR glossary: Excess damage

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Exchange: A word printed in four senses, each read from its card. See rule 801.13.
title: CR glossary: Exchange

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Expend: To turn a resource sideways for 1 mana, once per turn, to pay a mana cost. See rule 106.5.
title: CR glossary: Expend

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Feeble: An attribute: a Feeble unit can't block. See rule 802.12.
title: CR glossary: Feeble

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Fight: When two units fight, each deals damage equal to its power to the other. See rule 801.11.
title: CR glossary: Fight

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Fizzle: What an effect does if, as it resolves, it has lost all of its targets: it does nothing. See rule 704.6.
title: CR glossary: Fizzle

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Flying: A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Only flying units can block flying units." See rule 802.2.
title: CR glossary: Flying

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Formation: The placement of a player's units when they attack or block: an attacking or a defending formation. See rule 602.1.
title: CR glossary: Formation

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Free-for-all: A player setup (FFA) in which every player plays for themselves. See rule 903.1.
title: CR glossary: Free-for-all

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Full control: A client mode, held with the Control key, in which the client gives a player every stop. See rule D2.7.
title: CR glossary: Full control

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Glimpse: Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest. See rule 801.9.
title: CR glossary: Glimpse

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Graft: A modification, marked by the graft symbol, that combines several effects under a single cause. See rule 722.1.
title: CR glossary: Graft

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Half-column: The attacking units of one column, or its blocking units, which deal their combat damage together as one source. See rule 608.1c.
title: CR glossary: Half-column

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Hand: The zone of a player's own cards, which each player has and which is hidden from the other players. See rules 402.1, 402.2.
title: CR glossary: Hand

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Haste: A timing keyword: a card with Haste can be played during the haste step as well as during deployment. See rules 803.2, 207.3.
title: CR glossary: Haste

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Haste step: The last step of the planning phase, in which players may play only haste cards. See rules 504.1, 504.2.
title: CR glossary: Haste step

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Hidden simultaneous segment: A part of the turn in which both players act at once and neither sees what the other does until both are done. See rule D1.4.
title: CR glossary: Hidden simultaneous segment

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Host: The card a mod is applied to and becomes part of. See rule 720.6.
title: CR glossary: Host

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Hybrid: A card that belongs to two elements. See rule 105.2.
title: CR glossary: Hybrid

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Initiative: What one player has in each turn; in a 1v1 game the initiative player acts first. See rule 500.3.
title: CR glossary: Initiative

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Initiative token: The marker of which player has the initiative, passed clockwise when the turn is over; it is not a token. See rules 508.3, 508.4.
title: CR glossary: Initiative token

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Intent card: A card with which players declare attacks in free-for-all, all at the same time. See rule 905.1.
title: CR glossary: Intent card

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Inverted: An attribute whose reminder text begins "Invert the stat changes of inverted units." See rule 802.8.
title: CR glossary: Inverted

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Keyword action: A verb that card text uses with a fixed game meaning. See rule 801.1.
title: CR glossary: Keyword action

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Last-known state: What a unit was at the instant it left play. See rule 714.1.
title: CR glossary: Last-known state

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Learn to Play: One learner against the Tutorial Bot in one continuous game, with lessons shown as each rule first matters. See rule D8.1.
title: CR glossary: Learn to Play

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Lethal: An attribute whose reminder text reads "Any combat damage from a lethal unit will kill a player." See rule 802.24.
title: CR glossary: Lethal

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Life: What each player has, starting at 30; a player whose life total reaches 0 is eliminated. See rules 112.1, 104.1.
title: CR glossary: Life

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Live draft: A game mode in which the players share one deck and draft cards from it during the game. See rule 902.1.
title: CR glossary: Live draft

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Mana cost: The number of resources a player must expend to play a card, shown in its cost orb. See rules 202.1, 111.1a.
title: CR glossary: Mana cost

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Mod: A modification: a card that is applied to another card instead of being played. See rules 305.1, 720.1.
title: CR glossary: Mod

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Modular: An attribute whose reminder text begins "You can apply mods to a modular card from your hand and/or bin as it is played." See rules 802.26, 724.1.
title: CR glossary: Modular

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Negate: To remove an effect from the stack: a negated effect is removed at once, when the effect that negates it resolves. See rule 704.4.
title: CR glossary: Negate

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Non-combat attribute: An attribute printed in purple, such as Burst and Unstable, that describes a card and generally has nothing to do with combat. See rules 803.1, 802.1b.
title: CR glossary: Non-combat attribute

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Noncombat damage: All damage other than combat damage. See rule 112.7.
title: CR glossary: Noncombat damage

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Nonspell effect: Any effect that is not a spell effect. See rule 700.1b.
title: CR glossary: Nonspell effect

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Once: The [once] keyword: an ability marked [once] can be activated or triggered only once per turn. See rules 803.4, 109.9.
title: CR glossary: Once

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Open decision: A question the game is waiting on a player to answer, which they must answer, or concede, before taking any other action. See rule D2.1.
title: CR glossary: Open decision

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Owner: The player whose card it is; a card's owner never changes. See rule 102.4.
title: CR glossary: Owner

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Pack: In live draft, each player's face-down pile of 10 cards dealt from the deck, which that player drafts from. See rule 409.1.
title: CR glossary: Pack

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Phase: One of the four parts of a turn: the planning, battle, regroup and deployment phases. See rule 500.1.
title: CR glossary: Phase

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Piercing: An attribute whose reminder text reads "Excess damage from piercing sources is dealt to the recipient's controller." See rule 802.16.
title: CR glossary: Piercing

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Pips: The element marks with a card's cost, which are its affinity requirement and not part of its cost. See rule 202.2.
title: CR glossary: Pips

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Planning phase: The first phase of the turn, in which players prepare for the turn ahead. See rule 501.1.
title: CR glossary: Planning phase

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Play: The zone of the units, resources and tokens on the table. See rule 404.1.
title: CR glossary: Play

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Playing a card: What is done to units and spells, from whatever zone: meeting the card's affinity requirement, paying its mana cost and selecting its targets. See rules 701.1, 702.1.
title: CR glossary: Playing a card

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Poisonous: An attribute whose reminder text reads "Poisonous sources damage units in the form of -1/-1 counters." See rule 802.18.
title: CR glossary: Poisonous

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Power: The first of a unit's stats: how much damage it deals in combat. See rules 206.1, 301.3.
title: CR glossary: Power

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Powerful: A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Powerful sources deal double damage." See rule 802.10.
title: CR glossary: Powerful

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Prevention effect: An effect that prevents damage that would be dealt; it is not a replacement effect. See rules 708.11, 112.11.
title: CR glossary: Prevention effect

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Priority: The ability to take game actions such as playing cards or activating abilities. See rule 703.2.
title: CR glossary: Priority

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Priority window: A sequence in which the players (or teams) each receive priority in order. See rule 703.3.
title: CR glossary: Priority window

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Prismite: A resource with no element, which gives no affinity. See rule 106.8.
title: CR glossary: Prismite

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Prophecy: A keyword printed on a card's banner as a cost and a condition. See rule 803.7.
title: CR glossary: Prophecy

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Prophesy: To pay the cost on a card's prophecy banner and put it into the cache with its prophecy attached. See rule 801.14.
title: CR glossary: Prophesy

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Pure: An attribute whose reminder text reads "Pure cards and cards they are interacting with ignore all other attributes." See rule 802.25.
title: CR glossary: Pure

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Ranged (Obsolete): Not defined by these rules: the 2023 Rulebook's attribute that dealt combat damage first and could block fliers, which no current card prints. See rules 802.4, 802.2.
title: CR glossary: Ranged

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Reaping: An attribute whose reminder text begins "When a reaping source kills one or more units, draw a card." See rule 802.21.
title: CR glossary: Reaping

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Recall: To put a card into a hand. See rule 801.7.
title: CR glossary: Recall

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Recap: The playback each player is shown of what the other did in the haste step or in deployment. See rule D5.1.
title: CR glossary: Recap

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Recycle: To put a card on the bottom of the deck, past the deck's mark, into the recycle pile. See rules 801.10, 408.1.
title: CR glossary: Recycle

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Recycle pile: The cards past the deck's mark, where a card put on the bottom of the deck goes. See rule 408.2.
title: CR glossary: Recycle pile

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Refresh: The first step of the planning phase, in which each player's expended resources refresh. See rules 501.2a, 106.5.
title: CR glossary: Refresh

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Region: Where all gameplay takes place; there is one region for each player. See rule 601.1.
title: CR glossary: Region

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Regroup: The global step, once battle has ended in every region, that resets the game between battles. See rule 506.1.
title: CR glossary: Regroup

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Reminder text: Italic text that restates what an attribute or keyword does. See rule 205.2.
title: CR glossary: Reminder text

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Replacement effect: An ability that changes an event as it happens, written "If … instead". See rule 708.1.
title: CR glossary: Replacement effect

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Resonant: An attribute whose reminder text reads "Whenever a resonant source deals damage to a unit, it deals that much damage to that unit's controller." See rule 802.19.
title: CR glossary: Resonant

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Resource: A source of mana, which a player needs to play cards. See rule 106.1.
title: CR glossary: Resource

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Resource step: The step of the planning phase in which players create and activate resources. See rule 502.1.
title: CR glossary: Resource step

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Rockfall: Rockfall N means: each player chooses one of their units, and the source of the rockfall deals N damage to each chosen unit. See rule 801.12.
title: CR glossary: Rockfall

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Rot: A counter a player has, which deals that player damage equal to it at the start of each deployment phase. See rule 112.13.
title: CR glossary: Rot

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Sacrifice: For a player to choose a unit they control and put it into their bin. See rule 801.4.
title: CR glossary: Sacrifice

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Safe point: A moment at which the game makes state checks, such as the end of every action. See rules 713.3, 713.1.
title: CR glossary: Safe point

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Shard: A resource of its own kind, which pays one generic mana once activated. See rule 106.9.
title: CR glossary: Shard

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Side-block: A defending unit placed blocking where no attacker is. See rule 606.4.
title: CR glossary: Side-block

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Single Card Duel: A variant of constructed in which each player picks a single card and their deck is 30 copies of it. See rules 901.8, D8.2.
title: CR glossary: Single Card Duel

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Skirmish (Obsolete): The old rules glossary's name for the place where attackers meet defenders, one per player; the current term is region. See rule 601.1.
title: CR glossary: Skirmish

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Sluggish: A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Sluggish units deal combat damage last." See rule 802.5.
title: CR glossary: Sluggish

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Sneaky: An attribute whose reminder text reads "Sneaky units can't be blocked if attacking alone." See rule 802.14.
title: CR glossary: Sneaky

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Source: The thing that deals damage. See rule 112.6.
title: CR glossary: Source

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Spell: A card type that provides a one-time effect. See rules 302.1, 300.1.
title: CR glossary: Spell

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Spell effect: An effect that is a spell: a spell, a spell unit or a spell token on the stack. See rule 700.1a.
title: CR glossary: Spell effect

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Spell token: A spell that an effect creates directly into play, which its controller may cast from play. See rules 304.11, 108.2.
title: CR glossary: Spell token

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Spell unit: A card that is both a spell and a unit. See rule 303.1.
title: CR glossary: Spell unit

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Stack: The zone where cards being played, and abilities, wait to resolve, the last one put there resolving first. See rules 406.1, 703.1.
title: CR glossary: Stack

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Standing pass: Pass through stack or Pass all: a promise the client keeps on a player's behalf in later windows. See rule D2.2.
title: CR glossary: Standing pass

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
State check: A check the game itself makes at safe points, in which every unit that should be dead dies. See rule 713.1.
title: CR glossary: State check

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Static ability: An ability that states a change its card continuously makes to the game for as long as the card is in play. See rules 707.1, 109.4.
title: CR glossary: Static ability

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Stats: A unit's two numbers, printed power/defense. See rule 206.1.
title: CR glossary: Stats

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Strip: An effect that makes a unit lose all its attributes, all its abilities, or both. See rule 712.1.
title: CR glossary: Strip

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Subtype: A word of the type line other than its markers and its card type, such as Whale. See rule 204.3.
title: CR glossary: Subtype

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Swift: A combat attribute whose reminder text reads "Swift units deal combat damage first." See rule 802.4.
title: CR glossary: Swift

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Target: Something a card or ability chooses, with the word "target", to receive its actions. See rule 110.1.
title: CR glossary: Target

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Team game: A player setup in which two teams play against each other, 2v2 or 3v3. See rule 904.1.
title: CR glossary: Team game

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Thieving: An attribute whose reminder text reads "Whenever a thieving source deals combat damage to an opponent, draw a card." See rule 802.20.
title: CR glossary: Thieving

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Timestamp: When an effect began to apply. See rule 113.2.
title: CR glossary: Timestamp

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Timing icon: An icon in the top right corner of a card that changes when, and how, the card can be played. See rule 207.1.
title: CR glossary: Timing icon

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Token: A unit or a spell that an effect creates directly into play; a token is not a card. See rules 108.2, 304.2.
title: CR glossary: Token

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Tough: An attribute: a Tough unit's defense is doubled. See rule 802.6.
title: CR glossary: Tough

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Transform: To turn a card in play to its other face up; it stays the same unit and does not leave play. See rule 108.3.
title: CR glossary: Transform

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Trash: What happens to a card that enters a bin from any zone except the stack. See rule 801.2.
title: CR glossary: Trash

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Triggered ability: An ability that happens when something else takes place. See rule 706.1.
title: CR glossary: Triggered ability

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Turn: The global cycle of four phases that every player goes through together. See rules 500.1, 100.2.
title: CR glossary: Turn

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Type line: The line of a card that describes what the card is. See rule 204.1.
title: CR glossary: Type line

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Unaware: An attribute: an Unaware card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all stat changes: each is read at the stats printed on it. See rule 802.9.
title: CR glossary: Unaware

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Unit: A card type that, once it enters play, stays there until something removes it; units attack and defend. See rules 301.1, 300.1.
title: CR glossary: Unit

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Unit token: A unit that an effect creates, whether or not the effect calls it a token. See rules 304.4, 304.9.
title: CR glossary: Unit token

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Unstable: A non-combat attribute: an Unstable card that would enter a bin from an active zone is erased instead. See rule 803.8.
title: CR glossary: Unstable

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Virus: A timing icon: a Virus card can also be applied as an augment from the hand during battle. See rule 723.1.
title: CR glossary: Virus

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Vulnerable: An attribute: a Vulnerable unit is dealt double the damage that would be dealt to it. See rule 802.11.
title: CR glossary: Vulnerable

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
X: A number that the card defines. See rule 107.1.
title: CR glossary: X

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
You: On a card, the controller of the effect. See rule 102.6.
title: CR glossary: You

text:
Comprehensive Rules (unofficial) · Glossary
Zone: One of the places a card can be: the deck, the hand, the cache, play, the bin, the stack, the erased pile, the recycle pile and the pack. See rule 400.1.
title: CR glossary: Zone
